articleTitle: Thermomechanical ageing of rotating high-voltage machines: introducing a novel test setup to replicate thermomechanical stress
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Dynamic operation and elevated operating temperatures induce thermomechanical stress in the insulation system of global vacuum-pressure impregnated machines. Consequences include delamination, bulging and abrasion. However, the requirements regarding reliability of the electric insulation system are high. To comply with the high standards, understanding the process of thermally induced mechanical ageing is essential for manufacturers to develop and implement countermeasures. This work investigates the degradation process in the insulation system. A simplified experimental setup using miniature specimens and a compression-based stress replication is introduced to allow cost and time-efficient investigations. Electrical and mechanical measurements reveal that the first stress cycles entail the most severe change in the insulation system. Combining mechanical measurement data and phase-resolved partial discharge patterns proves that mechanical stress induces electrically relevant intrinsic changes in the insulation system.

articleTitle: Acoustic signal propagation in solid insulating materials
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Polymeric insulating materials are considered as a crucial part of most high voltage components. The continuous high electric stress applied across the insulation material may, over a long-time duration, initiate partial discharges which deteriorate the insulation and lead towards dielectric failure. The detection of the acoustic pressure pulses generated as a result of partial discharges can be helpful in detecting and locating the PD at the initial stage. Detection of Acoustic Emissions (AE) is a well-established technique for gas and liquid insulation systems but is not fully explored in the public domain for solid insulation systems. In this work, propagation behaviour of the pressure acoustic wave in nylon 6,6 rods of differing lengths were analysed in the laboratory. The discharge events were created in air but near the surface of one end of the polymeric rod. The acoustic transducer was attached to the opposite end of the polymeric rod to detect the arrival of the propagated acoustic signal. It was determined, based on the first peak of arrival for all data, that the drop-in magnitude of the propagating pulses follows the 1/r<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> relationship where r is the distance away from the discharging site.

articleTitle: Transient analysis of interconnected and unconnected grounding grids in stratified soils
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Grounding systems are fundamental to dissipate the impulse currents or minimize the induced high overvoltages on nearby grids. However, the grounding conductors can be damaged due to electromotive forces, disconnecting parts of the grounding grids. This work investigates the influence of the physical factors (frequency effect, stratification, water content, and porosity level) on soil modeling for studying the grounding systems. Then, two conditions are applied in the grounding grids are used: interconnected and unconnected grids with irregular areas, assuming frequency-constant (FC) and frequency-depending (FD) soil models. The Ground Potential Rise (GPR) generated for a lightning current of positive impulse is calculated. All results are calculated using the full-wave electromagnetic software XGSLab® employing the Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) method. Results indicated that the peak values of voltage waveforms are strongly affected by physical factors, especially when the frequency-dependent soils are considered. In addition, the unconnected condition between the grounding grids has demonstrated an elevation of the potential along the whole grounding system. This work demonstrates the importance of considering the porosity level, water content, and frequency effect on the soil parameters to adequately compute the transient electromagnetic responses.

articleTitle: Transformer oil detection feasibility with a love wave sensor
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In this paper, the use of a Love wave sensor is presented to verify the feasibility of detecting transformer oil. It was demonstrated that the Love wave sensor response exhibits significant variation with oil on its acoustic path, when compared to the bare sensor. We noted a difference of approximately -17.249 ± 0.552 dB in insertion loss magnitude and a frequency shift of approximately 125 kHz, when observing the transmission coefficient (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>). Moreover, the phase of the S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> parameter exhibits a good linearity over the working region of the sensor as well as a phase shift in the sensitive region when the oil is introduced, which can also be considered as a frequency shift. This result is a good indication of the feasibility of using a Love wave sensor as chemical sensor for transformer oil.

articleTitle: A case study on dielectric response measurement of high voltage generator insulation systems
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Dielectric response measurements (DRMs) are a non-destructive method that has long been widely employed to state the insulation condition of many power system components. Such methods can reflect the deterioration problems that occur in the insulation system of rotating machines, such as conductive contamination on the end winding surface, moisture absorption, and stress grading system deterioration. In this paper, the investigation of the DRM of the stator winding insulation of an indirect hydrogen-cooled generator rate of 211.75 MVA, 15.75 kV is presented. The DRMs are carried out using polarization and depolarization current (PDC) as well as frequency domain spectroscopy (FDS) on the stator winding insulation system. The experiments are performed on both phase-to-ground and interphase insulation. Various dielectric characteristics, which are polarization current, depolarization current and a dissipation factor are recorded and analysed. The phase-to-ground PDC results show the natural characteristic of the stress grading system as a hump occurring in the current trace. In addition, the measured PDC results are converted into a frequency window so that calculated parameters can be compared with the measured FDS test results.

articleTitle: Electronic circuitry for a non-contacting partial discharge GMR sensor
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) detection is an important tool for evaluating the insulation condition of high-voltage power equipment. This paper investigates a diagnostic system consisting of a magnetic sensor with dedicated electronic circuitry. The investigated sensor is based on the giant magnetoresistance (GMR) effect, which enables the possibility of contactless detection of magnetic fields caused by PD currents. However, the bandwidth of the circuitry can be a limiting factor. In order to exploit the bandwidth of an extra high-sensitivity adapted giant magneto-resistive (xMR) sensor, this paper describes dedicated designs for compensation and signal conditioning of the xMR signals. Typical performance has been evaluated, including frequency response and time-domain response to fast calibrator pulses by the xMR sensor with the implemented circuit. The results show that the xMR sensor with the implemented circuit covers a relatively broad bandwidth and can detect PD pulses with a minimum amount of 10 pC, preliminarily verifying its possibility to detect PDs. Using this xMR system, magnetic signals from an experimental model producing surface discharges have been detected and compared with simultaneously measured signals from a high-frequency current transformer (HFCT). The results show that the xMR system can measure the magnetic fields produced by the PD currents.

articleTitle: Providing protection of substations against geomagnetic induced currents with fiber optics
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Whether it is charging your phone, powering your house or energizing a city, secure and reliable transmission and distribution of electrical power is crucial in the ever-increasing demand for electricity. The electrical industry has become proficient in providing protection against a majority of the common faults facing the electrical grid such as line-to-line, line-to-ground, overvoltage and others. Today, there is an increasing level of danger to the electrical grid originating from sources outside of the Earth's atmosphere in the form of geomagnetically induced currents (GIC). One of the critical areas of concern in a substation is the control cables from the instrument transformers and sensors feeding into the control house. If GICs are introduced into the control cables, damage to the equipment within the control house can occur, thus, leading to loss of protection and potential outages. To eliminate this problem, fiber optic cables can be used to replace the copper wires to transmit the signals from the equipment in the substation yard to the control house. Fiber optic cables have the advantage of not being susceptible to GICs. With the addition of fiber optic networks to the control scheme of a substation, outages from GIC can be greatly reduced.

articleTitle: Observation of algae development on polymer insulators based on the results of BDV and SEM
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Polymer insulators is expected has high hydrophobicity compared to other insulator material such as glass and polymer. However, polymer insulators are susceptible to algae. The effect of algae on the dielectric strength of polymer insulators has been analysed. Polymer insulators are immersed in algae-contaminated water for 3 months. Prior to immersion, the polymer insulator was pre-conditioned with salt mist conditioning. Then Breakdown Voltage (BDV) is carried out periodically on the polymer insulator. Meanwhile, Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) testing was carried out on new insulators and insulators that had been submerged in algae to observe how deep is algae penetrate inside the polymer and its effect on the BDV. The BDV value of the new polymer insulator is higher than that of the contaminated insulator when it experienced internal breakdown. When the algal contaminants only grew on the surface, the BDV value was higher than that of the clean polymer.

articleTitle: Enhanced dielectric energy storage performance of P(VDF-HFP) with high hexafluoropropylene content
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The development of power system requires high energy density and miniaturization of power capacitors. Polymer-based dielectric capacitors have been widely studied because of their excellent dielectric breakdown strength, mechanical properties and easy processing. Polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) is one of the most widely studied polar dielectric polymers, which contains semi-crystalline areas with a variety of crystal phases, including the non-polar α phase and the polar β, γ and δ phases. The β phase is an important structure, which exhibits high polarization strength under high electric field. However, the residual polarization of β-PVDF is high due to ferroelectric domain inversion, thus the stored energy cannot be released during discharge process, which limits its charging and discharging efficiency. In this study, by incorporating massive bulk monomer, namely hexafluoropropylene, into PVDF molecular chains and increasing its content ratio up to 25 wt%, the large ferroelectric domains can be broken into polar nanodomains and the interchain distance is thus widened. The molecular chains in the amorphous region tend to be ordered, and the crystal region changes from the non-polar phase to the polar phase, which results in higher charge-discharge efficiency and breakdown strength up to 800 kV/mm, leading to the energy density of 26 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of transient surface currents on polluted polymer insulators loaded with superimposed HVDC voltage
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This work discusses and analyses the measured impulse currents flowing over the surface of an artificially polluted polymer insulator loaded with a superimposed HVDC voltage. The pollution layer consists of a continuous, conductive film which is created by a mixture of liquid sodium chloride for the conductive part as well as powdered kaolin to make the film stick to the surface, resembling a highly polluted insulator. The impulse voltage forms are generated by a specific circuit design including a spark gap with which it is possible to generate impulse voltages with very slow fronts as well as standardized impulses, such as switching impulses. In addition to the impulses, the test specimen is loaded with a HVDC voltage generated by a HVDC voltage source for simulating real fault overvoltage scenarios at MMC HVDC Links. The results of the measured transient currents are presented in this paper and investigated with regard to the amplitudes and time parameters of the generated impulse voltage shapes.

articleTitle: Study on development of device detecting abnormal PD phenomenon
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Extra-high voltage underground transmission cables are critical transmission cables that are mostly located in metropolitan area, and occurrence of breakdown in such a cable is highly costly and takes a long time to repair, causing a ripple effect of social and economic damage. To prevent such an accident for critical transmission cable, partial discharge measurement and inspection is regularly performed regularly. To effectively perform preventative diagnosis via partial discharge measurement, first, the location of abnormal signal needs to be identified, a long-term monitoring and precision diagnosis should be performed, and the result of analysis is used to draw conclusion. in this paper, an entry-level extraction device for effective detection of abnormal signal location is configured, an identification algorithm is implemented, and a field test was performed.

articleTitle: Measuring HVDC-impulse composite voltages with high-voltage dividers: laboratory comparison and deviation analysis
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Correct and reliable metrology is one of the key challenges in the transformation in electrical power supply. The increasing use of high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission demands the correct and accurate measuring of new voltage types. These include, in particular, composite voltages. Composite voltages occur in the case of external or internal overvoltages in DC networks. Hence, they are part of dielectric HVDC component tests to ensure reliable operation over several decades. Thereby, the appropriate measuring equipment must correctly measure all voltage components of a composite voltage. However, the current standardisation lacks procedures for the calibration or qualification of measurement equipment to measure composite voltages. Therefore, the following investigation contributes to the standardisation by comparing a developed universal voltage divider for the measurement of composite voltages with a commercially available one in two different laboratories. Measurements were carried out using both dividers and then determining and comparing the measurement deviations between different parameters. It is shown that although both dividers comply with the current standardisation, there were differences in the measurement deviations in different laboratories, especially for the composite voltage stresses.

articleTitle: AC electrical breakdown of insulating polymer and external factors
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Electrical breakdown strength of polymers is an important parameter for their applications as high voltage insulation. The value is typically obtained by testing sample in the laboratory. However, it has been widely recognised that the breakdown strength measurement is affected by many factors, especially external factors such as electrode size, testing medium and the way the voltage is applied. In this paper, a series of AC breakdown measurements have been conducted on LDPE films using a pair of typical spherical electrodes to examine external factors such as testing volume, voltage rise rate and oil medium. More importantly, by measuring partial discharge prior to breakdown and observation of discharge marks on the surface of the sample, it is possible to postulate the breakdown process involved in the breakdown test. It is likely that the breakdown starts from the oil medium with partial discharges in void that attack the sample surface and initiate the breakdown through the sample.

articleTitle: Longitudinal dielectric interfaces with microstructures
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Solid-solid interfaces e.g., in cable accessories are important to achieve a necessary dielectric performance. However, within the sealing, the possibility of voids and cracks is not completely avoidable and needs to be focused. Such imperfect dielectric tightness at the interfaces increases localized electric field leading to partial discharges and subsequent breakdown process. Herein, we report, enhancement in electrical interface strength by using controlled structural features (Wrinkles) on the surface of longitudinal interface materials. Electric field simulations were done on these structures using different positioning of electrodes concerning the wrinkle shape. In addition, the trajectory of electron given by the wrinkle shape towards the high voltage electrode is measured along with ionization coefficient responsible for the avalanche mechanism.

articleTitle: Condition assessment of 150 kV outdoor composite insulators following a vegetation fire event
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In electric power transmission and distribution systems, the use of overhead lines instead of underground cables is preferred by power utilities mainly due to the lower construction cost and the easier maintenance access. On the other hand the equipment used in overhead lines is stressed by several factors, such as weather conditions, lightning, vegetation fires, etc. In particular, vegetation fires under the overhead transmission lines could have catastrophic results for the installed equipment and can cause long-lasting electricity interruptions. In this study, condition assessment results are presented for eighteen 150 kV composite insulators exposed to a forest fire event, occurred in the August 2021, in the island of Rhodes, Greece. The evaluation of the fire effects on composite insulators was performed by employing several macroscopic and microscopic diagnostic techniques including visual inspection, hydrophobicity classification, Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and optical microscopy analysis.

articleTitle: A stable discontinuous-Galerkin method for propagation of particle densities in nitrogen under high superimposed-impulse stresses
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In the process of energy transition, the integration of non-fossil energy sources and the associated measures within the energy transmission grid represent an infrastructural challenge. High-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission plays a crucial role in reducing transmission losses. Under HVDC stress and/or pulses, the insulation medium air loses its dielectric strength, which manifests itself in electrical discharges. These local discharges lead to electrical breakdowns in high-voltage systems and damage components. To prevent this, conductive components with different electrical potentials have to be spatially separated. A prerequisite for a corresponding breakdown is the formation of a conductive plasma (streamer). If this exceeds a certain limit temperature, a breakdown is to be assumed. The formation of the plasma or an ionizing channel is usually modelled by coupling the Poisson equation with a transport equation for the charge particles involved. Of particular importance is the numerical calculation of DC voltages which are superimposed with new slow front pulses occurring in HVDC. Due to the high electric fields over different orders of magnitude, there are special requirements for the solution method. In order to guarantee the important particle preservation in conservative systems, a flux-correcting method such as the discontinuous-Galerkin method is used for the numerical solution.

articleTitle: Space charge measurment in multi-dielectric arrangments using LIPPS
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Due to the expansion of power grids, the need for HVDC (high voltage direct current)-cable links is increasing. When evaluating HVDC suited insulation materials the investigation of the space charge behaviour is inevitable. Cable accessories arrangements consists of two different insulation materials, one for the cable main insulation and another one for the accessory. Space charges behaviour can be studied using the LIPP (laser induced pressure pulse) method, which has the advantage, that derived space charge profiles from single arrangements can be directly interpreted without the need for complex signal processing. Nevertheless, measuring space charges in multi-dielectric arrangements is challenging. Due to the acoustic impedance mismatch of the used insulation material combination acoustic reflections occur and makes it difficult to interpret the actual space charge behaviour. This paper presents a method for reducing space charge signal artefacts caused by reflection phenomena in multi- dielectrics. Exemplarily space charge measurement data derived from multi-dielectric arrangements are used for testing and evaluating the developed correction method. The results of the correction procedure show that the proposed method is suitable to reduce signal components caused by acoustic reflections in a sufficient manner. Possible model uncertainties are analysed and further developments are pointed out.

articleTitle: Shielding failure flashover rate estimation for A 66 kV overhead line through stochastic lightning attachment simulations
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In this work, the shielding failure flashover rate (SFFOR) of a 66 kV single-circuit overhead line (OHL) is estimated based on a stochastic approach. Lightning incidence along the span of the OHL is computed via a stochastic lightning attachment model on the basis of fractal structures, that integrates physical leader inception and propagation criteria. The critical lightning currents resulting in line insulation flashover are computed using an ATP-EMTP simulation model of the 66 kV OHL. Simulation results of the two models are integrated into a formulated methodology for estimating the SFFOR of the 66 kV OHL. A comparison is made with commonly used electrogeometric models; the effect of lightning activity at the OHL location on SFFOR computations is studied. Based on the proposed approach, simplifying assumptions of the IEEE Std 1243 procedures associated with lightning incidence estimation and critical flashover current calculation could be overcome, assisting thus, in more comprehensive lightning performance assessment studies for OHLs.

articleTitle: Dielectric electrophoresis of cellulose nanocrystals/epoxy resin mixtures under alternating current field
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) are often used to modify advanced electrical materials because of their excellent mechanical properties, high length-diameter ratio, and low density. Ac electric field electrophoresis-assisted assembly is a new preparation technology for nanocomposites in recent years. In this paper, the dielectric electrophoresis of CNCs in epoxy resin was studied under the AC field. Firstly, the dielectric electrophoresis model of CNC under an AC electric field was established, and the influence mechanism of electric field parameters on each physical process was obtained by numerical simulation. An optical observation platform was established to observe the dynamic physical process of dielectric electrophoresis of the CNC/epoxy resin hybrid system under the AC electric field. The results show that the experimental phenomenon is consistent with the theoretical model of dielectric electrophoresis, which preliminarily verifies the feasibility of the theory.

articleTitle: Influence of sampling interval and trigger threshold on measured lightning current waveform characteristics
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The authors have carried out measurement of the current waveforms associated with lightning discharges to wind turbines at the Nikaho Kougen wind farm near the coast of the Sea of Japan since 2013 and completed in 2022. During the measuring period some settings of the digital recording system, such as the sampling interval, has changed. From 2021 the authors start the measurement of the lightning current at another wind farm in the vicinity of the Nikaho Kougen wind farm with the digital measuring system with the low trigger threshold. In this paper the authors investigated the lightning current waveforms initiated by upward propagating leaders in winter up to 2022. The influence of the sampling interval on the estimated peak of the measured current waveforms associated with return strokes after the extinction of the ICC (initial continuous current) is studied. Furthermore, the influence of the trigger threshold on the component ratio of the classified ICC types is also studied.

articleTitle: Formation of conventional fault gases and higher hydrocarbons in various insulation liquids under electrical faults
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Arcing leads to enormous stress of the insulation system of a transformer and initiates ageing mechanism. The ageing processes in the insulation liquid and the plasma atmosphere produce several fault gases. The well-established dissolved gas analysis (DGA) allows the detection of transformer fault type. In addition to the conventional fault gases, also higher C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> to C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> hydrocarbons are generated during electrical stress. This new fault gases could allow the development of a more reliable DGA interpretation algorithm due to the reduction of failures during oil sampling and transport as well as a better classification of the faults within a fault type. In this contribution, four different insulation liquids, a natural and a synthetic ester, a gtl-oil and an uninhibited mineral oil, were investigated regarding to their gassing behaviour under electrical stress. Large differences in the amount as well as the type of fault gases were obvious. In addition to the typical conventional fault gases, further C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> hydrocarbons could also be identified as characteristic fault gases. Furthermore, a clear correlation could be observed between impulse energy, number of breakdowns and the concentration of gases. With increasing of energy or number of impulses, more fault gases are generated.

articleTitle: Initial continuous current of the negative upward lightning to the Peissenberg Tower, Germany
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The parameters of the Initial Continuous Current (ICC) of the negative upward lightning measured at the Peissenberg Tower, Germany, from 2008 to 2022 are analysed. In total, 77 negative upward lightning were investigated, 49% of them were ICC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Only</sub>-flashes (without significant ICC-pulse), 30% of them were ICC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RS</sub> - flashes (with subsequent return strokes), 18% of them were ICC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</sub>-flashes (with ICC-pulses > 2kA), and 3% of them were ICC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Bipolar</sub>-flashes (includes a positive current component). The research revealed that the ICC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Only</sub>-flashes were the weakest and the ICC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</sub>-flashes were the strongest ones, the ICC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RS</sub>- and the rare ICC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Bipolar</sub>-flashes were in between. Compared to the values fixed in the standard IEC 62305-1 for LPL I, in four (5.2%) cases the ICC lasted longer and had a higher amount of charge, and in 11 (14.3%) cases the average current exceeded the tolerable current limit. The strongest flash transferred a charge of 386 C.

articleTitle: Experimental characterization of laminated dielectric in LN2 bath for use in Brazilian HTS cable project
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: One of the most important problems in the development of high temperature superconducting cables (HTS cables) with cryogenic dielectric is the electrical insulation system. It is essential to measure losses in dielectric materials at cryogenic temperatures to improve the project of a HTS cable. Obtaining the dielectric strength and losses allows calculating the cable electrical insulation and the additional thermal load for the cooling system. In the present work we propose the evaluation of dielectric strength voltage, the loss-tangent and the permittivity of laminated dielectric material samples, rated to operate at 77 K (liquid nitrogen bath), commercial frequency (60 Hz), and voltages up to 13.8 kV. The insulation material under test is composed of two materials, Nomex® and Kapton®, in a laminated configuration (NKN), the first is an aromatic polyamide synthetic polymer, and the second is a polyimide film. Each dielectric sample consists of a Kapton® sheet laminated on either side by a layer of Nomex®. The choice of this material for investigation was due to the inherent high dielectric strength of its components and the restrictions in accessing the PPLP® (polypropylene laminated paper) in the context of "D712: SUPERCABO Project", a strategic project on new technologies for power transfer demanded by the Brazilian National Electric Energy Agency. The selection of this material constitutes an original proposal for use in a superconducting cable project. The dielectric strength measurement followed the ASTM D149 directions, and the loss-tangent was measured using an LCR meter. The electrical permittivity can be obtained from the capacitance and geometric values. The developed experimental setup uses sample holders made with PTFE (Polytetrafluoroethylene). Measurements at room temperature and in an LN2 bath are compared, measurements for Kapton® and Nomex® samples are also conducted for comparison purposes.

articleTitle: Simulation of PD RF EM wave propagation in different MV bus bar compartment configurations
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Monitoring of partial discharge (PD) in air-insulated medium voltage (MV) switchgear can reveal potential insulation failure. There is still clarification needed to understand the most effective placement of RF probes, especially along extended MV switchgear line-up structures. In this work a simulation study was performed to investigate the differences between the PD propagation characteristics of electromagnetic (EM) waves in one single bus bar and a triple line-up of bus bar compartments. A finite element method (FEM) bus bar compartment model is created and simulations are performed in Comsol Multiphysics. By applying PD sources at specific locations on particular phases, RF signals are recorded along the compartment surfaces. Based on created signal energy interpolation maps, the potential best sensor position placement areas of RF sensors is revealed for each PD case for the different compartment structures. The investigation reveals that for the sake of PD signal propagation studies PD within a single compartment model may produce similar PD sensor positions patterns to PD of a central bus bar chamber within a triple compartment.

articleTitle: Development of a resistive field conform voltage divider from DC up to 500 kHz
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The development of a resistive electric field conform voltage divider [1] enables the measurement of high-frequency voltage components superimposed on the DC voltage in the latest generation of HVDC systems [2]. The development starts from a standard 100 kV voltage divider with a 50 MΩ resistive tissue. The 100 kV design is based on a presented field calculation and a further torus optimization. In the scope of this paper, it will be shown that a broadband frequency response from DC to 500 kHz can be achieved by adapting the resistive distribution of the divider.

articleTitle: Improving surface flashover voltage of epoxy under eco-friendly C5F10O/CO2 gas mixtures by ultraviolet irradiation
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: As an environmentally friendly alternative gas for SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>, C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>O/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas mixtures have shown great potentials for applications in gas-insulated equipment because of its extremely low global warning potential (GWP). However, the research on the surface flashover of epoxy under C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>O/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas mixtures is still lacking. In this paper, we studied the effect of surface treatment on the surface flashover performance of epoxy resin under C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>O/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas mixtures. Epoxy resin/Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> composites were prepared and then irradiated by ultraviolet for 6 h in air. Infrared spectrum, water contact angle, surface potential decay, surface resistivity and DC surface flashover voltages of the pristine and modified samples in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> and C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>O/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas mixtures were determined. The results showed that that the flashover voltage in both SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> and C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>O/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> mixtures was improved obviously after surface treatment. It was found that the ultraviolet irradiation increased the energy level and density of both shallow and deep surface traps, which resulted in strong trapping effect and finally increased the flashover voltage. Our work provides an effective way to improve the surface flashover voltage of epoxy under C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>O/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas mixtures by ultraviolet irradiation.

articleTitle: Effect of surface resistivity of coated PET film on discharge propagation before flashover
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Lightning strike damage to the blades of wind turbines represents a serious problem to the power industry and it is increasing due to the increase in the installed number of wind turbines and in their height. In order to clarify fundamental phenomena of discharge penetration through insulators as the blade, we have conducted discharge penetrating experiments using polyethylene terephthalate film. In this paper, an untreated film or a coated film was placed between rod and plate electrodes, and the effect of surface resistivity on the propagation of lightning impulse discharge was investigated. As a result, penetration probability was 60% in the case of untreated film, whereas that of coated film was 0%. Furthermore, propagation process with untreated film was that discharge progressed from a position of the film in vicinity of rod electrode toward plate electrode and then both leader discharges occurred from the film and the plate electrode. On the other hand, propagation process with coated film was that discharge progressed from the tip of the rod electrode toward the edge of the film and then both leader discharges occurred from the edge of the film and the plate electrode.

articleTitle: Partial discharge behaviour of a fixed protrusion in eco-efficient gas-insulated systems under AC voltage stress
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The insulating gas sulphur hexafluoride (SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>) is used in gas-insulated systems (GIS) as dielectric and arc quenching medium. Unfortunately, the gas is the most potent greenhouse gas. Therefore, grid operators as well as manufacturers are looking for eco-efficient alternatives. One suitable solution, to replace SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>, is a gas mixture with carbon dioxide (CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>), oxygen (O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) and a fluoronitrile additive (C4-FN). However, the use of eco-efficient solutions for electrical power transmission must ensure an identical high availability of the power supply. An appropriate method to verify the condition of GIS is the surveillance of partial discharges (PDs). Until now it is unclear whether the well-known technical and physical relations of the PD behaviour in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> are applicable on new insulating gases. Therefore, aim of this contribution is to analyse the PD behaviour of a fixed protrusion under AC voltage stress in an eco-efficient insulating gas based on a C4-FN gas mixture at 0.7 MPa depending on the voltage stress. For the experiments carried out in this investigation, the weakly inhomogeneous electrical field of a GIS is resembled by a sphere-plate electrode arrangement. A protrusion is connected to the sphere electrode on ground potential. The findings are derived from experimental investigations, especially high-bandwidth discharge current measurements. The comparison of the measured PD current with field bound analysis in the UHF range allows to draw concluding remarks for PD diagnosis.

articleTitle: Investigation on the influence of fast switching pulses and high frequency on solid insulation materials
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Solid Insulation materials are widely used in modern power electronics devices and applications. The characterisation of the material properties is crucial for the proper design of an insulation system suitable for the targeted application. With the increased use of fast switching semiconductor switches, the influence of high frequency and steep pulsed signals on the insulation must be investigated. The dielectric breakdown and ageing mechanisms are important factors and highly depend on different electrical stress conditions. The state of the art as well as the basic mechanisms are briefly discussed in this paper. Further, the relevance of the topic is discussed as well. Additionally, the current methods of testing for high voltage, high frequency and/or pulsed voltages is presented. Finally, a preliminary test of the breakdown voltage two devices under test (DUTs) and their frequency dependency is given.

articleTitle: Study on influence of arc ignation mode on the arc and pressure process in oil
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: On-load tap changer (OLTC) happens frequent switching when running, switching process will produce arc fault in OLTC tank, which leads to arc reigniting. Insulating oil under the effect of arc is decomposed into high-temperature and highpressure gas. The transient process will produce severe shock wave, is likely to cause explosion accidents in OLTC tank. In this paper, the wire electrical explosion was uesd to simulate the arc fault in OLTC, and an experimental platform was built to study the pressure characteristics of wire electrical explosion process in closed cavity, the process of wire electrical explosion and the form of discharge current in the closed cavity were analyzed. Different wire lengths were obtained to explode wires under the same discharge energy. Discharge current and shock wave pressure were recorded and analyzed. Experimental results indicate that with the increase of the length of the arc wire, the shock wave pressure increases, and the maximum discharge current decreases. But when the wire reaches a certain length, the shock wave pressure decreases sharply. Furthermore, the difference of arc process, shock wave pressure in two ways of wire electrical explosion and oil breakdown is studied.

articleTitle: Application of power line communication for online partial discharge monitoring in a simulated substation
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In power system, partial discharge (PD) activity is an important measure of high voltage equipment health. A thorough monitoring system is needed to understand whether the equipment working properly or needs a maintenance. This paper proposes power line communication (PLC) as a medium that allows partial discharge data to be sent. Here, PLC receiver detects partial discharge simultaneously with demodulation of the PLC signal. The detection principle is that the PLC perceives PD as a disruption and decreases the communication rate (PHY rate). Furthermore, a circuit simulating a substation is constructed in attempt to measure the partial discharge by PLC system. It was found that signals detectable by PLC were propagating in PLC and identifying PD from defect-simulated electrodes by PLC was possible. This research compares low-cost online PD monitoring system based on power line communication with conventional PD measurement.

articleTitle: Long-term AC partial discharge characteristics of a 22 kV cast resin transformer in accelerated tests
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper reports long-term trend analysis of partial discharge (PD) characteristics of an aged 22 kV cast resin transformer (CRTr) with accelerated AC voltage application till breakdown. Experimental results under the accelerated test revealed that an increasing trend of PD activities was observed during 6651 h from the start of the test to breakdown. The residual lifetime corresponds to 23 years of operation assuming the acceleration factor 30 of the test calculated from the multiplication of applied voltage acceleration factor 5 and frequency acceleration factor 6. A trend of phase-resolved PD pattern exhibited that the maximum value of PD charge continuously increased and the phase at which PD occurred became wider. The result suggests that degradation of CRTr was progressing due to PD in void defect inside the insulation system of CRTr.

articleTitle: Magnetic core reset technology for high repetitve solid state linear transformer driver
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The Fast Linear Transformer Driver (FLTD) based on solid-state switch has an important application prospect in the field of pulse power technology. Whereas the remanence of magnetic core in FLTD seriously affects the output waveform of the driving source. In this paper, three reset methods including RCD magnetic reset, LC resonance magnetic reset and winding magnetic reset are compared, and experimental tests are carried out. The results show that the magnetic reset time increases correspondingly with the increase of pulse width, and the excitation and leakage energy are consumed by the resistance in RCD magnetic reset circuit. The resonant capacitor of the LC magnetic reset circuit slows down the MOSFET switching speed, increases the pulse leading and trailing edge time, and also aggravates the temperature rise of the switching tube. In the winding magnetic reset circuit, the third winding creates a reuse of energy, and the core reset time increases as the input voltage rises. Therefore, this paper proposes a hybrid magnetic reset method combining RCD magnetic reset circuit and MOSFET's own LC resonance. Experimental test results show that the linear transformer driver prototype can output a stable 1MHz pulse sequence with the hybrid magnetic reset method.

articleTitle: Reference measurement system for traceability of composite and combined waves
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Type and routine testing of new HV cables and switching elements are conducted using composite and combined waves. In this testing the fundamental voltage stress, HVDC or HVAC, is superimposed with a Switching or Lightning Impulses (SI, or LI). Lacking traceability for direct measurements of these wave shapes separate measurements are followed by calculation of the actual voltage stress on the device under test, which is described in the current IEC 60060-1 standard. Commercial universal measurement systems exist on the market, but until now such measuring systems lack traceability. A measurement system has been developed by RISE which will provide traceability for composite and combined waves, consisting of a software and two modular universal RCR dividers. The software for sampling and analysis, acquires a composite wave for two terminal test objects, or measures and calculates the combined wave stress from two composite waves for three-terminal tests. The extended measurement uncertainties for the wave components are 200 and 400 μV/V for DC and AC and 1% for peak voltage of SI and LI. The resulting system measurement uncertainty for composite and combined waves will be presented, and new parameters discussed for input to the revision of the IEC 60060 series.

articleTitle: AC breakdown strength and EL inception field of TiO2/epoxy nanocomposites having different particle dispersion
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: We have revealed that AC breakdown strength of TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/epoxy nanocomposites having agglomerate sizes smaller than 0.5 μm is higher than that of the unfilled epoxy. This paper investigates AC breakdown strength and electroluminescence (EL) inception field of TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/epoxy nanocomposites having different particle dispersion as a basic study to clarify the mechanism of enhancing the breakdown strength. The particle dispersion of the TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/epoxy nanocomposites was controlled by using centrifugation. We prepared NC0H samples containing agglomerates and NC3H samples not containing the agglomerates larger than 0.05 μm. Compared to the unfilled epoxy, both the EL inception field and AC breakdown strength of NC3H were higher, while the EL inception field and AC breakdown strength of NC0H was lower.

articleTitle: Investigation of stator winding insulation condition of MV motors based on dielectric response measurement
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper presents an investigation of the stator winding insulation condition of medium voltage (MV) motors operated in a power plant. The investigated motors have the same voltage rate of 6.6 kV. Such motors continuously encounter various stresses during service which alter the dielectric properties of the insulation system. Thus, the dielectric response measurement (DRM) was utilized in this research to evaluate the integrity of insulation of stator winding insulation, whether the bulk insulation e.g., moisture absorption, or the surface insulation e.g., existing conductive contamination over- or even moisture adsorption along the endwiding surface. In addition, polarization and depolarization current (PDC) and frequency domain spectroscopy (FDS), as techniques based on DRM, were employed to allow the analysis in both time and frequency domains. Such techniques were performed on the whole MV motors during the shutdown for time-based maintenance, both before and after cleaning and drying for comparison purposes. The visual inspection of such motors evidences that there has considerable dust over the endwinding surface. Such motors were thus thoroughly cleaned to remove such visible dust over the surface of the endwinding. Then, the DRM test results before and after cleaning, were comparably analyzed to characterize the dielectric properties due to such contaminant. Therefore, the effect of the contaminants on the dielectric properties of the stator winding insulation system is introduced and discussed.

articleTitle: Equivalent transmission line model of pulsed electro-acoustic method for space charge measurement inside solid insulation
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Space charge accumulation inside solid insulation can distort the local electric field, which can thus lead to partial discharge and insulation failure phenomena. At present, the pulsed electro-acoustic (PEA) method is widely used in space charge monitoring and diagnosis of single-layer sample, while the multi-layer material measurement puts forward higher performance requirement for the PEA system. This paper proposes an equivalent method of the signal transmission and transformation in the PEA measurement. The mathematical characterization of the signals in the transmission line model and the PEA system is firstly established, based on which the equivalent model of acoustic wave propagation in the latter is proposed. Further comparison of experiment and simulation results verifies the reliability of the model. Based on the simulation of multi-layer material measurement, it is found that the reflected signals in the PEA system can affect the obtained information of space charge, which is also affected by the thickness and layer number of the measured sample. A selection criterion for the multilayer materials in the PEA measurement is finally proposed. The above research can provide an effective analysis scheme for the PEA method in complex measurement and diagnosis.

articleTitle: Statistical analysis of partial discharge activity in CO2, N2 and technical air
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Partial discharges occur when there is a high enough electric field that causes ionisation of the gas molecules, leading to the formation of charged particles and subsequent electrical current flow. Phase-resolved partial discharge patterns provide a comprehensive view of partial discharge activity in electrical equipment in relation to the applied voltage. By analysing these patterns, it is possible to identify different types of partial discharge and the severity of insulation degradation to prevent equipment failure and power outages. This paper investigates quantifying the partial discharge occurring under each half-cycle of the applied voltage for artificial partial discharge defects. The gases utilised during testing are CO2, technical air and N2. The discharges occurring in each half-cycle are split according to polarity. A particular Gaussian curve is developed for each defect under a specific gas utilising histograms and the non-linear least squares fitting method. The plots developed for each case demonstrated an efficient way of visualising the partial discharge acquired from the testing, whilst also providing an efficient tool for quantitative comparison between different cases.

articleTitle: Wavelength-modulation cavity ring-down spectroscopy for SF6 characteristic decomposition component H2S sensing
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Continuous-wave CRDS generally uses cavity length modulation or wavelength modulation to achieve resonance between laser mode and cavity mode. However, cavity length modulation has complex structure and brings measurement error which are difficult to eliminate due to the variation of cavity length. Therefore, in this paper, wavelength modulation is applied to calibrate the spectral frequency. The gas absorption spectrum scanning program was developed based on FPGA, which adopted the strategy of step modulated laser frequency scanning technique and obtained the gas absorption spectrum near wavelength of 1.578 μm based on the ring-down time, thus realizing the accurate measurement of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>S concentration. The Gaussian Profile, Lorentz Profile and Voigt Profile (VP) fitting analysis of the H2S absorption spectrum were carried out to verify the measurement accuracy. It is validated that Lorentz Profile and Voigt Profile are more effective in characterizing the absorption spectra of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>S at 101.3 kPa compared to the Gaussian Profile. The technology is verified to obtain low detection limit and accurate concentration results, which is proved to be reliable in electrical equipment inspection application.

articleTitle: Transient propagation characteristics of ±320kV XLPE cable considering frequency and temperature effects
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Transient propagation characteristics in HVDC cables are of considerable importance for overvoltage calculation and fault location. This paper presents an improved calculation method for wave propagation of a ±320 kV XLPE cable considering frequency and temperature effects as well as a multi-layer distributed model. The material parameters of the cable under different temperatures and in a wide frequency range, 0.1 Hz~100 MHz, were measured. And the results were fitted into the calculation of the impedance and admittance, which was compared with the methods with the approximation of semiconducting layers. It is found that the method proposed in this paper has a better accuracy than others in a wider frequency range. The contribution of the semiconducting layer on total impedance and admittance are both significant, which is required to model separately. Above 1 MHz, the effect of the frequency on the semiconducting material leads to the change of admittance value, which results in differences in the propagation characteristics. Particularly, for the attenuation coefficient, the relative error can be up to 31.5%. In addition, it shows that the effect of the temperature is significant on the propagation characteristics in the low frequency.

articleTitle: New reference HVDC divider for the calibration of testing equipment up to 1600 kV
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: An international metrology project named "EMPIR 19ENG02 FutureEnergy" started in June 2020, is developing, building, and evaluating measurement equipment and systems for the UHV level. This paper describes the work on a new reference UHVDC voltage divider for the calibration of testing equipment up to at least 1600 kV. This divider has a modular design and target expanded measurement uncertainty of 200 μV/V. The need for such measurement systems results from new measurement methods for future energy transmission grids. After the construction of the UHVDC voltage divider, the targeted measurement uncertainty of 200 μV/V was successfully at 1200 kV during a measurement campaign at PTB. The linearity and temperature dependence of the UHVDC divider modules as well as the overall results of this new divider are included in this work. This work will lead to new calibration and measurement capabilities (CMC) for traceability of the designed divider systems for participating national metrology institutes (NMI).

articleTitle: Development of a test platform for DGA studies of transformer liquids under electrical faults
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In the field of condition monitoring of liquid-immersed power transformers, dissolved gas analysis (DGA) is considered to be one of the most effective techniques for indicating incipient thermal and electrical faults. Typical electrical faults can be classified into partial discharge (PD), D1 (discharge of low energy) and D2 (discharge of high energy). It is well known that different dissolved gas patterns correspond to specific fault types. Partial discharge (PD) is usually considered as a low energy process producing key gases such as hydrogen (H2) and acetylene (C2H2) in a mineral oil. However, hydrogen (H2) is an elusive gas, which escapes easily due to its small molecule size and high diffusivity. It shows low affinity for solvents and therefore has relatively low solubility in transformer liquids. As a result, inconsistent H2 results from DGA-electrical fault studies are often found in the literature. This work aims to develop a gas tight platform and a detailed procedure suitable for studying gas generation by PD occurring over a long period (several days). Headspace-gas-chromatography (HS-GC) was used to detect gas in liquid concentrations. The relationship between gas production and discharge energy was also quantified during the course of an experiment where a stable PD was established for a duration of 96 h.

articleTitle: Ionisation coefficients in HFO-1336mzz(E) and HFO-1336mzz(E)/synthetic air mixtures
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Prebreakdown ionisation current I(d) in (E)-1,1,1,4,4,4-hexafluoro-2-butene (HFO-1336mzz(E) vapour and HFO-1336mzz(E) vapour/synthetic air mixtures is measured by the Steady-State Townsend (SST) method, and the ionisation and the electron attachment, effective ionisation coefficients are deduced. It is found that the value of the limiting reduced-electric field in HFO-1336mzz(E) vapour is at approximately 410 Td. It is also found that the value of the limiting reduced-electric field in the mixtures exceed that in SF6 for the mixtures the ratio of which is over 70% HFO-1336mzz(E) content.

articleTitle: Forecasting the current-voltage behavior of multilayer dielectrics based on monolayer measurements
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Equipment connections in MVDC networks may combine different materials. We consider here the assembly of an epoxy and a silicone rubber composite. As the apparent conductivities of the two materials are highly dependent on temperature, water content and electric field, situations may arise where the voltage applied to the bilayer insulation is mainly applied to one of the two layers, either epoxy or silicone, or is divided over the two sheets. Current densities-voltage (J-V) measurements were carried out on the 2 mm thick bilayer samples either at 40℃ under three relative humidity conditions (dry, 50% and 90% relative humidity) or under dry conditions at 40, 60 and 80℃. The voltages applied were between 0.25 and 10 kV. These measurements are compared to the currents calculated from measurements made on each monolayer sample under similar T and RH conditions. Under conditions of T and RH where the apparent conductivities of the two materials are very different, as expected, the currents measured in the bilayer samples were close to the currents flowing in the more resistive material. When the currents are of the same order of magnitude, the calculated currents were found to be relevant for evaluating the measured current in the bilayer samples.

articleTitle: Detection of partial discharge caused by repetitive voltage pulses using high frequency current transformers
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In the evaluation of insulation systems, partial discharge (PD) diagnostics have proven to be a recognized means of nondestructive testing. Normally, PD is expected at high voltage equipment. However, high electrical field strengths also occur in low-voltage equipment like low-voltage motors and consequently PD occur, especially in low-voltage machines that are subjected to pulsed voltages. In order to be able to differentiate these PD pulses from interference caused by a voltage pulse with fast rising edge, measurements in the range of triple-digit MHz have to be considered. In this work it is shown that PD in the high frequency range can be measured on twisted pair devices under test (DUTs) as well as on real motor windings of a 3 kW asynchronous machine. It was irrelevant whether the DUTs were stressed with sinusoidal voltages or repetitive steep-edged test voltages. The repetitive test voltage is generated by a 3-Level Neutral Point Clamped (3L-NPC) inverter. Measurement results are given on the sensitivity of the measurement method and the location of the PD occurring on the test samples were investigated.

articleTitle: Effect of conductive coating on surface discharge of resin composites under impulse voltage
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Fiberglass/epoxy composites are widely used in various types of outdoor radomes and wind turbine blades. Since it is a non-conductive material, radomes and fan blades are susceptible to lightning damage. By coating the lower surface of glass fiber composites with conductive coatings, a new method for regulating the surface discharge characteristics of composites is proposed. Firstly, by changing the content of conductive fillers, coatings with different conductive properties are obtained, and the influence of these coatings on the surface discharge characteristics of composites under lightning impulse voltage is studied. The electrostatic field distribution of the discharge structure is further calculated, and the influence mechanism of the coating on the surface discharge of the composite is analyzed based on the electrostatic field distribution.

articleTitle: Impact of supercapacitor energy storage on transient behaviour of MMC-based grid-forming ES-STATCOM
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Grid-forming controlled Static Synchronous Compensators equipped with an ancillary energy storage are a promising approach to enhance future transmission grid stability by providing virtual inertia. Therefore, this contribution investigates a concept related within a modular multilevel converter-based application and its corresponding grid-forming controls. Here, the additional energy storage is placed on the converters dc-side consisting of supercapacitor modules. The aim of this contribution is to investigate this concept's behaviour related to the charging and discharging processes within the supercapacitor storage and the required instantaneous power supply due to the inherent grid-forming control response of the modular multilevel converter comparing a detailed modelling approach of the supercapacitor storage as well as a simple RC element representation.

articleTitle: Composite crossarm for distribution lines
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Currently, porcelain, epoxy, silicone or glass insulators are used for the insulation of high voltage overhead power lines, which are fixed to the steel structure of the pole. The presented solution is a glass-fiber reinforced composite insulating structure serving as a dielectric crossarm in high voltage power lines. The essence is a solution assembled using components made of composite materials supplemented by steel elements, which exhibits lower weight compared to all-steel solutions and achieves sufficient insulation properties. The solution also includes the additional possibility of using smaller additional ceramic or composite insulators. The individual components are made of suitable materials with regard to their mechanical and electrical stresses and functions throughout the structure. The paper describes the design of a numerical model that simulates the behaviour of the insulator structure, both mechanically and electrically. The investigated characteristics of the materials are described and the final dielectric and mechanical design verification of the crossarm is presented. The electrical tests were done at several materials (polyurethanes and epoxy). The test results of lightning pulse voltage bring no significant differences between materials. Final HV tests for polyurethanes (decision for PU due to the technology) crossarms were performed at final products with good flashover results. The mechanical tests verified the numerical model, which accurately indicates the positions of the failure of the composites under mechanical loading. This phenomenon was observed in every calculation in which contacts were used, especially between steel and composite parts. This is then used as a safety margin for manufacturing, the effect of material aging and climatic effects on the material of the proposed crossarm. The material characterization of several polyurethanes and epoxy variants was investigated using high voltage test methods and mechanical verifications. The new concept of composite crossarm has been introduced regarding the simulations of mechanical and electrical properties.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation on lightning impulse flashover of a 24 kv silicone line pin insulator
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: An experimental investigation is presented on the flashover characteristics of a typical 24 kV silicone line pin insulator under lightning impulses 0.34/47 μs, by considering the amplitude and polarity of the applied voltage as influencing parameters. Based on the oscillographic records of the applied voltage and discharge current different phases of discharge growth could be discerned. Thus, inception, growth and flashover discharge characteristics are assessed and discussed. Increasing amplitude of the applied voltage causes more intense streamer corona activity, which, associated with greater charge, exerts a hindering effect on leader inception, the latter occurring at higher voltages. This is more pronounced for negative impulse voltages under which corona initiates at higher voltage and with higher current, thus also charge. At a given leader inception voltage the charge related to the streamer corona activity preceding leader inception is lower under negative impulses, possibly due to negative surface discharges and charge deposition on the insulator surface, suppressing the growth of streamer corona in air. The average potential gradient required for leader inception at 2.5% flashover probability was estimated approximately 690 and 1050 kV/m under positive and negative polarity impulses, respectively. At a given steepness of the applied voltage at leader inception the charge associated with leader growth is approximately two times larger for negative than positive impulses. The charge at flashover increases linearly with the steepness of the applied voltage at leader inception.

articleTitle: Improvement of a loop antenna for partial discharge measurement of inverter-fed hairpin motors
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The high-frequency switching and steep slew rates from modern switches used in inverters might accelerate degradation of the insulation system of inverter-fed motors. Partial discharge (PD) measurements might be helpful to evaluate the state of an insulation system and detect degradation effects. Hence, PD measurement during common pulse width modulated (PWM) voltage operation is proposed to evaluate the motor insulation. Therefore, this paper mainly focuses on suitable PD measurement methods applicable to the motor during PWM operation using a loop antenna. The antenna is designed for PD measurement according to the characteristics of the PD signal in an inverter-fed hairpin motor. Based on the determined characteristic frequency range of a specific motor's PDs signal from 600 MHz up to 1 GHz, the loop antenna is designed to be sensitive in the range from approx. 0.9-1.2 GHz. It is designed for the PD measurement of the inverter-fed hairpin motor to increase the signal-to-noise ratio as well as its sensitivity to the PD signal. The comparison of the PD measurements done by different sensors in the lab is used to evaluate how loop antennas can improve the sensitivity to the PD signal in the hairpin motor.

articleTitle: Partial discharge characteristics to breakdown in cast resin transformer suffering lightning impulses to accelerate aging
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This research aims to evaluate partial discharge (PD) characteristics of a cast resin transformer (CRTr) up to dielectric breakdown. Multiple positive and negative lightning impulses were applied in a step-up manner to the high voltage windings of a 22 kV CRTr to further accelerate the degradation. Impulse PD signals were detected by a differential high-frequency current transformer. AC PD measurement was performed before and after the impulse applications to analyse PD characteristics under AC voltage. Experimental results revealed that PD activities occurred at 100 kV impulse voltage and impulse PD charge amounted to the magnitude of μC, which is distinctly larger than PD charge under AC voltage (pC), and increased with the number of applied LIs. Breakdown reaching the ending of lifetime of CRTr was observed at the 13th impulse application. PD inception voltage decreased below the operating voltage. Discharge pulses became more intense in the PRPD patterns. PD maximum and mean charge and repetition rate all increased after the LI application. LIs caused large-amplitude PDs in the winding insulation of the CRTr, resulting in significantly accelerated degradation and final breakdown.

articleTitle: Concurrent flashover characteristics of EGLA/rod-rod parallel gap in air for 66/77 kV overhead transmission lines
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Lightning is one of the important problems for the insulation design of transmission lines. In Japan, externally gapped line arresters (EGLA) mainly have been applied to transmission lines for several tens of years, which have excellent features to improve lightning protection performance. On the other hand, multi-phase back-flashover phenomena for overhead transmission lines with EGLA application have not yet been clarified quantitatively in terms of the flashover characteristics in air gaps. In this paper, we report the concurrent flashover characteristics in EGLA / rod-rod parallel gap configuration in consideration of multi-phase fault phenomena under lightning overvoltage. The concurrent flashover characteristics under short-tailed lightning impulse voltage are obtained while observing the propagation of the leader discharge in a series air gap of EGLA and a rod-rod- gap. In addition, we compare the experimental characteristics of discharge propagation and the calculated value for the concurrent flashover model proposed in this paper. As a result, not only the leader discharge but also streamer-type discharge propagation could cause concurrent flashover in EGLA / rod-rod parallel gap configuration.

articleTitle: Useful life estimation of insulated cables based on loss tangent measurement and SVR
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: A study to estimate the useful life of high voltage insulated cables is presented in this article. The methodology suggests a simple way for online measurement of cable's loss tangent. An inductive current meter and a probe with insulation capacity greater than the rated voltage is used to obtain the leakage current and voltage (between the conductor and the cable armor) waveforms, respectively. The value of the loss tangent is obtained from the decomposition of the leakage current signal into active and reactive components. The second part of the methodology suggests the use of an artificial intelligence technique based on the regressive model Support Vector Regression in order to estimate the future values of the loss tangent and to identify the optimal time for an intervention on the cable. Fictitious data based on results published in the literature were used for validation. As a result, the regressive model presented a mean absolute percentage error and a mean squared error of 8.64% and 0.013, respectively. In this way, the effectiveness of the proposed estimation was proven to predict the evolution of the loss tangent and its application proves to be assertive for the preventive monitoring of insulated cables.

articleTitle: Experimental study of exhaust gas temperature in a prototype CO2/C4-FN/O2 circuit breaker using pyrometry
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: High-voltage (HV) circuit breakers have undergone significant developments in recent years to reduce their size, operating energy as well as using eco-efficient insulation gases. While interrupting fault currents, the insulating gas is heated up by the arc to several thousand degrees Celsius which flows to the breaker enclosure via conducting exhaust outlets. The high temperature of the gas at the exhaust can lower the dielectric strength and cause electrical breakdowns at the exit of the exhaust outlets. In this study, we experimentally investigate the temperature of the hot gas at the exhaust pipes in an early prototype of an eco-efficient CO2/C4-FN/O2 based HV circuit breaker using the novel two-colour pyrometry technique. In parallel, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations with conditions identical to experiments are performed, wherein the temperature of the hot gas obtained was in good agreement with the measured values. These studies, done early in the development phase, allow us to optimize the design of the HV circuit breakers in order to avoid hot gas and the associated dielectric breakdowns.

articleTitle: Dielectric model of polarization mechanisms in time domain FEM simulation
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The presented study describes a method to model dielectrics including their polarization mechanisms in time domain FEM simulation to analyse field stresses occurring at pulse voltage. The transition to renewable energies accelerates the development of power modules with higher power density and efficiency. Components close to switched power supplies are stressed with repetitive pulse voltage.
