Especially SiC and GaN based switched power sources allow for high efficiencies together with steep pulse rise time causing accelerated ageing of insulating systems or triggering partial discharges. FEM simulation allows to understand the field stresses inside an insulating system at pulse voltage and may help to identify design weaknesses. In this paper, there is presented a method to model a material including its polarization mechanisms in FEM simulations suitable for pulse voltage excitation. Dielectric spectroscopy measurements were performed to investigate different materials depending on excitation frequency and temperature. Collected data is post-processed to identify the Debye relaxation equations in both the time and frequency domains. The equations are transferred to COMSOL to model the materials in time-dependent simulations. Identified equations and the resulting COMSOL model are both tested against measured spectroscopy data. Measured dielectric spectroscopy data indicate that several materials pass a dispersion region during the transition from rising flank to voltage plateau during pulse voltage excitation. This effect can lead to electric field distributions different from those considering constant permittivities when combining multiple materials in an insulating system. The application of the model shows mentioned challenges in designing insulating systems for pulse voltage that require attention to modelling Debye relaxation mechanisms for specific materials. This modelling approach can be used for further research helping to set up test objects to investigate partial discharges as well as ageing mechanisms at pulse voltage.

articleTitle: Comparison of GIS UHF partial discharge measurements in clean air and SF6
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Gas-insulated switchgears (GIS) as junctions of transmission and distribution networks have increased significance for the assurance of a high quality of the electrical power supply. Considering the increasing cost pressure to the network provider and system erector the reliability and quality of the electrical equipment needs to be assured. Therefore, suitable diagnostic technologies are commonly used to monitor electrical equipment and to potentially extend their service life. For GIS insulation monitoring the UHF partial discharge (PD) monitoring have become the industry standard. More than 40 years' experience exist for such PD measurements in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> GIS. Due to the significant Global Warming Potential (GWP) of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> alternative insulation gases are introduced in last years. The most promising approach in compliance with expected regulations of F-Gas restrictions including PFAS (poly- and perfluoroalkyl substances) is using Clean Air under increased pressure as insulation [1]. Clean Air is a mixture of 80 % Nitrogen and 20 % Oxygen and has a GWP of zero. To understand the impact of the alternative gas on the UHF PD Monitoring approach detailed comparisons of UHF PD measurements in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> and Clean Air are presented in this paper. Investigated are the amplitudes and frequency ranges in which PD signals can be measured. And the PRPD patterns that can be observed for typical PD defects are shown for Clean Air and SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>. Standard monitoring equipment with a frequency range of 300 to 1500 MHz is used. The conclusion of the detailed investigation is that the standard UHF PD monitoring systems can be used for Clean Air GIS as well as for SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> and PRPD patterns look quite similar with some minor deviations.

articleTitle: Non-destructive measurement of permittivity distribution in permittivity graded materials (ɛ-FGM) by X-ray computer tomography
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Toward the compact gas insulated switchgears (GIS), we have been investigating a novel electric field grading technique around the GIS spacer by “functionally graded materials (FGM)” with spatial distribution of permittivity (ɛ-FGM). We have already designed and fabricated the cone-type ɛ-FGM spacer samples with the relative permittivity (ɛr) of 10.0-4.0 for an actual 245 kV-class GIS as well as those with ɛr of 12.7-4.0 for its 1/4-sized model and revealed the improvement of flashover voltage in SF6 gas through experiments and calculations. It is important to develop a non-destructive method to measure and verify the permittivity distribution inside the spacer to realize the practical application of ɛ-FGM spacers. In this paper, in order to establish the non-destructive measurement method for ɛ-FGM spacers with the relative permittivity distribution, we focused on X-ray computed tomography (CT). We obtained the relationship between the permittivity and the X-ray transmission intensity by analysing different disc-shaped samples (or =12.2-4.2) and verified the measurement possibility of the relative permittivity distribution inside ɛ-FGM spacer by comparison to the target distribution at the fabrication of ɛ-FGM spacer.

articleTitle: Measurement system for surface potentials in realistic HVDC-GIS environments
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The growing use of high voltage direct current (HVDC) systems has led to a growing interest in the use of gas insulated systems (GIS) for HVDC applications. Compared to traditional AC systems, the use of direct current poses different challenges within the insulation design. One of these is the slow migration of charges on insulator surfaces like partition insulators. In this contribution a measurement setup is presented to investigate the behaviour of these charges inside a real GIS setup under full service conditions over long observation times. The setup consists of a heated HVDC GIS loop in which surface charges on insulators can be investigated, with voltages up to 350 kV<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DC</sub> for both polarities. To provide conditions comparable to a GIS in service, operating temperatures are obtained by heating the inner conductor using induced AC currents. The surface potentials are measured using field probes. A 5-axis robot inside the GIS can position the probes on every point of the insulators’ surfaces. Due to the slow speed of the charge migration, the setup is designed for long term measurements of several months. This contribution introduces the entire setup used for the proposed investigations and determines the capabilities of this method by first test measurement results.

articleTitle: Outdoor composite hollow insulators with extra-large diameters
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Siliconization of composite hollow insulators is a usual technology to cope with the condition of outdoor installations of high voltage (HV) equipment. Here different kind of silicones, different application methods and different manufacturing methods were developed. For all of them one common limiting factor can be found: the diameter of the glass fibre reinforced epoxy structure (GFRP). Typical limitations are in the range of 1.2 to 1.5 m. Especially for devices like high voltage test equipment diameters up to 3.5 m are required. To cover such large diameters suitable manufacturing technologies needs to be developed and proven. The paper will cover the analysis and comparison of methods to manufacture extra-large diameters of siliconized hollow insulators. Details are given from the comparison and measurements of different gluing methods. Exemplary, DC voltage tests of extra-large hollow insulators as part of an HV test system at rain conditions are discussed. Here the leakage currents were measured and evaluated to determine the effect of loss and recovery of hydrophobicity.

articleTitle: Electrical characteristics with surface roughness and interfacial pressure for HVDC PP cable joint model
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In this paper, the DC breakdown characteristics of a PP/EPDM interfacial model with interfacial pressure and roughness were studied for the development of the joint for HVDC PP cables. As a result, it was confirmed that the breakdown voltage varied depending on the degree of surface roughness (#320, #800, M(mirror-like smooth surface)) of the PP sample and interfacial pressure (0.5 bar, 1.0 bar, 1.5 bar) between PP and EPDM. The #800 sample did not show a difference in breakdown voltage between 0.5 bar and 1.0 bar, but showed an increase in breakdown voltage when the pressure was increased to 1.5 bar. The #320 sample showed low breakdown values regardless of the pressure, indicating that the insulation strength did not increase even with increasing interfacial pressure due to the high surface roughness of the sample.

articleTitle: Possibilities and limits of diagnostic methods for power transformers in service
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The detection of possible faults in an early state is of elementary interest to operators of transformers in order to avoid unplanned outages. Such unplanned failures lead to the interruption of energy supply or even loss of production. Therefore, a large number of diagnostic methods are available such as oil analysis and electrical measurements up to high-voltage tests on site. For this reason, it is necessary for operators to select the meaningful diagnostic procedures in each case. In this contribution investigation are discussed concerning the question which diagnostic procedures or which combination of procedures can be used to detect faults reliable. This was done based on a large population of transformers in service.

articleTitle: Simulation of energy loss in distribution transformer considering three-phase unbalance
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Three-phase unbalance in power distribution network causes the extra energy loss of distribution transformer. To quantitatively analyse the influence of unbalance degree on the loss level, simulations works based on power system simulation and finite element method were conducted. Typical distribution transformer connection layout including Y/y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n0</sub> and D/y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n11</sub> were considered in the simulation. Simplified equivalent model established in PSCAD software indicates that the active loss increase rapidly when the distribution network is unbalanced. Further modelling about detailed transformer structure in COMSOL software displays that eddy-current loss in clamp is another non-negligible heat source besides the copper loss. With the increase of unbalance degree, both copper loss and eddy-current loss display nonlinear growth trends. These additional losses arisen from three-phase unbalance should be carefully considered in the design and maintenance of distribution transformer.

articleTitle: Polarity reversal effect on partial discharge performance of different dielectric materials for aerospace applications
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Aeronautical conditions and increasing power demand bring challenges to the electrification of aircraft concept. Electrical systems should be designed to operate under extreme environmental conditions and high electrical stresses. To improve system reliability, the electrical performance of insulation within the aircraft must be specified to withstand those stresses and conditions. For the next generation aircraft, the energy sources will likely deliver direct current and therefore, dc grid structures are mainly considered by aircraft manufacturers. Partial Discharge mechanisms and insulation performance have different behaviour under ac and dc voltages. Polarity reversal during operation imposes high electric stress on the insulation material. For High Voltage Direct Current cables, there are polarity reversal strategies and defined polarity reversal periods. However, cables that are designed for aerospace applications operate under completely different environmental conditions and those strategies must be revised accordingly. In this work, a systematic study shows the effect of polarity reversal on partial discharge activity. Different insulation materials have been tested under variable sub-atmospheric pressure corresponding to different flight altitudes. The partial discharge performance of these materials is examined for various slew rates changing from one polarity to the other at the proposed operating voltages.

articleTitle: How to fail the measure of DC conductivity or resistivity of polymeric materials
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The advent of HVDC and MVDC applications arrived with a challenge for the dielectric's community: the determination of the conductivity of insulating materials under DC stresses, particular challenging for non-linear materials. Usually obtained from current-voltage (I-V) tests, this work shares a series of faults (and learnings) resulted from the struggle to tailor a reproducible and repeatable protocol for electrical current measurements of polymeric insulating samples. I-V measures have been conducted for epoxy and silicone samples under various electric fields, temperatures and water contents. Results shows that, if the objective is to fail in I-V measurement, it is enough to: Underestimate the structure/microstructure relationship of departure; underestimate key physical parameters during the test; and underestimate the structure/microstructure changes during the test. For each case, illustrations and quantification have being given. Because the electrical current seems to be highly biased by the system characteristics, and since the conductivity calculated from the Ohm's law has no physical meaning in non-Ohmic regions, the intrinsic conductivity of polymeric insulating is hardly attainable.

articleTitle: Design of a compact high voltage DC power supply for electron beam applications
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: For future mobile applications of electron beam sources, a modular and compact High Voltage DC Power Supply (HVDC-PS) is demanded. This paper describes the development of a HVDC-PS providing continuously power up to 120 kV / 100 mA with the added specification that the supply should be scalable to 500 kV / 200 mA by using Insulated Core Transformer (ICT) technology, in order to reduce weight, volume and enable a high degree of integration. The adopted architecture implements a high switching frequency and PCB based secondary windings and rectifiers. A higher power density and therefore smaller power supply volume can be achieved by means of the use of digital control and smart measurement. A prototype, using mostly low cost SMT components which are widely available, was designed.

articleTitle: Investigation of repeatability of conductive clothing laboratory testing process
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Live-line maintenance with bare-hand working methodology is a possible solution to carry out planned or failure-preventive interventions on the energized overhead lines of the high-voltage grid. During such an intervention, the linemen wear conductive clothing, which acts as a Faraday cage, when the worker is electrically connected to the potential of one of the phase conductors. As conductive clothing functions as a personal protective equipment (PPE), its continuous inspection is essential to guarantee the linemen's safety. However, the testing methodology of conductive garments is roughly defined, which can cause high deviation in the results, even a conductive clothing can fail or pass the testing process depending on which laboratory and which personnel inspects it. This article aims to investigate how the poorly defined parameters affect the laboratory inspection results and, in this way, the overall classification of the inspected conductive clothing. For this purpose, several laboratory measurements on different conductive suits were carried out to explore the testing method deviations; suggestions for standard improvement are also proposed.

articleTitle: Flashover voltage of permittivity graded materials (ɛ-FGM) spacer with metallic particles in SF6 gas
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Functionally graded materials with spatial distribution of permittivity (ɛ-FGM) are promising for the compact, efficient and environmentally benign GIS spacers. In this paper, for the practical insulation design and installation of ɛ-FGM spacers to GIS, the risk of metallic particles on ɛ-FGM spacers is investigated. Experimental results using the fabricated cone-type ɛ-FGM spacers revealed that the metallic particles in permittivity-grading area on convex surface were the most harmful and reduced the flashover voltage in SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas by about 40 %, compared with that without the particles. The flashover voltage was almost equal to that of the conventional spacers with a uniform permittivity distribution and the metallic particles in the maximum electric field area on concave surface. Thus, the risk of metallic particles on ɛ-FGM spacers can be almost the same as that of the conventional spacers.

articleTitle: Wideband characterisation of a high-voltage test transformer using Pseudo-Random impulse sequence perturbation
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: High-voltage test transformers are commonly operated in step-up mode to generate high voltages for testing power system equipment such as transmission cables, insulation, and transformers. Accurate equivalent circuit models of these transformers can provide insight into the processes that take place within the device, improve the simulation accuracy, and provide an understanding of the transformer interaction with external circuits. This paper explores the use of a Pseudo-Random Impulse Sequence (PRIS) as a perturbation signal for the wideband characterisation and parameter estimation of a high-voltage test transformer, which formed part of a larger master's study [1]. A 7.5kVA, 230V/100kV high-voltage test transformer is perturbed with a PRIS signal using a custom-designed perturbation source, and the frequency responses of the transformer open-circuit and short-circuit input impedances are determined. A wideband six-section lumped parameter equivalent circuit model is proposed for the transformer, and it is shown that the topology can represent the observed resonances in the frequency responses of the input impedances accurately up to 10kHz. A two-step parameter estimation methodology is subsequently implemented to solve for the model parameters that best fit the measured frequency responses.

articleTitle: Localization of partial discharge sources in power transformers using neural networks
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Since power transformers are an indispensable part of electrical grids, their condition monitoring plays a crucial role in maintaining a grid's reliability. Partial discharges (PD) are a common reason for ageing in power transformers, and ultra-high frequency (UHF) sensors installed on the transformer tank are an option for continuous online monitoring. One of the advantages of UHF condition monitoring is the possibility of three-dimensional PD source localization. However, the propagation paths of the PD signals are not straight lines because of the complex internal structure of power transformers. Such indirect propagation inside the tank leads to localization errors using time difference of arrival (TDoA) analysis. Therefore, in this contribution, dense neural networks (NN) are used to localize PD sources in a validated simulation model of a 300 MVA power transformer. The NN uses the information obtained from the time-domain signals to predict the coordinates of the PD source. Two approaches are implemented for this purpose, both based on TDoA. It is observed that the NN makes more accurate coordinates predictions than simply using TDoA. The NN predicts the coordinates of the source up to an average deviation of 13.65 cm, and on using cross-validation, the deviation improves to 10.77 cm. However, evaluating the model's performance when it encounters previously unseen data is also necessary. Hence, one PD source is removed during training, and the resulting accuracy for that source is 56.41 cm. The lower accuracy, in this case, may be due to the lack of variation in the training data.

articleTitle: Comparison of movement behavior of wire and spherical particles applying AC and DC voltage
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In the SF6 Gas Insulated Switchgear (GIS), metallic particles of various shapes generated during normal operation and manufacturing processes are levitated and moved under the influence of an electric field. The levitated metallic particles affect the high-voltage conductor and cause serious dielectric problems such as partial discharge and dielectric breakdown. This problem can be solved by applying a resistive coating inside the GIS that suppresses the levitation of metallic particles. However, in the case of resistive coatings, the unit cost is high, so when applied entirely inside the GIS, a considerable cost is incurred. For this reason, considering economic feasibility, an efficient application area is required, and the behavioral characteristics of metallic particles should be analyzed. In this paper, when AC and DC voltages are applied to a parallel plate, the motion characteristics of the shape and number of metallic particles and the lift-off voltage are tested. As a result, it was confirmed that the lift-off voltage decreased when the number of metallic particles increased in AC and DC voltage, and both the maximum bounce height and the first behavior width of particles increased.

articleTitle: Insulation properties of fluoren-based epoxy resin composites in humid and hot environment
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Epoxy composites are widely used in high voltage bushings, GIS insulators, dry type voltage/current transformers and other power equipment because of their good heat resistance property, insulation property and machinability. In the service process, epoxy resin composites will be affected by the external humid and hot environment, and then aging happen, resulting in the deterioration of its insulation performance, ultimately leads to equipment insulation accidents. In this paper, in order to solve this problem, multiple benzene ring structure was introduced into epoxy resin to improve the hydrophobic ability of epoxy composites, and then improve the insulation performance of epoxy composites under hot and humid conditions. The fluoren-based epoxy resin composites was cured by methyltetrahydrophthalic anhydride, and its insulation properties before and after wet and thermal aging were tested with bisphenol A epoxy composites. Compared with the common bisphenol A epoxy composites, it was found that the insulation properties of epoxy composites with multiple benzene ring structure were significantly improved after wet and thermal aging.

articleTitle: Test method for evaluation of ability for recovery of hydrophobicity of composite insulators
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: A key feature for composite insulators is their ability for recover of hydrophobicity of the housing, which should be preferably kept during the whole service life. As long as a material is "alive" and produce the so-called Low Molecular Weight (LMW) components, encapsulating salts in the pollution layer, the in-service pollution performance will be good. At present there is no relevant tests to evaluate the recovery of hydrophobicity, only the so-called Hydrophobicity Transfer Test became recently available in IEC standards (2021). The test is purely intended to distinguish the Hydrophobicity Transfer Materials (HTM) from non-HTM, rather than to rank different HTMs. Thus, a new test, called Test of Recovery of Hydrophobicity (Dynamic Hydrophobicity Test) is proposed in this paper. Development of this test method is presented starting with the plates of materials and to the insulator's samples. The background for the test is as follows: LMW components governing the material's hydrophobicity penetrate the pollution layer and encapsulate the salt particles. This process gradually increases the electrical resistance of the pollution layer. The recovery ability can be evaluated and compared for different artificially contaminated insulators by measuring how the resistance of the pollution layer increases over time.

articleTitle: Effects of temperature on nonlinear stress grading materials for aerospace applications
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Many countries have developed roadmaps to achieve net-zero emissions and protect the environment from climate change. The electrification of transportation, including the aviation industry, is an important component of these efforts. The use of higher power electrical systems in aerospace applications leads to the need for higher voltage levels. As a result, there is likely to be a requirement for grading of surface electric fields should technologies such as screened cables be adopted. The electrical conductivity of the stress grading system plays a critical role in managing surface electric fields to safe levels. However, their performance is affected by temperature. Therefore, it is necessary to investigate the effect of the temperatures expected in the aerospace environment on the electrical conductivity of stress grading materials and develop suitable designs for high-voltage aerospace power systems. In this paper, the performance of a non-linear stress grading tape is assessed by experiment and the results analysed using finite element techniques in the context of a high voltage aerospace power system.

articleTitle: Using capacitive electric field sensors to measure transient overvoltages: a case study
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper presents the application of a measurement system based on capacitive electric field sensors to measure transient overvoltages in a 420 kV substation. Capacitive voltage transformers (CVTs) are commonly used to measure voltages above 123 kV in substations, but they have a band-limited frequency response due to design characteristics. Therefore, a device with a wide frequency band is required to measure fast transients accurately. First, the limitations of CVTs in measuring fast transients are discussed. Then, the measurement system used in this case study is presented, including the results of the tests performed in the high-voltage laboratory and details of the installation in the substation. Afterwards, exemplary transient overvoltages measured and recorded by the measurement system on a 420 kV overhead line are presented and discussed. The transients are related to the switching operations of a transmission line and a disturbance in the power system. The results show that the measurement system can successfully record transient overvoltages in a substation. Moreover, it is easy to install and does not require de-energization. Therefore, this measurement system is an efficient solution to monitor transient overvoltages.

articleTitle: The adsorption behaviour along insulator-interface and spatial dispersion concentration detection of micron-nano metal-dust in GIL
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: GIL is an important carrier of new power system transmission, which is widely applied in urban power corridors, power transmission across rivers and other scenes. Metal micron-nano dust is inevitably produced in the process of GIL's production, transportation, operation and maintenance. Under the influence of coupling field in GIL cavity, micron-nano dust is dispersed in the cavity space and easily adsorbed on the insulator surface. With the increase of dispersion concentration and the accumulation of adsorption capacity, it will cause serious insulation breakdown. Therefore, this article first studied the adsorption characteristics of micron-nano dust, special adsorption phenomena such as "dust speckles" appeared. Then, a detection platform for the spatial dispersion concentration of micron-nano dust based on light scattering method is designed. The laser source with 632.8 nm wavelength is used to detect the spatial dispersion concentration of micron-nano dust with 15 μm through the detection platform. The numerical relationship between spatial dispersion concentration and adsorption capacity of micron-nano dust was established through experiments. Thus, the detection of the spatial dispersion concentration of micron-nano dust can reflect the adsorption amount, provide effective and reliable data support in the initial stage of micron-nano dust adsorption, and provide the basis for fault warning and equipment maintenance.

articleTitle: Optical detection of gas discharges at small structures
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The requirements for electronic components are increasing, this concerns the cost pressure and the reliability specifications, such as the service lifetime. It is of decisive interest to know the lifetime and degradation mechanisms of the used materials, for example, circuit boards, cable connectors, circuit modules, inverters, or motors. Partial discharges can occur on any of these components at a corresponding electric field strength level. These discharges have an impact on the service life and cause a corresponding degradation of the components/insulations. The degradation leads to premature failure and can, however, be prevented by appropriate designs and other optimizations. The discharges manifest themselves in the form of UV light emissions, which cannot be detected by the human eye, but with appropriate camera technology and filters. State-of-the-art measurement systems on the market do not offer automated, precise, and reliable detection and even less localization of gas discharges. It enables precise localization of small discharges. In this paper, an example measurement is carried out on a specially developed circuit board with optical partial discharge detection. It is shown how sensitive the measurement is. The investigation of the sensitivity and the advantages and possibilities of the system is outlined.

articleTitle: Approaching low-level light extraction from GIS/GIL systems to enable optical partial discharge monitoring
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Ultra-high frequency (UHF) partial discharge (PD) detection is the most common technique for gas insulated switchgear (GIS) application. However, UHF detection is insensitive to defect types with slow discharge behavior. Also, PD from metallic particles on insulators may remain undetected, potentially leading to severe system failure. Optical PD measurement appears to be a promising technique to cope with these issues and can improve PD detection of existing GIS assets. One of the key challenges is collecting and extracting light from a hermetic GIS container in a minimally invasive way. This is achieved with transparent acrylic rods which are the object of this study. Aim is to assess their qualification for guiding low-level light from the inside of the GIS compartment to a retro-fitted photo multiplier tube (PMT) as an opto-electrical converter that feeds into conventional PD measuring equipment. The dependence of the received optical power on the incident angle of light is analyzed by means of measurements in accordance with ray tracing simulations. A 405 nm laser and a corona PD are used as light sources. Maximum collection sensitivity could be identified for frontal and lateral incoming light.

articleTitle: Study on PD characteristics of internal gas-gap defects in composite insulation under high-frequency electric stress
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: High-frequency power transformer (HFPT), with the function of flexible voltage conversion and renewable energy integration, was regarded as an ideal equipment for building a new power system. At present, HFPT mainly uses dry insulation, that is, epoxy resin (EP) as cast insulation and polyimide (PI) as inter-turn insulation to form a composite insulation structure. HFPT is prone to introduce air gap cavities at the composite insulation in the process of installation, operation, and maintenance, which is considered to be one of the causes of equipment discharge failure. It is of great practical significance to study the partial discharge characteristics of air gap cavities at the interface of composite insulation under electro-thermal coupling. In order to clarify the influence mechanism of the temperature on partial discharge (PD) characteristics of air gap cavity under a high-frequency electric field, a set of composite insulation partial discharge test platforms under high-frequency voltage was established. The PD characteristics of the epoxy resin-polyimide composite insulation interface were investigated under different temperatures. The results show that when the experimental temperature of composite insulation increases from 30 ℃ ℃ to 180 ℃, the PD inception voltage (PDIV) decreased by 38.9%, the average discharge amplitude and the number of one-cycle discharge increased from 35.2 mV and 50 times/s to 171.9 mV and 268 times/s respectively, while the discharge repetition rate also increases from 50 times/s to 268 times/s. At the same temperature, the discharge amplitude decreases with the increase of voltage frequency, while the discharge times increase. It is revealed that the influence mechanism of temperature on PD characteristics of composite insulation is as follows: The temperature rise will improve the migration speed of charge at the interface and decrease the synthetic field distortion in the air gap cavity, which increases the number of discharges and the discharge amplitude. This paper is helpful to provide a basis for the detection of the composite insulation state of HFPT.

articleTitle: Measurement and simulation of synthetic test circuit interaction during breaking operation in a vacuum interrupter
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The aim of the society is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions it is necessary to establish an alternative to SF6 circuit breakers. An environmentally friendly alternative is the vacuum interrupter (VI). Researches and developments are needed to increase the switching performance of VI. Therefore, breaking operation tests are necessary. The vacuum interrupter is stressed during the breaking operation by a high current and transient recovery voltage. Thereby, responses out of the test circuit are generated by transient events. Additionally, an interaction between plasma behaviour and test circuit occurs. In this paper an analysis of the measured current at current zero is carried out. This current is split into response current and post-arc current. Measurements and simulations were carried out in a synthetic test field, a Weil-Dobke circuit. Currents up to 30 kA peak, 50 Hz and transient recovery voltages of 70 kV peak were investigated. Variations of the circuit elements were examined to show which element has the most influence on the circuit response. Aim is to identify the response current and which has the most influence on the measured post-arc current to prove the pure plasma behaviour. A variation of the elements shows the possibility to determine these influences.

articleTitle: Isothermal space charge measurement at low temperatures
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The electrical properties of polymers can change dramatically under low temperatures, which limits their application. There are several polymers to be investigated, such as polyethylene, polypropylene, and epoxy resin. In this work, with the help of the improved pulsed electro-acoustic (PEA) technique, we take more observations on polyethylene. The basic tests in the range of -120°C ~ 20°C are implemented. It is indicated that below some temperature points, the short circuit waveform is more valuable than the poling waveform. The isothermal current theory and detrapping model can be used in the short circuit process to estimate the trap distribution and apparent mobility. It is found that the graphite electrode is more likely to inject charges than the aluminum electrode, and the polarity differences are distinct. Some peculiar phenomena, such as the trap depth calculated by residual charge having a shift at low temperatures, emerged and are discussed. The results show correlations with some thermal analysis results.

articleTitle: Propagating uncertainty using IEEE STD C57.104-2019 dissolved gas analysis methodology for transformers
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Dissolved Gas Analysis is a well-established tool for transformer health monitoring with published Standards to help with its interpretation. However, even though it is known that there is measurement uncertainty regarding the true value of sampled gas, there is less available guidance regarding the practical implications. This paper proposes a method for propagating the measurement uncertainties through the methodology presented in the IEEE Std C57.104-2019 to provide the degree of support for its potential outputs. This is done relying on the simplifying assumption that the measurement uncertainty can be expressed as a symmetric triangular distribution for a given gas sample, and that gas samples are independent. The joint probability function is derived in general terms analytically and then a stratified sampling approach is proposed to numerically solve the function. In addition, a modification is made to allow for a more constrained sampling space by deriving and using a simplifying marginal probability without impacting accuracy. These are presented via a use of a case study to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approaches.

articleTitle: Partial discharge power flow in gas-insulated substations using magnetic and electric antennas
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Some partial discharge (PD) charge estimation challenges in gas-insulated substations (GIS) are reflections and external interference. In a recent study, the authors demonstrated that it is possible to estimate the charge in a GIS using magnetic and electric antennas. Furthermore, the forward and backward components are segregated when both antennas are combined, enabling PD power flow calculation and overlapping reduction. This paper shows the antennas-combination method in a fullscale GIS, where the power flow pattern was compared between PD and external noise. Furthermore, the charge was calculated for the individual antennas and their combinations. The results show the possibility of identifying PD from interference using the PD power flow and charge estimation improvement. These results are promising for GIS qualification tests and online insulation condition monitoring.

articleTitle: Modelling of arcing phenomena during opening contacts in novel circuit breaker
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: With the resurgence of interest in long-distance transmission and the integration of green energy projects into the power grid, high voltage DC (HVDC) technology has emerged as a promising solution. This is due to its lower investment cost and losses, as well as its superior controllability and stability compared to AC transmission systems. Consequently, equipment manufacturers and network operators are increasingly focused on high voltage DC circuit breakers as essential components for AC and DC grid interconnectivity and for interrupting DC faults without causing widespread power outages. However, challenges persist in breaking HVDC circuits during electrical faults, given the absence of zero crossings and the rapid spread of faults. Arcing is inevitable between the separating electrodes, and understanding its behaviour is crucial for the design of new switching devices. In this paper, we present a 2D arc model between two axisymmetric cylindrical copper electrodes and calculate the arc core resistance for a stationary arc. Subsequently, we propose a simplified analysis of the circuit breaker, effectively introducing the circuit with a variable arc resistor. This conceptual model can predict the commutation process and arc interruption using a straightforward circuit model with variable arc resistance.

articleTitle: Dielectric strength of epoxy-air interface under superimposed AC+DC voltage
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In modern electrical grids DC voltage is becoming more widely spread. In addition to the need of coupling DC networks with the existing AC grids, DC networks of different voltage levels must be coupled with each other. In coupling installations, the insulation system is stressed by a superimposed AC+DC voltage. This leads not only to the higher electric field strength in the insulation, but also to accumulation of space charges in solid insulation caused by the DC voltage. The space charges create the electric field of their own which can influence the resulting electric field and the breakdown voltage. The goal of this study is to evaluate the influence of the accumulation of space and surface charges under AC and DC voltage on the dielectric strength of an epoxy-air interface under superimposed DC+AC 50 Hz stress. The results show that the dielectric strength under AC+DC stress depends on the value of the DC voltage. At the same time the surface charge distribution under AC+DC and pure DC stress is different. The higher the AC component, the lower the charge density. Approaches to quantify the influence of space charges on the electric field distribution using COMSOL Multiphysics were considered.

articleTitle: Prediction of the lightning discharge impact point by neural networks
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In this paper a software program using neural networks is developed in order to predict the impact point of the lightning discharge in the presence of a protection. A bank of previously established experimental data is used for learning. Thus, we are interested in the influence of several parameters on the validity and precision of the elaborated neural network among which we include the number of: hidden layers, neurons, iterations as well as the polarity of the applied voltage (positive or negative). The simulation results are compared with those obtained experimentally. It was shown that the variation in the number of neurons and hidden layers influences the validity of the neural network. This allowed us to deduce the optimal values from the established network. The number of iterations does not have too much influence on the validity of the model but rather on its precision. The study of each polarity independently of the other is essential. Indeed, by combining the databases of the two polarities the validity of the network decreases. This result calls into question the simplifying assumptions of the electrogeometrical model which does not take into account the polarity of the applied voltage when sizing protection.

articleTitle: Recommendations for the use of the sweep-frequency-response-analysis method for fault diagnosis on rotating machines
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Sweep-Frequency-Response-Analysis (SFRA), a known diagnostic method for power transformers, can be applied for rotating machines without difficulty. It can be carried out without great effort. The measuring voltage is 10 Vpp and therefore cannot cause any damage to the machine. The SFRA result creates a good overview of the overall condition of the machine, including information about the electrical and inductive circuit or mechanical integrity. Furthermore, it proves advantageous that also information is gained about parts of the machine that are not directly in the electrical measurement circuit. This makes it possible to determine even faults that are difficult to detect, like failures in the rotor of a rotating machine with pure stator measurements. However, there are some requirements to be considered for a successful application on rotating machines. In this work, specific recommendations shall be given to ensure reproducible and reliable results. The first part deals with the topic of connection techniques. Since the measurements are made in the frequency range up to 2 MHz, a connection technique and grounding is necessary, which minor influences on the measurement result itself. Another essential point is the influence of the rotor position during the measurement. For a reliable time-based comparison, the position must be equal. Alternatively, measurements of an entire rotation range (0°…360°) can be recorded and analyzed. An explanation of the influence of the rotor angle on different frequency ranges is given. The resolution of the measurements depends on the number of pole pairs of the machine, for which concrete steps are suggested. Lastly, various statistical factors like the Standard Deviation of Difference (SDD) or the Root Mean squared Error (RMSE) for the interpretation of SFRA results are presented in the paper. These are compared with each other and their suitability for this application is evaluated.

articleTitle: Characteristics of the inter-section insulation transformer winding model with esters under short-tailed impulse voltages
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Replacing petrochemical-derived mineral oil with biodegradable bio-derived ester oil for the electrical insulating oil used in transformers has gained attention in recent years. In general, ester oil has a high saturated moisture content, and in the case of transformers, the residual moisture of both the conductor-coated insulation paper and pressboard is transferred into the ester oil, thereby suppressing the degradation of the solid insulation. Therefore, they are expected to extend the lives of transformers. The insulation properties of three types of biodegradable insulating oil were investigated using an inter-section insulation model of transformer windings, simulating the case of a lightning impulse applied to an oil-immersed transformer. As a result, V-t characteristics were obtained, in which the dielectric breakdown characteristics improved with the applied short tail of the lightning impulse waveforms. The dielectric breakdown voltages at room and elevated temperatures showed a large difference in the dispersion of the measured data, although the average values and V-t characteristics were almost the same. We further analysed the data using the Weibull probability distribution and compared the results.

articleTitle: Short-time evaluation technique of degradation degree by surface discharge
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Silicone rubber (SiR) is being adopted as the housing material for insulators. However, the hydrophobic property and the recovery characteristic might be degraded under multiple stress. As one of the degradation diagnosis techniques for the long-term reliability evaluation of SiR, we have proposed a continuous salt fog test in which 20 - times salt fog aging tests by applying ac voltage for 3 h were repeatedly carried out. However, it takes a much longer time. In this study, we examined a novel technique by using surface discharges (SDs) instead of the previous technique. The SDs were generated on the aged SiR surface for 10 s, and then the hydrophobicity recovery time obtained by measuring the contact angle of a water droplet on the SiR was evaluated. The results indicate a possibility that the hydrophobicity recovery time after the SD treatment can refer to the degradation degree of SiR without causing physical and chemical damage.

articleTitle: Accelerated cable ageing at elevated frequencies in wet conditions
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Ageing processes due to long-term operation cause a negative effect on a power cable insulation system. Most common causes of insulation deterioration are elevated temperature, operating voltage and humidity. Some standards require ageing tests, which are usually long-term tests, as an acceptance test for power cables. In one type of the ageing test, the power frequency voltage is applied on the cable for a duration of two years. In order to reduce the duration of this test, the standard HD 620 offers an accelerated ageing option where the applied voltage frequency is elevated (500 Hz). In these conditions, the duration of the test should be 3000 h. According to the test procedure, a 60 m long cable should be immersed in warm water (55 °C) and an elevated frequency voltage is then applied to it. This kind of a test is challenging because a 60 m long cable is a big load for a typical laboratory source. Moreover, since these tests are long-term, customers often require multiple cables to be tested in parallel. Compensation of capacitive currents imposes as a solution to that problem. However, the design of compensation equipment is a challenge as well because losses in core of the compensating inductor at 500 Hz are huge, and air inductors, on the other hand, have low inductance and therefore low compensating effect. In this work, a test circuit designed in high voltage laboratory for accelerated ageing test on power cables with elevated frequency is described. Derived through FEM analysis, the compensation solutions for elevated frequency using multiple air inductors and design of those inductors are described as well.

articleTitle: Predicting the surface charges using discharge current pulses
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The buildup of charge on the surface of an insulator is one of the concerning factors in many areas such as electrical, aerospace, biomedical, etc. In high voltage systems, micro discharges are inevitable and responsible for the insulator surface charging, which further causes the system to malfunction by altering the local electric field. The phenomena of insulator surface charging also find applications in electrostatic painting, surface coating, electrets, etc. Therefore, the analysis and measurement of surface charge need to be realised with an advanced approach. This work proposes an idea to estimate the surface charge deposition through the corona current pulses. The relation is obtained by varying the pressure from 101 to 70 KPa in the needle-to-plane gap. It is observed that the charge calculated from the current pulse has an approximately linear relation with the total charge deposited on the insulator sample.

articleTitle: Experimental study of air discharge under various frequency stress with inhomogeneous field
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In this paper, air discharges for different frequencies are tested in a point-plane geometry with different air gaps. The stress frequencies vary between 50 Hz to 5 kHz, and air gaps vary from 2.5mm to 10mm. It is observed that the partial discharge inception voltage of the positive corona increases with the increase of frequency, while the inception voltage of the negative corona stays nearly the same. The breakdown voltage increases with the increase of frequency in our test set, and breakdowns happen during negative half-cycle, especially at 5kHz, which is supposed to be caused by the space charges.

articleTitle: Antioxidant migration on dielectric properties of long-term impregnated insulating oil
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: High voltage capacitors are widely used in electrical power systems. For better capability in applications, capacitors are impregnated with insulating oil. Polypropylene in its natural state is inherently unstable and degrades when exposed to oxygen. To avoid oxidation that occurs in the process of film forming, antioxidants are developed and used. In this paper, the polypropylene casts added respectively with antioxidant 1010, 3114, 330 and BHT were long-term impregnated in benzyl toluene oil. Secondly, the frequency domain dielectric spectroscopy method was used to study the dielectric properties of the oil. In addition, the effect of antioxidants on the polarization relaxation process of insulating oil was analyzed. The results indicate that antioxidants and small molecular polypropylene in the amorphous region of the film migrate to the oil during long-term impregnation, resulting in increases in relative dielectric constant ɛr, dielectric loss tanδ and dc conductivity σdc, and affect the polarization relaxation process. Among these antioxidants, antioxidant 1010 has the greatest impact on insulating oil, while antioxidant 330 has the least impact.

articleTitle: Justification for development of a partial discharge resistant insulation system for medium-frequency medium-voltage transformers
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The increasing occurrence of couplings between AC and DC systems or the decoupling of two AC systems leads to an increasing demand for medium-voltage converter systems. The current developments in the field of power electronics have led to a raised investigation of Solid-State-transformers (SST) for medium-voltage applications. This paper offers a technological overview of medium-frequency medium-voltage (MF-MV) transformers included in SSTs. By using a meta study on key design parameters of the MF-MV-transformers the state of the art is identified and future operating parameters are estimated. Based on a defined scenario, the advantages of SST systems with high operating voltages over conventional topologies are presented and considered critically. After an economic view, a comprehensive picture of the advantages and disadvantages of MF-MV-transformer with high operating voltages in SSTs is shown.

articleTitle: Very fast transient overvoltages estimation method using Fourier transform in gas insulated switchgear
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Very Fast Transient Overvoltages (VFTO) are generated mainly from switching operations in Gas Insulated Switchgear (GIS). The capacitive voltage sensors have been developed and applied for measuring exact VFTO waveforms which cannot be measured by existing equipment like potential transformers and coupling capacitor voltage transformers. The capacitive voltage sensors proposed by previous research works showed they have an accurate performance to observe VFTO waveforms. However, the application of these sensors requires additional space and cost to place them on the GIS structure. Hence, this paper proposes a new method to estimate VFTO waveforms by using pre-installed ultra-high frequency (UHF) sensors combined with Fourier transform. A black-box model is developed to identify frequency responses between a GIS and a UHF sensor in a range of 1 Hz to 15 MHz frequency. An inverse black-box model is derived by taking inverse Fourier transform of the black-box model to estimate the original VFTO waveforms from the output of the UHF sensor. This inverse black-box model allows to calculate VFTO occurred at the main conductor of a GIS. Experimental results conducted in a laboratory-scaled 72.5 kV GIS mock-up show that the proposed method can reform the VFTO waveforms with below 5 % error rates.

articleTitle: Towards 3D electric field imaging using E-FISHG
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Electric field measurement using electric-field induced second-harmonic generation (E-FISHG) has attracted attention because of its non-invasiveness and high temporal/spatial resolution. For the electric field measurement by E-FISHG, it is necessary to consider that the electric field profile along the laser path affects the SHG signal. We have proposed a method of calibrating and restoring the electric field profile from SHG distributions along the laser pass. The successful restoration of a relatively simple electric field profile from a series of SHG signals has been demonstrated. To measure more complex electric field distributions, we apply our method to two cases of electric field profiles: (1) the profile with different sharpness and (2) the profile with noise superimposed on the SHG signal. It is found that the electric field distribution can be restored within a 10% error by adequately choosing the confocal parameter.

articleTitle: Application of principal component analysis for power transformer asset management
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Measurements from insulating liquid are utilised to indicate the health of power transformer insulation systems. Due to various dynamics within the transformers, assessing the transformer health through condition monitoring data and their risk profile require input from transformer experts. This paper investigates the application of Principal Component Analysis (PCA) as an automated tool in ranking transformers based on their condition monitoring data with minimum expert input. Oil test data obtained from a transformer fleet over a five-year span was used for the analysis. For each transformer, a single value for each measurement was obtained by using the 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> percentile data from the five-year measurement span. Furthermore, multiple imputation was applied for transformers with missing data. The rankings obtained from PCA was compared against the ranking developed based on expert knowledge. Results indicated that PCA has potential to identify transformers with poor health condition with minimum expert input.

articleTitle: Study on the motion characteristics of metal particles in GIS
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: GIL/GIS has become an important carrier for power transmission in China because of its excellent transmission performance. However, different types of particulate foreign matter will be generated during its production, transportation and installation and operation. The metal particles will move under the electric field when operating with electricity, which will produce damage to the insulation performance of GIL/GIS. In this paper, we studied the generation of particles in the air chamber of the circuit breaker during uncharged operation. After several mechanical operations, we found that the number of metal particles generated tended to be stable, and their shapes were linear, sheet and spherical particles. After that, the movement characteristics of each metal particle were studied. The movement of metal particles inside the GIS gas chamber includes three processes: metal particle initiation, metal particles moving violently and gradually to the low field strength area, and triggering the violent flashover phenomenon. This experiment summarizes the influencing factors of metal particle motion in GIS gas chamber, including: particle type, material thickness, and air pressure. The kinematic characteristics of metal particle motion under different initial influencing factors are studied to quantitatively analyze the law between the generation of flashover and different initial conditions.

articleTitle: Partial discharge under pulse voltages with different frequencies and rise times
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Cables play a critical role in the normal operation of the electrical system as an energy transmission channel. However, the increasing load demand and higher power density of the system raise the voltage level of the cables, leading to a higher probability of partial discharge (PD). At present, there is a considerable body of research on PD under pulse voltage . However, few studies have investigated the changing characteristic of PD using simulation methods. This paper presents a study of the partial discharge characteristics of cables under pulse voltages of different rise times and frequencies using simulation. Firstly, a physical model of the cable is built using finite element software, and the partial discharge phenomenon is simulated using numerical co-simulation. Based on the simulation results, the trend of PD caused by the change of these two parameters is studied. Subsequently, an actual experiment platform was established to verify the accuracy of the simulation results. The findings indicate that the increasement in rise time significantly reduces the amplitude and discharge times of the PD model and weakens the discharge intensity, and the frequency has an "inflection point" effect on partial discharge, wherein the effect first strengthens and then inhibits PD.

articleTitle: Analytical sound pressure level determination around a transformer using measured vibration velocity distribution
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Tank surface vibration is radiated as noise to the surrounding medium, depending on the radiation efficiency of the tank wall material and the medium acoustic properties. In this paper, a one-third-octave spectrum of sound pressure level (SPL) is calculated analytically. The calculation is done at the chosen points around the transformer using the measured vibration velocity distribution at the tank surface for short-circuit (SC) test. The measured object is the 5 MVA transformer experimental model. The tank wall is treated as an incoherent radiator in the calculation method used for this problem. Incoherent sounds have random relative phases, which sum as scalar quantities on an energy basis. Each surface of the transformer tank is treated as a separate plane source so the analytical calculation can be applied. The summation of contributions at the calculation point is done only for the surfaces for which that point is in front, i.e., from 0° to 180°. The SPL around the transformer for SC operating condition is measured in the semi-anechoic chamber. Those measurements are compared with analytically determined SPL.

articleTitle: Measurement and evaluation of partial discharges at higher-frequency sinusoidal and impulse test voltages
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In this work, four instruments are investigated and compared concerning the measurement of partial discharges under high-frequency sinusoidal and impulse test voltages in a laboratory environment. The chosen instruments, typically employed for detecting partial discharges under voltages with high dV/dt-ratios, are a high-frequency current transformer, a D-dot probe, a detection capacitor connected in series to the test object, and a photomultiplier. Initially, the sensitivity of the instruments is assessed for discharges taking place over a single period of a sinusoidal test voltage (1 kHz) and during a positive, unipolar, slow-rise impulse. Next, individual instrument signals in response to either a single weak (units of pC) or a moderate (hundreds of pC) partial discharge are analysed in detail, and the suitability of the instruments for the construction of a phase-resolved partial discharge pattern is evaluated (sine, 10 kHz). Ultimately, the performance of the instruments for steep-flank (∼375 kV/μs) impulse test voltages is studied. Analog filters are employed to improve the instruments' detection capabilities, and an overview of the instruments' strengths and weaknesses is presented. The detection series capacitor instrument is shown to have the best overall performance for the studied aspects of partial discharge measurement.

articleTitle: Multispectral characteristics analysis of partial discharge in transformer oil
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In order to obtain more abundant discharge characteristic information and improve the efficiency of partial discharge diagnosis, a deep learning fusion method for partial discharge in transformer oil with multispectral information is proposed. Firstly, based on the miniature optical sensor devices and the spectral distribution of partial discharges, a multispectral synchronous detection platform for partial discharges is constructed, and multispectral data of four discharge types are obtained through experiments. Then a convolutional neural network model is constructed, and the partial discharge data of different spectral bands are used as inputs to different channels of the model, and the effective information in the multispectral signals is extracted using channel-level fusion to accurately identify the types of partial discharges of oil-paper insulation. The results show that the multispectral information of different discharge types can be used as effective features for pattern recognition. With the help of multispectral information, the recognition accuracy of the proposed method can reach over 98%. Compared with the statistical feature parameter analysis method and deep neural network, the proposed method is more effective in the fusion of multispectral information and the recognition accuracy is higher.

articleTitle: Applying deconvolution methods in high voltage measurements
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The convolution method is recommended by standards for high voltage testing techniques to evaluate the dynamic performance of impulse voltage measuring systems. This method uses the impulse response of the measuring system to calculate output waveforms from known input impulses. The convolution method should not be used for direct correction of measured waveforms, since the actual input waveform is unknown and only provides the output for an assumed input. In high voltage measurements it is more advantageous to find the unknown input waveform, on the high voltage (hv) side, from the measured low voltage signal, and this method is often called deconvolution. Convolution and deconvolution methods require previous knowledge of the impulse response of the measuring system, which can be obtained from the unit step response, acquired applying low voltage steps to the measuring system. Due to the high ratio of dividers, recording instruments use different gains to measure hv impulses and step response. Noise from measured signals and difference in instruments could affect the implementation of deconvolution techniques. In order to achieve proper impulse reconstruction the measured step response and hv signals should be matched numerically before applying the deconvolution. This contribution proposes some recipes for the practical implementation of the deconvolution on lightning impulse measurements.

articleTitle: Streamer inception in technical air with and without C5-fluoroketone for a rod-plane gap
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In this study, the inception probability of negative streamers in technical air with 7.5 %vol C5-fluoroketone (C5-FK+air) at 1.0 bar absolute pressure is studied. Similar tests were done for both polarities in technical air (80% N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, 20% O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) for comparison with the C5-FK+air results and to investigate polarity dependencies in air. The streamers emerged from a grounded needle electrode placed 48 mm below a planar electrode. The electrode setup was stressed by a fast rise time impulse voltage. The streamers in air showed a significant polarity dependence, with substantially higher voltages required for negative streamer inception. This is speculated to be due to either differences in source of first electron or the critical volume, or both. The negative streamers in C5-FK+air required a stronger field than both polarities in air. This is believed to be due to C5-FK being more electronegative than pure air. Differences in critical volume and source of first electron might also contribute to this difference.

articleTitle: Electrostatic modelling of gas-filled voids and conductive particles in highly non-uniform electric fields
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The reliability of modern high voltage equipment strongly relies upon the prevention of partial (or complete) electrical discharges. Electric field enhancement, caused by defects and contaminants inside insulating materials, can play a major role in discharge initiation, potentially leading to the catastrophic failure of critical equipment. The problem is exacerbated when considering existing regions of nonuniform electric field, possibly caused by unintended metallic protrusions, surface roughness, and other high aspect-ratio features. In this work, gas-filled voids and conductive particles of spheroidal geometry were investigated under highly nonuniform field conditions. By employing an analytical methodology, the electric field distribution has been modelled around a spheroidal dielectric inclusion, subjected to a nonuniform electric field, and generated with a needle-plane electrode system. A systematic study was conducted to investigate the effects of inclusion type (gas-void or conductive particle); inclusion proximity to the HV electrode; inclusion radius; inclusion eccentricity; and needle curvature, on the enhancement factor of the redistributed field inside and outside of the inclusion. The results arising from this work further advances the understanding of insulation defects and contaminants near complex geometrical features, aiding the future development of high voltage power and pulsed power systems.

articleTitle: Temperature rise in conductivity graded materials (σ-FGM) spacer for HVDC GIS/GIL
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Functionally graded permittivity and conductivity materials (ɛ/σ-FGM) application is a novel method to improve electric field distribution around HVDC GIS/GIL spacer. Since there is interdependency between temperature and conductivity, in this paper, the relationship between conductivity and the semi-conductive SiC filler concentrations in epoxy-based ɛ/σ-FGM spacer is clarified, and the effect of SiC filler concentrations to the leakage current (ILC), maximum temperature (Tmax), as well as maximum conductivity (σmax) are investigated through electric field and thermal simulation. The simulation results revealed that Tmax started to exceed the temperature of HV conductor when σmax exceeds 4×10-9 S/m and ILC is of a few hundreds of nA. Since this criterion corresponds to 21 vol% SiC-filled epoxy composite in σ-FGM, 5–10 vol% SiC-filled epoxy composite in the specified U-type σ-FGM spacer has low enough conductivity not to cause temperature rise.

articleTitle: Measurement of partial discharge of power cables using oscillatory wave test system
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Oscillating Wave Test System - OWTS using damped AC Voltages (DAC) is an alternative test method for continuous AC voltage testing for partial discharge measurement of power cables at field. It is a method which is used to analyse the healthiness of the insulation of capacitive test object. Damped AC voltages (DAC) is an effective and portable method to detect PD and assess the condition of insulation for on-site medium voltage XLPE cables of very long length of high capacitance. The input power requirement of OWTS test system is low compared to conventional power frequency PD measurement system. IEEE 400 and IEEE 400.4 standards recommend partial discharge measurement by continuous or damped AC voltages (DAC). In this paper, the OWTS system with PD detection are simulated using the SIMULINK tool box of MATLAB and PSCAD. Defective medium voltage XLPE cable is also simulated in both MATLAB and PSCAD. The simulated circuits of OWTS, defective XLPE Cable and the PD Detection circuit are all integrated as a one circuit and the partial discharge characteristics of the XLPE cable are compared with both SIMULINK and PSCAD software platforms. The partial discharge measurement with 50 Hz voltage was also simulated in both the platforms. The partial discharge measurement for various dimensions of void sizes and various rating of power cables are compared with 50 Hz and Oscillatory test voltage frequency in the simulation environment of SIMULINK and PSCAD.

articleTitle: Simulation and measurement of long-term polarization processes on PET films in a DC stressed bushing
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The increasing importance of high voltage DC transmissions requires to investigate the DC behaviour of the used materials. For plastics, long-term polarization processes are observed under DC stress, which may last several weeks. This leads to the question of suitable tests or simulation scenarios to take these processes into account with sufficient accuracy. In this paper it is presented how FEM simulations can be adapted to consider long-term polarization processes. Temperature and field strength dependencies on polarization and DC conductivity is considered and discussed. The simulations can be performed for DC and any other voltage waveforms such as polarity reversals. The influence of stationary or dynamic temperature gradients can also be considered. The given material parameters of the plastic films are verified with measurements on an experimental setup. To get sufficient results, side effects like surface conductivity and parasitic capacities are considered. The results of the simulation program are compared with potential distribution measurements on an indoor 170 kV bushing with defined temperature gradient and an outdoor 660 kV bushing. It is evaluated and discussed in context of engineering aspects.

articleTitle: I-V characteristics of short sphere-plane air gaps: modelling using an ATPDraw object
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Corona inception and growth characteristics of short sphere-plane air gaps under positive ramp high voltages with variable rate of rise are experimentally investigated. I-V characteristics were obtained through continuous monitoring and measurement of the applied voltage and discharge current. Corona initiates in the form of streamer discharge whereas at slightly higher applied voltage a stable glow is established in the gap. The inception voltage of the various corona modes is experimentally determined using several processing methods. The associated corona inception field is theoretically estimated based on electrostatic field simulations and physical modelling of the glow and streamer discharge; reasonable agreement between experimentally determined and theoretically predicted values is shown to exist. With the aid of an empirical formula accounting for the effects of applied voltage and gap length on discharge current, I-V characteristics are dynamically modelled in ATP-EMTP by developing an ATPDraw object. Using the latter, simulated I-V characteristics of bundled conductors are in excellent agreement with measurements from literature.

articleTitle: Backflashover rate estimation for a 66 kV overhead line considering lightning strikes along the span
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This work aims at estimating the backflashover rate (BFR) of a 66 kV single-circuit overhead line (OHL) by considering the distribution of lightning strikes to the shield wires along its span. For that purpose, a stochastic lightning attachment model based on the theory of fractal structures is employed to compute the shield wire interception radius, as well as the distribution of lightning strikes along the shield wire span. An electromagnetic transient (EMT) model in ATP-EMTP is also used, representing accurately the lightning impulse behaviour of overhead line components, to compute the minimum backflashover current for several span segments of the OHL. The results of the two models are combined for estimating the BFR of the 66 kV OHL; a discussion is made with respect to the BFR expression suggested by CIGRE. Based on the proposed stochastic approach, simplifications of the CIGRE expression regarding BFR estimation for OHLs, which omits the lightning strikes spatial distribution along the span, could be overcome.

articleTitle: Effect of pore structure on nanosecond pulsed surface dielectric barrier discharges at atmospheric pressure
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Plasma generated by nanosecond pulsed surface dielectric barrier discharge (SDBD) at atmospheric pressure has been shown to provide a promising alternative treatment for biomedicine, such as wound healing, antiphlogistic and bactericidal.
