However, compared with conventional high-voltage AC excitation, SDBD under nanosecond pulse excitation has higher ignition voltage, poorer discharge stability, and unclear discharge mechanism. In this study, porous electrodes are designed to solve these problems. The effects of pore shape on discharge electrical characteristics, luminescence intensity, uniformity, and plasma temperature were investigated. In addition, the influence of the above parameters on the electric field distribution was studied by using the numerical simulation. The results show that pore structure is the key to generate low temperature, high energy density, stable and controllable plasma in nanosecond pulse SDBD instantaneously. However, compared with hexagon and square pores, circular pores are more likely to produce uniform and stronger discharge plasma.

articleTitle: Development and practical realization of 154kV direct-molded bushing using ZnO electric-field-relaxation layer
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: We have developed and put a 154 kV direct-molded bushing and an outdoor termination for cables by applying a ZnO electric-field-relaxation layer into practical use. The direct-molded bushing is a completely solid-insulation type using epoxy resin for the main insulation and covered with a silicone rubber outer coating, and we commercialized it in 2004 as 66/77 kV-class products. This is lightweight, compact, and has excellent earthquake resistance. 154 kV-class bushings have a higher surface electric field under high voltages such as equipment withstand voltages, so normally it is necessary to increase the overall length and outer diameter of the bushing and to decrease the surface electric field. In contrast, we focused on the non-linear characteristic of ZnO, and by placing the ZnO/epoxy resin composite at the lower part of the direct-molded bushing, we were able to reduce the length of the in-air bushing by about 30 % compared to a conventional bushing using porcelain hollow insulators. By appropriately controlling the operation start electric field of the ZnO layer of this developed product, the electric field at the lower part of the bushing was averaged, and the AC withstand voltage performance was also successfully improved by approximately 35 %.

articleTitle: Determination of protective measures against atmospheric discharges in the vicinity of underground medium-voltage cables
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper identifies and describes the damages to underground power cables and cable sheaths caused by atmospheric discharges in their vicinity. Based on field experience the process of damage formation and the impact on this process of different geological and atmospheric conditions is given. It outlines the correlation between the distance of the affected cable and the lightning strike as well other electrical, chemical and mechanical elements which deteriorate the cable dielectric strength to avoid electrical breakdown of the cable. An analysis has been drawn up of lightning flash density along the underground power cable corridor, the electrical current parameters and the degree of exposure of underground power cables, using the lightning location system SCALAR. The influence of nearby buildings and protective elements during a lightning strike on the distribution of the electric potential near the underground power cable is also presented. The risk assessment regarding the importance of part of the electrical network is discussed, as well as the aspect of repetitions and the size of the amplitude of the lightning current. Finally, protective measures against lightning strike are analysed and recommendations are given for additional underground power cables protection in areas with high lightning flash density.

articleTitle: Electric field relaxation by FGM on permittivity to three-core type GIS spacer
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: For the relaxation of electric field (E-field) stress around Gas Insulated Switchgears (GIS) spacer, we have proved the effectiveness of an application of spacer with functionally graded materials (FGM) with a spatial distribution of permittivity ε (ε-FGM). However, we have investigated the effectiveness of the FGM spacer only in the case of single-core type GIS, so far. For wider application of the FGM spacer, it is needed to investigate its effectiveness not only in single-core type but also in three-core type GIS. For this purpose, in this paper, we carried out the three-dimensional electric field analysis for three-core type GIS, in order to investigate the E-field relaxation effect by an application of ε-FGM spacer. Firstly as fundamental investigations, we consider a simplified model for a three-core type FGM spacer. The cone-type spacer model for the three-core type GIS is used. We added ε distribution into the internal part of the spacer. Then we calculate E-field stress in and around three-core type GIS spacer for various ε distributions inside the spacer. Finally, we quantified relaxation effect of the maximum E-field stress.

articleTitle: Towards the on-line diagnostics of cable joints
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Cable joints are one of the most critical parts of power distribution systems as they influence to a great extent the reliability of the power network. In this work, we introduce a diagnostic system that, through the measurement of partial discharges (PDs), can help to predict their aging. The system can identify whether a signal has been triggered by a PD source inside or outside the joint. In the former case, it is possible to localize the PDs source (possibly a Treeing) with sub-millimetre precision and to trace its evolution over time. The algorithm also provides, for each PD event, an evaluation of the real discharge intensity. In this work, we briefly introduce this novel technique and test its performances in a technically relevant case.

articleTitle: Stress grading system design criteria in aerospace electrical systems
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: As the aviation industry is heading to partially or fully electric systems to reduce their carbon emissions in line with the need to combat climate change, higher voltages are increasingly used in aerospace electrical systems. In response to this, some companies have started to market screened cables similar to the types commonly used in terrestrial power systems. However, there are no clear guidelines for the design of the stress grading systems in an aerospace environment. In ground-based systems, it is common to design a stress grading system in a way that limits the maximum longitudinal electrical field to a value in the order of 0.45kV/mm. Results from authors who have investigated how the stability field of a streamer varies as a function of temperature and pressure is used in this paper along with an FEA model of a screened aerospace cable. The paper demonstrates the limitation in operating voltage that may result from the operation of screened cable systems in aerospace applications.

articleTitle: Measurement of space charge accumulation in motor winding insulator under rectangular voltage simulating PWM control
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In this report, the space charge distribution that accumulates inside the materials when a square-wave voltage is applied to polyamide-imide (PAI) and Polyimide (PI) films at elevated temperatures was measured using the pulsed electro-acoustic (PEA) method. The PI and the PAI used as insulating materials in power devices and motor windings are subjected to square wave voltage at high temperatures. If space charge accumulates in the insulating materials due to this voltage application, it may cause partial discharge or enhance the dielectric breakdown generation, so it is necessary to measure the space charge distribution that accumulates in the insulating materials when square wave voltage is applied at high temperatures. However, until now, there have been no examples of measurements of space charge distribution in insulating materials at high temperatures such as 150°C, where square wave voltage is applied to insulating materials. Therefore, in this report, we attempted to measure space charge distribution by applying unipolar and bipolar square wave voltages of 500 Hz at 150°C to PI and PAI samples. As a result, although space charge does not accumulate when unipolar and bipolar square wave voltages are applied to PI at 150°C, space charge does accumulate when unipolar square wave voltages are applied to PAI. This result suggests that unexpected partial discharge or dielectric breakdown may occur in power devices and motor windings using the PAI due to space charge accumulation when square wave voltage is applied at high temperatures.

articleTitle: Artificial intelligence applied to PRPD patterns classification using UHF printed monopole antenna and envelope detector
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This work proposes the generation and classification of PRPD patterns through partial discharges signals detected using UHF printed monopole antenna (PMA) connected to an envelope detector to reduce the system sampling rate. The PRPD patterns were classified by means of a Multilayer Perceptron with 5 hidden-layers. From the apparatus mentioned above, three typical classes of partial discharges were evaluated: internal, superficial and corona with five test objects. To evidence the pulses of these discharges, threshold signal filtering algorithm was evaluated. The proposed methodology presents potential for PD monitoring of electrical equipment in practice, since it was verified that there is separability among the patterns obtained in this study from the use of UHF PMA with envelope detector for all test objects evaluated with average accuracy of 88%.

articleTitle: Development of optical voltage transformer using electro-optic Pockels effect for HVDC transmission systems
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: A new conceptual optical DC voltage transformer (VT) for HVDC transmission systems is proposed. Although it has been shown that relatively low DC voltage can be directly measured using the electro-optic Pockels effect with a longitudinal modulation arrangement, the maximum measurable voltage is generally limited by the Pockels crystal-specific half-wavelength voltage, e.g., tens of kV. In this research, two Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>Ge<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> (BGO) crystals with slightly different half-wavelength voltages each other are combined and installed in the DCVT tank to expand the theoretical maximum measurable voltage to the target value of the HVDC transmission system. The dielectric strength along the creepage of the BGO crystals is improved with pressurized SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas with 0.4 MPa-g. Furthermore, a Faraday rotator and an optical modulation technique are utilized to remove the influence of optical noises and to achieve the long-term stability of the voltage measurement. Finally, a prototype of the DCVT with the rated voltage of DC 250 kV is fabricated. Then, it is experimentally confirmed that the accuracy of voltage measurement meets the requirement of IEC 61869-15, class 1, and it has adequate electrical insulating performances toward DC, AC, lightning and switching impulse voltages.

articleTitle: Effect of electric field on conductivity of synthetic ester
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Synthetic ester has emerged as an environmentally friendly alternative to mineral oil for power transformers and is being considered as a potential replacement for mineral oil in HVDC converter transformers. However, the conductivity of insulation is a crucial parameter in the design of HVDC transformers, and there has been little research on the conductivity of esters compared to mineral oil. This paper investigates the impact of electric field on the conductivity of a synthetic ester. The results indicate that the conductivity of the synthetic ester was generally higher than that of conventional mineral oil. A positive correlation was observed between short-term conductivity and the electric field, while long-term conductivity exhibited a non-linear trend. The increase in short-term conductivity with the increase in electric field was found to be primarily due to the field-enhanced charge dissociation.

articleTitle: Analysis of loss tangent in current transformers using the finite element method
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Failures in Current Transformers (CTs) can have a significant financial impact on utilities, causing revenue loss, service interruptions, and even damage to nearby equipment. To minimize the effects of CT degradation on the electrical system, predictive techniques and continuous monitoring are essential. One such tool that can aid in the supervision and diagnosis of equipment in service is the loss tangent. This parameter is directly related to the aging and degradation of electrical insulation, making it a useful indicator of possible failures in CTs. Therefore, this work aims to perform computer simulations using the finite element method (FEM) to simulate the effect of oil and paper degradation on the loss tangent values of a 230 kV current transformer. To achieve this, the COMSOL Multiphysics® software was used to verify the loss tangent as a function of the conductivity of parameters correlated to the CT dielectric. The results of the simulations show that the degradation of oil and paper substantially increases the value of the loss tangent. Additionally, it was found that the simultaneous or individual degradation of oil and paper have different effects on the loss tangent values obtained. The findings of this study demonstrate the usefulness of loss tangent as a tool for the diagnosis and supervision of electrical equipment in service.

articleTitle: Investigation of electric field distribution on polymeric bushing using non-linear field grading materials
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This study investigated nonlinear resistive field grading material based on a ZnO microvaristor to optimize the distribution of the electric field along with a 36 kV composite bushing surface. In this work, we consider some parameters that influence nonlinear resistive field grading material properties such as different shapes of microvaristor layer design, switching parameters of field grading material including initial conductivity, non-linearity coefficient, and field switching threshold on the field distribution. A suitable design of field grading material has been proposed for effective stress control near the flange ground terminal. A polymeric bushing with field grading material has been proposed to evaluate some parameters using 2D axisymmetric models in COMSOL Multiphysics. Electric field enhancements at the triple junction points near the flange ground terminal are successfully suppressed. This consequently reduces the probability of corona and electric surface discharges, minimizes the possibility of dry bands formation, raises the flashover voltage, and may improve the long-term operation of the polymeric bushing in service.

articleTitle: Investigating the possibility of arc detection in power transformers
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Arc is known as one of the most dangerous faults in transformers and quickly increases pressure inside the transformer tank. In some cases, the usual protection systems do not operate fast enough, thus the arc can cause serious damage to the transformer tank as well as explosion. Therefore, fast and reliable arc detection can prevent life-threatening hazards and financial losses. In this paper, the arc detection with different semiconductors is explained and investigated. An arc emits electromagnetic waves into the environment in the form of visible and ultraviolet (UV) light. Moreover, an arc is accompanied by electromagnetic interference (EMI), which causes a significant electrostatic effect on its adjacent electric circuits. Both phenomena have to be considered in order to develop a reliable arc detection system. Based on the investigation of different semiconductor sensors a new method is proposed to detect arcs. This method is investigated within different liquids with different ageing conditions, thus the colors of the insulating liquids change from white transparent to dark brown in order to verify if the new method is able to detect arcs in different environments. Results demonstrated that by using the presented new method, the arc signal is recognizable from within the oil at different distances. Furthermore, the applied mechanism is caused to eliminate the magnetic interferences as a noise factor. Based on the results, the method which is introduced has the potential for a reliable and sustainable arc detection.

articleTitle: Novel testing method on insulation materials used for e-mobility
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The upheaval in industry and in the private sector towards electrification and mobilisation is associated with the increasing use of electric motors, for example in cars, bicycles, robots, wheelchairs and also in the aircraft industry. In order to meet the increasing demand and the requirements, further development of the production technology for e-motors is required. This development includes the quality and service life, especially of the winding insulation.This study presents a novel testing method for insulation materials used for e-mobility. In this regard, twisted enamelled wires are prepared. The partial discharge inception voltage and breakdown voltage were measured for this samples inside a water bath as a novel but simple measurement method. The investigations were performed for three differently insulated enamelled wires. Therefore, the aim of this paper is to determine the electrical properties of magnet wire after different ageing times and to evaluate them with regard to a possible use as winding insulation in electric motors. Furthermore the advantages and disadvantages of the new test method are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: A flexible pulsed current source to characterise future switching technologies
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: To support research of high-current switching devices, suitable laboratory equipment is required. Today, new technologies such as switches for DC grids or with alternative switching gases are requested, and testing with other than sinusoidal current shapes would be of great help. Until now, no usable high-power current source is available that provides the needed versatility with respect to envisaged current shapes. To address the need of a new laboratory facility to characterise emerging technologies and plasma physical behaviours, ETH Zurich undertook the development of a flexible pulsed current source to supply arbitrarily shaped high-current pulses. The topology of the device is based on a prior source. However, the significantly increased demand on current, voltage levels and regulation dynamics originated a completely new development. The source has a system voltage of 10 kV and can output up to 24 kA nominal. It is achieved by a parallel arrangement of eight individually controlled buck converters (IGBT) and switchable energy-absorbing devices (MOV). This source can ramp up to the nominal current and down to zero within less than half a millisecond while maintaining an output current over several tens of milliseconds. This contribution presents the design of the source and its control, its realisation, and example measurements.

articleTitle: Charge simulation method and surface charge computation for design of high voltage devices
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the charge simulation method (CSM) developments which started at the Technical University of Munich in the 1960s and continue until today. The CSM features and the corresponding formulations created during three major development phases are summarised. Altogether, eight types of equations used in the latest CSM-implementation are presented. The newest surface charging simulation procedure, which is one focus of this paper, has been illustrated by two examples of devices belonging to the medium voltage range: a triple point test arrangement and a silicon coated vacuum interrupter. A comparison of results between computations and a dedicated AC test enabled generalisation of the procedure for simulation of triple points. An evaluation of the extremal saturation charge on the silicon coating has shown its impact on LI-withstand and has indicated possible improvements of the insulation shape. The differences between the 2D CSM results and the results obtained using a 3D Boundary Element Method implementation are discussed.

articleTitle: Influence of core lamination pressure on vibration of shunt reactors
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Shunt reactors are one of the main apparatuses used in power systems to compensate the capacitive current resulting from the increasing demand of HV cable. Reducing their vibration and noise emission will lessen their environmental impact. In this study, the effects of different core lamination pressures on the vibration characteristics of shunt reactors were investigated experimental and analytically. Experimental modal analysis (EMA) and finite element analysis (FEA) were performed on a scaled-down yoke model to validate non-linear contact behaviour of the laminations. Modal and harmonic analysis supported by the results from EMA were used to investigate the influence of core lamination pressure on vibration velocity. These indicate that core lamination pressure is one of the key factors in characterising shunt reactor active part vibration and consequently can be used as an effective means to reduce vibration and noise emission.

articleTitle: Performance of aligned earth rods under low-magnitude variable-frequency current
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper analyses the behaviour of earthing systems under low and high frequency ranges, aiming to provide effective design and mitigating risk associated with fault current inducted potentials. A parametric analysis is carried out to study the behaviour of two interconnected earth rods under different conditions by varying the length of rods, separation distance, soil resistivity and frequency of the injected current. For long separation distances, the effect of current injection point is studied where above- and under-ground insulating conductors are selected and compared to the case of and bare conductors. Simulations using HIFREQ module of CDEGS are conducted where earthing impedance over frequency is considered as a prime parameter. The results are grouped into several sections in order to provide a clear image on the effect of aforementioned parameters.

articleTitle: Spatial-temporal dynamic characteristics of growth and evolution of micron-nanometre dust-speckles along insulator interface in GIL
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In the process of production, installation, and operation of GIS/GIL equipment, it is inevitable to produce micron-nanometre dust. However, in the GIL cavity, micron-nanometre dust is easily adsorbed on the insulator surface due to the coupling effect of multiple physical fields, significantly reducing the insulation performance. Therefore, the adsorption characteristics of micron-nanometre dust on insulator surface are studied and a dynamic adsorption observation platform for micron-nanometre dust is set up. It is found that the dynamic growth behaviour of micron-nanometre dust in SF6 environment includes the following five processes: the micron-nano dust is lifted under the action of voltage and diffused and adsorbed on the insulator, indicating that dust speckles are formed on the insulator surface; the thickness of micron-nanometre dust speckles increases and forms obvious contours; the micron-nanometre dust violently "explodes" to form wing-shaped diffusion marks, and the dust speckles end up growing; severe surface flashover or strong partial discharge (non-breakdown) of dust speckles lead to the ignition of dust speckles; the position of the dust speckles left obvious discharge path and ablation trace, and the dust speckles was destroyed. The experimental research and theoretical analysis in this article can provide a significant basis for further research.

articleTitle: Inception, a software for partial discharge simulation
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Numerical simulation has played a key role for modelling partial discharges (PDs). In recent years, semi-empirical approaches have been supplemented by more complex methods based on plasma physics and the solution of a set of partial differential equations (PDEs). In this work we describe a model based on the latter approach: it describes the drift and diffusion of charged species by means of the electric field. This field is influenced by both an external potential, produced by the voltage applied to a set of electrodes, and by the concentration of charged particles. Several test cases have been considered to evaluate the performances of this approach and to test its accuracy.

articleTitle: Hydrophobicity classification of RTV silicone rubber-coated insulators using deep learning algorithms
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Outdoor polymeric insulators based on silicone rubber are widely used in power transmission and distribution networks. They exhibit several advantages like light weight, vandalism resistance and superior pollution performance due to their hydrophobic surface property. However, silicone rubber insulators suffer from aging that will lead to the loss of their hydrophobicity property. Various methods have been used to classify the hydrophobicity of the insulator surface including static and dynamic contact angle measurement and hydrophobicity class as per the IEC 62073 standard. The main goal of this paper is to use deep learning techniques to automatically assess the hydrophobicity classes (as per the IEC 62073 standards) of non-ceramic insulators under various conditions. A dataset of the hydrophobicity classes (HC1-HC6) was created including 4197 images each having 224×224 pixels size to train the proposed model. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Transfer Learning (TL) were used in this study to categorize and evaluate the hydrophobicity classes of ceramic insulators coated with room-temperature vulcanized silicone rubber. Compared to other CNN pre-trained models, the MobileNet model was found to have the highest accuracy and the lowest training time under several conditions, with maximum classification accuracy of 97.8%.

articleTitle: A modular universal divider for calibration of UHVDC, and composite waves up to 1400 kV
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: With the development of new high voltage cables and switching elements for continuously higher system voltages, especially for HVDC operation, the need for new reference measuring systems for on-site calibration to support activities in type and routine testing. Traceability in testing the fundamental voltage stress, high voltage DC or AC, is superimposed with a Switching or Lightning Impulses has up to now been lacking. This paper describes the design of a new universal RCR divider developed at RISE for a reference measurement system for traceability of ultra-high voltage (UHV) composite and combined waves. In composite/combined wave measurements the RCR divider is rated 500, 330, 600 and 700 kV for DC, AC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rms</sub>, Switching Impulse (SI) and Lightning Impulse (LI) respectively. For UHVDC measurements the extended measurement uncertainty is better than 40 μV/V. In a composite/combined wave measurement, the extended measurement uncertainties for the divider are better than 150 and 400 μV/V for DC and AC and 0.5% for peak voltage of SI and LI. Two voltage dividers have been built for the purpose to measure both composite and combined waves. This divider is modular, where the HV arms can be stacked to 1000, 660, 1200 and 1400 kV and beyond.

articleTitle: Electrical performance of 400-kV Cap-Pin and composite string insulators. COMSOL multiphysics simulations
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The paper deals with the electrical characterization of clean 400 kV insulator models using computer-based simulations. These simulations offer the flexibility to obtain complete information about the current waveforms and their dissipation within the systems (air and material). For this purpose, Cap-Pin and composite string insulators are considered using 2D-axisymmetric profiles in COMSOL Multiphysics. Electric field and potential distributions are presented and analysed along the leakage path and at the central axis of both insulators. Density streamlines and waveforms of the leakage current are computed, and the components of the leakage current passing through the material and air are discussed. It was found that the leakage current intensity is higher through the air compared to the insulator material, with a higher ratio in Cap-Pin than in the composite insulator. This achievement contributes to a better understanding of the insulating materials used in 400 kV transmission systems.

articleTitle: Improved energy storage of polyurea / PCBM composites with excellent discharge efficiency
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Polymer dielectrics have been widely used in capacitors due to their excellent advantages such as high breakdown strength, ease of film forming and low cost. However, they still suffer from low energy density and poor discharge efficiency at high temperatures, which limits their use in extreme conditions. In this work, the PCBM/polyurea composites has been constructed to improve the energy storage performance at high temperatures. Due to the high electron affinities of PCBM, the charge transportation has been significantly hindered and the conduction current has been greatly suppressed. At 150 °C, the maximum Ue with η above 90% of the PCBM/polyurea composites remains as high as 6.1 J cm−3, which is 3.5 times that of pristine PU and superior to most of the current dielectric polymers and composites.

articleTitle: PRPD analysis in current transformers using UHF sensors and signal conditioning system
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The detection and interpretation of partial discharges (PD) is a robust tool that can be used for monitoring and risk assessment of insulation failures in high voltage equipment. The radiometric method stands out among the methods of monitoring PD activity due to its stability, non-invasive nature, and robustness against common interference in substations. Thus, it is used for detection, classification, and location of defects. Regarding the PD classification, one of the most used techniques for the interpretation of types of partial discharges, based on the patterns obtained, is the Phase–Resolved Partial Discharge (PRPD) analysis. A difficulty for the implementation of PRPD analysis of PD signals detected with the radiometric method stems from the need for a high sampling rate and high memory requirements of the acquisition system to obtain the necessary precision for PRPD. Therefore, in this paper PD measurements were performed on current transformers using a signal conditioning system based on the envelope detection for analog smoothing of the signal obtained from the UHF sensor. From the results, it was possible to detect that when using the signal conditioning system and the PRPD analysis could be performed with greater reliability.

articleTitle: Application of artificial inteligence for the diagnosis of deffects in surge arresters using thermal images
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Non-invasive diagnosis techniques for electrical equipment are essential as they enable field monitoring, eliminating the need to remove equipment from the power system. Thus, it becomes possible to detect defects while the equipment is operational. Thermovision has emerged as a promising tool for identifying defects as most of them exhibit thermal abnormalities. However, these abnormalities are often noticeable only when the equipment is on the brink of failure. This paper proposes the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques to analyse thermal images and identify defects, thus mitigating the risk of equipment failure. The study was conducted on a ZnO surge arrester. Several AI techniques were employed to find a suitable classifier for thermographic images. The images used for training and testing the classifiers were obtained from the High Voltage Laboratory of the Federal University of Campina Grande. The results of this study found that Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) are effective classifiers for analysing thermographic images.

articleTitle: Breakdown strength and dielectric properties of stereolithography 3D-printed dielectrics for high voltage applications
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Additive 3D printing processes have already been successfully introduced in many industrial sectors. For use in energy technologies it is necessary to examine the electrical and dielectric properties of materials. The breakdown strength provides information about the insulation capacity of a material and opens up the fundamental design of equipment. In addition, the relative permittivity and the dissipation factor are also key criteria to design an electrical insulating system. Material samples with x-y-dimensions of 80 x 80 mm and various thicknesses from 0.3 to 1.0 mm were produced with the stereolithography printer Form 3L from Formlabs using the epoxy resin materials Standard Clear V4 (SCV4) and Rigid 4000 (R4K). The breakdown strength of the materials with the thinnest thickness of 0.3 mm is in the range of 40 to 50 kV/mm. At 1 mm, the strength of both materials is only between 20 and 30 kV/mm. The results of the permittivity measurements of both materials show a continuous increase over the frequency from εr ≈ 3.5 at 5 kHz to εr ≈ 9 at 0.1 µHz. The course of the dissipation factor starting around 2% and increasing with decreasing frequency to about 20%.

articleTitle: The design of high-voltage coaxial transmission lines pressurised with pure nitrogen for testing to IEC standards
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The environmental advantages of pure nitrogen as an insulant for metalclad power systems have remained unexploited. It has yet to be shown whether the stringent IEC standards for high pressure gas insulation can be met by nitrogen: it is clear that IEC 62271-203:2022 requires a breakdown voltage which is at least 25% higher than the withstand test voltage and is also 450% above the phase voltage. Nonetheless this paper shows that the limited available test data on large nitrogen coaxialsystems can provide a physical basis to design coaxial systems of optimised conductor/enclosure dimensional ratio (dO /DO = 0.368) that may satisfy IEC specifications for the withstand voltage. These designs use a feasible N2 pressure range of 0.5 — 0.8MPa at standard rated line voltages from 33kV to 400kV. Further test data on large systems are urgently needed.

articleTitle: Diagnostic of breakdown in high voltage bushing power transformer 500kV Cirata substation
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Power transformer is one of the critical things of the system transmission. Regular tests of the power transformer are very important to maintain the reliability of the power. One of the causes of failure of the transformer is the breakdown of insulation caused by the presence of voids in the equipment that is electrified. As a result of the voids that occur in this power transformer equipment, it can cause Partial Discharge. Several methods were used to determine the occurrence of damage to the power transformer equipment, such as Sweep Frequency Response Analysis (SFRA) and Tan Delta. In Inter Bus Transformer (IBT) 500/150 kV Cirata Extra High Voltage (EHV) Substation, a breakdown occurred in the T-phase tertiary bushing. From the lessons learned in this case, a complete electrical test was carried out. From the results of the complete electrical test, there was a suspicion of deterioration in the post-breakdown SFRA results. After overhaul and inspection, traces of voids were found on the tertiary bushing which indicated a breakdown in the tertiary bushing of the IBT 500/150kV Cirata Substation transformer.

articleTitle: Influence of surface charge accumulation on flashover voltages of cone-type insulating spacers in dry air
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper describes the effect of surface charge accumulation on the flashover voltage (FOV) of insulating spacers in dry air gas insulated switchgear (GIS). SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> is widely used in Gas Circuit Breaker (GCB), GIS, Gas Insulated Line (GIL), and so on, in order to fulfill high voltage insulation and current interruption performances. Since SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> has a high Global Warming Potential (GWP), which is 25,200 times higher than that of CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, dry air is going to be adopted as an insulation gas for GIS. In this experiment, we used 1/4 size mini model insulating spacers designed on a 245 kV class SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> GIS. The spacer surface on the concave side was positively or negatively charged by twenty times standard lightning impulse flashovers (±1.2/50 μs). After charges accumulation on the spacer surface, reverse polarity standard lightning impulse FOV was measured by the step-by-step voltage raising method. As the result, we confirmed that the positive 63.2% FOV was not influenced by negative charge accumulation on the spacer surface in 0.1 MPa-abs dry air. On the other hand, the negative 63.2% FOV was decreased by positive charge accumulation of the spacer surface in 0.1 MPa-abs dry air.

articleTitle: Impact of alternative dielectric liquids on temperature rise of station service voltage transformers
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Biodegradable dielectric liquids have been present in the power transformer world for a while. However, their implementation in instrument transformers has only recently gained momentum. The main insulation system and design principles of instrument transformers differ from that of their power transformer counterparts, which has an undeniable impact on the applicability of the existing experiences with implementation of biodegradable liquids. The aim of this paper is to present the impact of biodegradable liquids on thermal performance of instrument transformers. Specifically, this paper focuses on Station Service Voltage Transformers, which are similar to instrument transformers in terms of construction and manufacturing principles, while sharing the same function as power transformers. Since their primary use is energy transfer, they do exhibit more pronounced temperature rises in comparison to conventional instrument transformers, making them a more fitting candidate for this research. Two different liquid types are considered in comparison to conventional mineral oil; synthetic esters and bio-hydrocarbon based biodegradable oil. Two pairs of Station Service Voltage Transformers, with mutually different ratings are included in this work. Findings presented in this paper are one vital part of the qualification process for different biodegradable liquid solutions and technologies.

articleTitle: Complex process of evaluating safety of touch voltages for transmission line towers using ALARP method
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: For power line towers, electrical safety is generally associated with the grounding system and touch voltages of installed towers that are publicly accessible. The paper describes and discusses the entire process of safety assessments of transmission overhead line towers from the point of view of touch and step voltages, including measurements, fault simulations, database tools, and ALARP (‘as low as reasonably practicable’) evaluation. Grounding parameters change over time, which is associated with equipment aging, resulting in significant changes in the safety assessment of individual towers. Measuring the grounding of towers causes a considerable amount of needed service intervention, especially in extensive power transmission and distribution networks. The ALARP method can provide the prioritization for maintenance assessment and service works. The ALARP methodology is applied for high-voltage overhead line towers and is based on calculating the probability of human exposure to hazardous touch voltage. All discussed aspects were introduced into the Czech transmission system operator (CEPS) internal technical standards. The paper deals with a practical view of the complex safety assessment of grounding systems of power line towers and aims at conclusions from the use of ALARP methodology in practice.

articleTitle: High voltage design of additive manufactured dielectric test samples
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper shows a first design for additively manufactured gradient material that saves material without weakening the dielectric properties. The produced dielectric test samples are investigated for partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV), loss factor and permittivity with different filling degree ranges. The reduced filling degree saves material and printing time in non-critical areas. The cylinder insulators (CI) constructed using the fused filament fabrication (FFF) process consist of an insulation layer and two electrodes. The 1 mm thick insulation layer separates the two electrodes and is made of polylactic acid (PLA). The pluggable electrodes are printed from conductive electrostatic discharge (ESD) PLA. To prevent the emergence of partial discharges (PD), it is important to avoid creating a local high field stress in the reduced filling degree area. The separating insulation layer of the cylinder test specimen has a 100 % filling level. Insulating material discs are manufactured with both filling levels for loss factor and permittivity testing.

articleTitle: Gaseous by-products generated by bus-transfer current switching in dry air and their impacts
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Alternative gases to sulfur hexafluoride (SF6), especially natural-origin gases, are now demanded in electric power equipment to reduce the environmental impacts. Dry air insulation technologies have recently been studied for the application to gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) and vacuum interrupters as the surrounding insulation. When developing high-voltage equipment using alternative gases, the investigation of gaseous by-products generated by high power arcing is important to obtain a quantitative understanding of the physical and practical characteristics, and to evaluate the potential health risks. This paper studies the decomposed gases generated by electrical arcing during bus-transfer current switching tests, and evaluates their impacts on material compatibility of GIS component parts and on the health risks.

articleTitle: Lifetime of power transformers due to degradation of insulators supporting the winding
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In order to verify the failure behaviour of transformers due to degradation, short-circuit tests on core-type disc-winding transformers (3 types of winding structure) with an average DP of 200 to 450, which is the life level of insulation paper were conducted. The results revealed that transformer failures caused by damage to the insulation paper do not occur, but instead there are transformers that fail due to electromagnetic mechanical forces acting in the axial direction of the transformer windings (external thrust). The author recognized that there is a high possibility that the phenomenon of external thrust increasing was caused by shrinkage and changes in the stress-strain characteristics of the pressboard piled up along the height of the winding as it aged. Initially, the stress relaxation characteristics of a pressboard tightened at the default stress were investigated. To verify changes in pressboard characteristics in aged transformers, the state of tightening of windings was investigated. Moreover, It is shown that the Frequency Response Analysis (FRA) is expected to be applied as a means of externally detecting residual strain.

articleTitle: Remote measurement of salt deposit density on porcelain insulator using laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: We have developed a portable laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) system for the on-site diagnostics of the pollution of the porcelain insulators. The emission lines of Na I (819.48 nm) and Cl I (837.59 nm) were investigated as main elements and O I (777.19 nm), Ca II (854.21 nm), and K I (766.49 nm) were investigated as reference elements, called the internal standards to compensate the change of measurement conditions, for the calibration curve for the SDD measurement. For the measurement at a distance of 1.3 m, the emission intensity of Cl I (837.59 nm) increased linearly against SDD, ranging two orders of magnitude from 0.007 mg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 0.385 mg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a correlation coefficient of 0.96. The emission intensity ratios of Na/K and Cl/Ca optimally compensate for the difference in the trend of Na and Cl versus SDD with the difference in laser energies. For the remote LIBS measurement at a distance of 6 m, the emission intensity of K, used as an internal standard, compensated for the fluctuation of the emission intensities of Na versus SDD. These results suggest that remote measurement at a distance of up to 6 m is possible using the portable LIBS system.

articleTitle: Electrical evaluation of nanofiller-applied insulation materials for EHV cable
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Compared to overhead power transmission lines, underground power transmission lines have the effect of improving the reliability of electricity supply, urban disaster prevention, and urban aesthetic environment. For this reason, in recent years, in Korea, the social demand to replace the existing processed line with an underground line has increased. The voltage grade of the underground transmission line are HV and EHV. Among them, in the case of HV cables, the cable has been greatly thickness reduced. However, since the EHV cable was standardized in Korea in 2003, the insulation thickness of the underground cable has been maintained at 27mm. This paper will describe the results of electrical and thermal tests conducted on nanocomposites with magnesia nanofiller added to the insulating layer to develop a EHV power cable with an insulating thickness reduced. In addition, we would like to propose the most developable nanofiller content by cross-validation mechanical test results.

articleTitle: Integration of measurement data into probability assessment of high-voltage assets
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Knowing the failure probability of high-voltage assets becomes increasingly important. Measurement data gives an indication of the failure probability, which is manly based on threshold values for these measurements. Values below the threshold are not considered at all or by a warning range shortly before reaching the threshold value. The presented work introduces a methodology to quantify the failure probability depending on the difference between the measured and threshold value. Therefore, Bayes' theorem is used to assess the failure probability, while measurement data determines the conditional probability through a shift of the probability density function of the measured data. The methodology is exemplified by gas density measurements of circuit breakers.

articleTitle: Detecting ground faults in synchronous machines using sweep-frequency-response-analysis (SFRA)
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Synchronous machines are important equipment in power plants and drive systems. Safe and trouble-free operation is essential, but this can be interrupted by electrical or mechanical faults. Commonly occurring faults in synchronous machines are grounding faults. This results in a conductive connection between parts of the winding and grounded elements. In this work, the Sweep- Frequency-Response-Analysis (SFRA) method is used to detect these specific faults. The SFRA method is relatively simple and fast to apply, is non-invasive and sensitive to various electrical and mechanical parameters of the machine. For the purpose of ground-fault detection, multiple ground faults are generated at the stator and rotor winding and the changes in the frequency response are observed. For example, artificial stator-to-ground faults were implemented on different phases and different positions within one phase. It was found that the failure position can have an influence on the frequency response. Faults near the middle of the winding show similar frequency responses, even with reverse measurement direction. However, faults near a terminal result in specific changes after inverting the measurement direction. If a stator-to-ground fault was detected in a first place, this characteristic might help to narrow down the fault location. Additionally, artificial rotor-to-ground faults were implemented. Comparable behavior to the stator faults can be seen when measuring the field winding on the rotor. Beyond that, the SFRA is sensitive enough to detect such failures by measuring purely the stator side without direct contact to the stator. The fundamentals for this behavior are explained in detail using a previously developed model and verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Evaluation of HVDC ripple effect on partial discharge testing using a hybrid method
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper presents a needle-to-plane test setup to simulate one typical potential defect in high voltage direct current gas insulated switchgear, and correspondingly evaluate its generated partial discharge characteristics under multi-order high voltage direct current harmonic components. An arbitrary waveform high voltage source was used to stress insulation defects under different excitation voltages especially sinusoidal ac and dc with impressed ripple. Discharge behaviour was measured simultaneously using an ultra-high frequency antenna and high-frequency current transformer. Of particular interest are the novel phase resolved partial discharge algorithm that could be adopted in dc ripple conditions to evaluate the discharge behaviours, along with the simultaneous identification of discharge distribution under dc ripple and ac conditions without phase reference. The comparable results revealed that dc ripple discharge distribution and amplitude have more correlation to the peak of repetitive harmonic content by applying the same post-processing methodology, while ac partial discharge distribution and diagnostics method in the phase domain is directly decided by the power frequency. It was found that while the phase resolved patterns are drastically different under ac and dc ripple, the correlations between the energy of the radiated discharge and its apparent charge are similar in both cases. Hybrid techniques may therefore offer a new approach for distinguishing between partial discharge behaviour in ac and dc systems in the absence of a phase reference by analysing the relationship between the two measured quantities that yields more information on the shape of the current pulse and the physics of partial discharge.

articleTitle: Influence of bonding wire arrangement on current distribution in lightning strike to automobile
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In recent years, due to the effects of global warming, vehicles with low environmental load such as electric vehicles and fuel cell vehicles have become widespread. Compared to gasoline-powered vehicles, these vehicles use more electronic components for control and may be vulnerable to electromagnetic disturbances caused by surges such as lightning. When an automobile is hit by lightning, the lightning current flows from the body to the ground via the internal gears and from the wheels. At that time, a transient electromagnetic field is generated in the vehicle, and this kind of transient electromagnetic field causes malfunction or failure of electronic devices. However, it cannot be said that lightning countermeasures for electrical and electronic equipment inside the vehicle have been sufficiently studied. The importance of lightning protection for such equipment is increasing. In fact, ``engine start failure'' and ``battery failure'' etc. are reported as lightning damages, and it is thought that countermeasures for electronics and electrical equipment connected to a battery are necessary to prevent lightning damages. In this paper, we conducted a test to investigate the shunting of the current flowing into the batteries of automobiles with different bonding wire arrangements, and clarified the characteristics of each vehicle.

articleTitle: Advanced pollution monitoring and modelling for insulation dimensioning
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Power companies often need to evaluate the Design Pollution Severity (defined in IEC 60815-1 as SPS, Site Pollution Severity). This is valid both for new overhead lines and substations and for the uprating and refurbishment projects. This is especially important for severe polluted environments, where pollution performance is a dominant dimensioning factor, but may also be important for lower polluted environments providing optimal insulation dimensioning. To define the SPS with high level of confidence, reliable pollution monitoring is a must. This paper summarizes latest improvements in pollution monitoring using Directional Dust Deposit Gauges (DDDG). These include DDDG combining standard measurements with direct pollution measurements and with leakage current measurements. This paper also summarizes the verification of the most promising weather model for the modelling of SPS. Finally selected Ohba model is verified using 17-months field pollution measurements by DDDG and by pollution measurements on some insulators flashed over in service. The improvements allowed to increase the correlation factor between modelling and actual measurements to high value of R2=0.86. The model can detect areas where the faults occur or are at increased risk to occur. More work is needed to get a resolution at a single tower level.

articleTitle: Concept of automatic diagnosis of high voltage switchgears using IED
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In recent years, efforts have been made to install sensors on substation equipment, combine and analyze the information from sensors with information obtained from IEDs, and utilize the information for condition diagnosis and asset management of power equipment. When a new substation is built, it is possible to employ power equipment with built-in sensors in advance, but in existing substations, sensors are retrofitted to the power equipment. Therefore, the authors studied a method of equipment diagnosis that utilizes only data stored in IEDs and data from existing substation equipment (e.g., monitoring cameras), without installing new sensors on power equipment. These methods for diagnosing the operation of switchgear by utilizing the functions of the IED like oscilloscope-function, external contact output, and log data related to switchgear opening and closing. By utilizing these functions, the condition of equipment can be monitored and signs of malfunction can be seized before the switchgear becomes "inoperative" without having to perform periodic inspections. Reducing the number of periodic inspections will not only reduce the costs associated with inspection work, but also reduce the risk to the power supply by reducing the number of facility outage for inspections.

articleTitle: Classification of partial discharge sources under DC voltage by wavelet decomposition
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Due to the increasing importance of high voltage DC components in the transmission systems, HVDC-specific diagnostic methods will become indispensable. In AC systems it is possible to perform a partial discharge diagnostic analysis about the nature of the fault based on the way and the phase angle in which partial discharges occur. Unfortunately, a similar technique is, due to the lack of angular references and time invariability in the case of HVDC systems, impossible. Based on these considerations a method based on a wavelet packet decomposition for the classification of partial discharges is presented in this contribution. Partial discharges were induced and measured in models of typical faults in solid insulation systems in two different polymeric solid insulation materials. Special test sequences optimized to reduce the influence of space charges and to analyse the influence of the voltage and the test period as well as the type of used measurement bandwidth were implemented. The use of the investigated method shows a good performance in classifying partial discharge sources, which demonstrates the potential of wavelet packet decomposition for the development of diagnostic tools.

articleTitle: Statistical evaluation and numerical indexing in quantification of VLF tanδ for water tree
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: KEPCO (Korea electric power corporation) uses the VLF TD (Very low frequency tanδ) diagnostic technique as one of the diagnostic methods for determining the degradation state of power cables for distribution. This is a diagnostic technology that measures dielectric loss through a phase difference between voltage and current by applying a sinusoidal AC power source with a very low frequency characteristic of 0.1Hz to the power cable. Measurements are taken eight times over the same line. The test voltages of IEEE and KEPCO standards shall be 0.5 U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, 1.0 U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and 1.5 U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. The test result is used as the most suitable method for determining signs that may occur from degradation, such as the generation of water trees inside an insulator or voids. In this paper, various determination factors that can be obtained through the above diagnosis method are introduced, limitations of determining the degradation state of a cable using these factors are considered, and a solution is proposed.

articleTitle: Characteristics of partial discharges under SPWM voltage excitation
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The high frequency switching associated with pulse width modulation (PWM) excitation voltage in variable speed drives can cause partial discharges (PD) in the motor winding insulation, the rise time of the PWM pulse influences the PD characteristics. Experiments are carried out on twisted pairs of winding wires under sinusoidal PWM (SPWM) applied voltage to simulate PDs occurring in motor windings. The PD measurement is hampered by the interference caused by the SPWM switching. A filtering scheme based on a combination of hardware and software filters is used to extract the PD signals, the latter developed based on the stochastic characteristics of PD and the repeatability of the switching. Results demonstrate the proposed filtering scheme improves interference rejection and PD detection sensitivity. The influence of SPWM rise time and twisted turns on PD characteristics is examined including the shape and rise time of the PD waveform, and phase-resolved PD pattern. Comparison is also made with measurements of similar type of surface discharges from a flat dielectric sheet.

articleTitle: Location of partial discharges sources using radiometric signal envelopes
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In this paper, an experimental arrangement was developed with four UHF antennas and high-voltage equipment to emulate Partial Discharge (PD) activity. From the measurements carried out in this arrangement, two approaches were used to determine the source location: the first one is the time difference of arrival method, which requires the time of arrival of the original signal, while the second one is the received signal strength method, which is only based on the PD amplitude and was performed by extracting the envelope of the original signal. The results showed that both algorithms were effective in determining the location of the PD source. However, the second method does not require synchronism or a high sample rate, showing to be a promising approach.

articleTitle: Calculation of temperature dependent critical field strength of mixtures containing C5-FK, CO2 and O2
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Many of today's novel SF6-free gas mixtures for high- and medium-voltage insulation use low-percentage admixtures of perfluoroketone (C5-FK) or perfluoronitrile (C4-FN) in mixtures of CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, and/or N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Mixture compositions vary widely based on target operating conditions, with several different mixtures being reported in literature. Testing each mixture composition in real equipment is time consuming and financially too expensive. While carrying out classical breakdown tests is simple, it requires numerous tests to cover all relevant technical geometries, including those with defects and consequent ly high field non-uniformities. Adding to the complexity, the breakdown mechanism in non-uniform fields depends on the ambient pressure, field utilization factor and gas properties, among other factors. Models for characterizing the insulation properties of pure gases under arbitrary electrode configurations and arbitrary voltage waveshapes exist [1 - 4]. Important input for these models is the temperature dependent critical field strength and thermodynamic properties of the gas. A first step towards using these models to investigate the insulation properties of gas mixtures is an accurate chemical kinetic description of the gas mixtures. Recently, chemical decomposition and recombination pathways of pure C5-FK and C4-FN have received much attention [5]. In the present contribution we study kinetic models for mixtures containing C5-FK, CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> based on ab-initio calculations. We include reactions of the carrier gas molecules, CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and present a method for calculating the temperature dependent critical field strength of mixtures containing C5-FK, CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Results are given for a selected mixture over a wide pressure and temperature range, and we motivate the need for more thorough kinetic modelling of the C5-FK decomposition process.

articleTitle: In search of the optimal declination of the silicone insulator profile
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The objective of this work is to search for the optimal declination of the silicone insulator profile. This amounts to examining the behavior of water droplets on the surface of the silicone elastomer used for the coating of the insulator systems, confronted with the external pollution aggression. In this context, we investigated the Silicone's loss of hydrophobicity according to the declination of the insulation surface, this under the effect of the following influence parameters: the size of the water drops, their electrical conductivity, their distribution, and the material surface condition (virgin and aged under 50 Hz alternating voltage in the case of both a clean surface and surface polluted with conductive wet solution). For each considered cases, it comes to determine the contact angle θ and hence the silicone hydrophobicity index (HI) to decide on its state, this for different angle α of silicone insulation surface declination.

articleTitle: Research on power frequency insulation characteristics of five refrigerant gases
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas is restricted by many countries due to its GWP value of 23500. It is now a hot issue to find its alternative environmentally friendly insulation gas. In this paper, power frequency breakdown tests for R32, R152a, HFC-1234yf, HFO-1234ze (E) and HFO-1336mzz (E) refrigerant gases are carried out under unified test conditions. The power-frequency insulation strength of different gases under the condition of 0.1 MPa pressure and the slightly nonuniform electric field is studied, and compared with SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>, CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gases. The results showed that the insulation strength of R152a, HFC-1234yf, HFO-1234ze (E) and HFO-1336mzz (E) is weaker than SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> and stronger than the buffer gas N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Carbon precipitation occurred in all the test refrigerant gas after discharge, which polluted the test chamber and produced a conductive layer. There are limitations for tested refrigerant gas to replace SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> as the main insulating gas.

articleTitle: Predischarge current measurement for large electrodes tested with switching-like voltage impulses
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The atmospheric air is a widely used electrical insulating media. There is general knowledge on how it would behave under different conditions, like changes in its physical properties and surrounding materials where it works as electrical insulation. To control electric field concentrations on high voltage equipment and possible failures of the air insulation, large, rounded electrodes are designed to provide shielding. The electrical discharge propagation process has been an important study area, to understand the characteristics of air as insulation media. Fast cameras, digital storage oscilloscopes, sensors have been used in high voltage laboratory testing. By measuring the transient current during the electrical discharge initiation, it is possible to determine three early stages: corona inception, streamer to leader transition and the final jump, last stage before full flashover. In this study we present the results of laboratory testing done on large electrodes tested with switching-like voltage impulses, where an innovative predischarge current measurement system was employed, paying special attention to the requirements of bandwidth and magnitude for fast current transients, remote operation at the high voltage electrode and voltage stress endurance of the whole system to measure small currents and withstand the full impulse current.

articleTitle: Electrical tracking and combustibility performance of RTV silicone rubber composite insulation
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The overhead electricity network heavily relies on silicone rubber-based composite insulators. The insulation possesses superior flashover and hydrophobic properties which is desirable for reliable network operation. However, its poor electrical tracking and combustibility resistance is a concern. This work reports the electrical tracking and combustibility performance of silicone matrix using alumina trihydrate (ATH), graphene nanoplatelets (GN) and milled glass fibre (GF). The test samples with different formulations such as S0 (pristine), S1 (30%-ATH) and S2 (30%-ATH, 1%-GN, 5%-GF) are fabricated, and the tracking resistance is evaluated according to IEC60587 using criterion 2. In addition, the combustibility is evaluated using the cone calorimeter following ASTM E 1354.0. Results show that tracking performance improves by 42.7% and 58.6% in S1 and S2 relative to S0 and it is improved by 27.7% in S2 compared to S1. Furthermore, S1 and S2 offer 33% and 46% more reductions in peak heat release rate (PHRR) than S1, while S2 offers a 20% better reduction in PHRR than S1. The high fire performance index (FPI) and low fire growth index (FGI) of S2 also indicate its enhanced combustibility resistance.

articleTitle: Development of a sensor for monitoring the paper condition using infrared spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Abstract The service life of a power transformer depends mainly on its insulation system. As the insulation system ages, the electrical and dielectric properties of the insulation decrease. High temperatures, acids and water accelerate ageing. Acids are a product of cellulose degradation and oil ageing. Cellulose degradation mainly results in polar low-molecular-weight acids, which accumulate in the paper and considered to be highly harmful. Currently, the total acid number (TAN) of the insulating oil is used to assess the condition of the insulating material. However, monitoring the acidity of the insulating paper is a more feasible method as harmful acids remain there. It is reasonable to develop a tool to monitor the acid in the paper that can be done directly, non-destructively and at a low cost. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) can be used to detect changes in the chemical structure of the insulating paper and identify acids. Acids have a specific absorption peak in the spectrum and the intensity of the absorbance determines the acid concentration. For this reason, a basic functional model of an online-monitoring system was developed.

articleTitle: Fundamental study on thermal deterioration diagnosis for thermally upgraded paper
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: A method of calculating the average degree of polymerization of kraft paper used in power transformers was developed by one of the authors to evaluate the thermal deterioration of the paper. This method is based on a transient temperature calculation employing a thermal-circuit model of the transformer. The average degree of polymerization of kraft paper can be calculated from the transient temperature of the paper and its thermal deterioration characteristics. In this study, this method is expanded to the thermally upgraded paper used in transformers. Thermally accelerated aging tests of the thermally upgraded paper are conducted, and their thermal deterioration characteristics, that is, the temperature characteristics of the half-value period of the average degree of polymerization, are obtained. Using the obtained thermal deterioration characteristics of thermally upgraded paper combined with the developed method, the life of thermally upgraded paper used in power transformers is evaluated and compared with that of kraft paper under realistic load conditions.

articleTitle: An evaluation of condition monitoring and diagnosis system for transformer bushing
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: For ensuring the reliability of transformer operation, it is imperative to develop online bushing monitoring and condition assessment technologies capable of diagnosing early-stage internal insulation degradation and initiating appropriate measures upon exceeding permissible thresholds. This paper deals with the development of a bushing PD diagnostic method on a very high-frequency (VHF) range that enables the detection of insulation defects in the early stage and minimizes external noise interference. The development of a bushing tap adaptor sensor to measure the PD signal from internal bushing and the diagnostic algorithm to identify bushing defects were preceded. Utilizing the result, we have successfully completed the development of a bushing diagnostic system and its performance verification has been done with the PD test according to IEC-60270.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of air breakdown voltage at different altitude conditions
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The dielectric strength of external insulation is influenced by several parameters such as the type of overvoltage stress, geometry, the location and surroundings, and the air atmospheric conditions at the location, among others. Usually, the equipment site location might have conditions different than the normal service design conditions and the standard reference conditions. Therefore, for the sake of achieving proper design or testing, it is required to apply atmospheric correction factors between the specific site conditions and the standard reference conditions and/or the standard service conditions.The present paper studies the atmospheric corrections for altitude used in external air insulation for short gaps. It gathers data of different tests performed under positive DC and SI impulses for quasi-uniform and non-uniform gaps. Tests in a pressurized chamber were performed variating the pressure, to replicate altitudes above sea level up to 5000 m. Simple arrangements as rod - plane gap, sphere - plane and toroid - plane gap were tested. Fifty percent breakdown voltage tests were performed and repeated several times. The data of the tests is compared with the altitude corrections following the recommendations of IEC standards.

articleTitle: Study of statistical failure rate evaluation for long life equipment based on operational data
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In developed countries, maintenance of aging electric power equipment is an important issue, and rational measures are being taken by utilizing the asset management techniques. Rational maintenance and renewal plannings based on risk analysis are required, and in order to perform such risk analysis, it is necessary to accurately estimate the failure rate according to the age of the equipment to be evaluated. One of the methods for understanding aging characteristics is statistical analysis of equipment operation data such as failures and operation records. However, there are some points to consider when applying this method to equipment that can be operated for a long period of time, has a wide age distribution, and is expected to have high reliability through preventive maintenance.
