In this paper, assuming a group of equipment with a wide age distribution and their failure rate characteristic by age, the author generates hypothetical operational data by simulating the failure occurrence assumed when the equipment is operated for a certain period of time, and try to estimate the original failure rate characteristic through the statistical analysis using these data. Within this study, the use of interval estimation in binomial distributions is proposed.

articleTitle: Performance of universal voltage dividers for measurement of superimposed voltages
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Tests with superimposed voltages are used as a means of of replicating the electrical stress occurring on power equipment. During these tests, the components are simultaneously stressed with either an AC or a DC voltage and an impulse voltage (e.g. LI/SI). The measurement of the resulting voltage is ideally achieved with universal voltage dividers (RCR dividers), which have not yet been standardized. This publication focuses on the performance of universal voltage dividers at different voltage combinations as a proposed contribution to the standardization of tests with superimposed voltages. The measurement results of two commercially available measurement systems from different manufacturers, based on universal voltage dividers, were compared with a reference measurement system to assess the effects of composite voltages on linearity and measurement uncertainty. The investigations were focused on the combination of DC and lightning as well as switching impulse voltages. The performed tests showed that a DC component (tested up to 350 kV DC, maximum bipolar impulse stress of 1100 kV) did not lead to any effects on the impulse voltage measurement performance of the measurement systems. All systems retained their high overall accuracy during all of the tests. The obtained results will be used to investigate how universal voltage dividers can be calibrated and how this process can be standardized.

articleTitle: Partial discharge behaviour in GIS with fluoronitriles: analysis of pressure dependence and PD measurement methods
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Eco-efficient insulating gases are investigated for more than a decade replacing sulphur hexafluoride (SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>) to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. One alternative to SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> is the gas mixture of fluoronitrile C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>-FN with CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. In gas-insulated systems (GIS) the analysis of the partial discharge (PD) behaviour is a very effective diagnostic method. Thus, this contribution focuses on PD measurements under AC voltage stress depending on the gas pressure in an eco-efficient gas mixture. A grounded needle and a plate connected to high-voltage potential are used as model arrangement. A four-channel-oscilloscope ensures the time-synchronous measurement of the PD current, optical signals detected with a photomultiplier, in the UHF range and of the applied voltage. Furthermore, a measurement according to IEC 60270 is carried out with a commercially available PD measurement system. The investigations are performed for two different gas pressures (0.35 MPa<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">abs</sub> and 0.7 MPa<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">abs</sub>). The partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) and the phase-resolved partial discharge (PRPD) patterns at different voltage levels are analysed. Pulseless discharges at the negative protrusion are detected by current measurement at 0.35 MPa<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">abs</sub> and 0.7 MPa<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">abs</sub>. Space charge accumulation in vicinity to the needle tip is significantly influencing the PD behaviour.

articleTitle: Comparison of transient and steady state dielectric behaviour of different oil and oil-pressboard barrier systems
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper aims at investigating and modelling the polarisation and conduction processes in oil and oil-impregnated pressboard (OIP) barrier systems of HVDC transformers. For this purpose, electro-optic Kerr-effect and polarisation current measurements are performed in oil-pressboard system mock-ups. The measurement results are compared with conventional RC models, so that their validity can be investigated. The results show that the initial behaviour after switching on the DC voltage as well as the steady state can be described with this simplified model. For the transient processes, only general assumptions can be made. However, the transient field distribution and the transient electric currents cannot be predicted. All in all, in this contribution, the applicability and the limits of the conventional RC modeling are shown.

articleTitle: Investigation of an online fault gas monitoring system for hermetically sealed power transformers
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Hermetically sealed oil-filled power transformers are manufactured with a sealed and gastight tank. A gas cushion, usually compressed nitrogen or dry air, is maintained above the liquid. In case of severe faults, the generation of a considerable amount of fault gases is expected, which will, in the case of hermetically sealed power transformers, gradually escape from the insulating liquid and diffuse into the gas cushion. As a cost-effective and compact alternative to gas chromatography, a prototype semiconductor-based online monitoring system of undissolved fault gases was developed by the Schering-Institute. In this contribution, the new monitoring system is investigated regarding its accuracy under different conditions. The developed online monitoring system in this contribution is based on a set of integrated sensors housed in an aluminium enclosure, a controller board, a DC power supply, and a device software, tracking the concentration of fault gases in the gas cushion continuously, through which faults in the insulating system can be detected early. Furthermore, physical parameters such as temperature, pressure, oxygen, and humidity are also recorded permanently. The proposed online monitoring system showed convincing and promising results.

articleTitle: Enhancement of cable life cycle assessment in DEWA network
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Power cables and their accessories are essential in transmitting electric power in a network. These components are exposed to degradation due to the complex working environment surrounding the distribution network. Life prediction of cables and their accessories is crucial to ensure reliable operation and efficiency within the network. Hence, the main objective of this study is to provide a methodology for the Condition Monitoring (CM), and diagnosis based on the calculation of aging score by utilizing the initial cable failure analysis and network data in order to reduce the optimization of maintenance and replacement policies. For this purpose, an aging score is calculated based on a combination of statistical approaches including; failure rates such as water penetration, excessive heat, prior damage, poor workmanship, water barrier issues, manufacturing defects, aged circuits and installation processes, insulation failure, termination condition, transient, short term stresses and condition monitoring results. These are the key factors to enhance the Life Cycle Management (LCM), which aims to make the best use of the operational value of power cable assets in Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA).

articleTitle: Numerical evaluation model of insulator pollution level for overhead lines in coastal salt fog region
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The surface of outdoor insulators, which plays a necessary supporting and insulating role in power grid lines and equipment, is easy to accumulate pollution under a long-term operation process. In case of heavy fog, drizzle and other weather conditions, the pollution on the surface of insulators can easily lead to discharge, or even cause flashover accidents and power outages. This has seriously hindered the safe and stable operation of the power grid, resulting in significant economic losses. This paper will develop a numerical evaluation method for the pollution status of transmission line insulators under the effect of salt fog, in which the operation voltage, relative humidity and equivalent salt deposit density are taken into consideration. Then, based on the mechanism analysis and regression analysis, numerical formulas of the leakage current amplitude, phase and frequency domain characteristics are constructed. Afterwards, a pollution flashover index based on hierarchical analysis is introduced to comprehensively evaluate the pollution level of insulators. The comparison between the calculated pollution level and the field data verifies the applicability of the proposed model, providing an effective and easy-to-use method for the diagnosis of overhead line insulators.

articleTitle: Investigation of pre-breakdown phenomena in CO2
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: While performing high-voltage pulsed breakdown tests in room temperature pure CO2 at 0.1 MPa, significant voltage dips (up to 20 kV) were observed preceding the breakdown on application of voltages in the range of 40-70 kV. The time duration of these voltage dips can be up to a few hundred nanoseconds, followed by the full breakdown of the gap. Such dips were observed on application of negative polarity impulses to the electrode in a rod-plane configuration at 0.1 MPa. However, the dips were absent at higher pressures. To investigate these pre-breakdown discharges in detail, an experimental setup was developed with necessary diagnostic tools to measure the pre-breakdown current. Optical diagnostics such as a photomultiplier and a (fast) intensified-CCD camera were also used to study the discharge characteristics. In the setup developed to measure the pre- breakdown currents, a commercial fiber optic transmission link is used to isolate the current measurement on the high volage side from ground. However, to power the fiber optic connectors, a novel method called 'power over fiber', was employed. In this study, along with the findings of the pre-breakdown phenomena to qualitatively describe the discharge process in CO2 at various pressures (0.1-0.9 MPa), the technique used to measure the current on the high voltage electrode side is also described.

articleTitle: Practical experience from industry on the lightning protection of solar PV modules
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper reports the practical experience from industry on the performance of the lightning protection of solar PV modules, which are necessarily installed in the open. The conventional practice as per the current industry experience is to use the support frame of the solar PV module for the passage of the lightning current should it be struck. Hence, the support frames are bonded to the lightning protection system installed. This leaves other parts of the PV modules vulnerable to direct lightning strikes with the result of the lightning current flowing through the DC cable rather than the lightning protection tapes that are bonded to the frame. This, therefore, results in the electronic AC/DC invertor being subject to the direct lightning current and against which they are not protected. The paper will provide examples of such incidents and will consider and discuss how best to avoid such penetration of direct lightning in future installations. The paper will also recommend that the industrial experience be considered during the next update of the Standard when referring to protection of solar PV modules against lightning. With the current global initiative to maximise renewable energy systems it is even more important to ensure that the systems are fail safe and can last their economic life thereby delivering the desired savings.

articleTitle: Importance of impulse calibrator output impedance and method of all-waveform compensation
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The influence of the impulse calibrator output impedance on the measured waveform is often ignored because of the rather limited bandwidth of lightning and switching impulses and the short cable connection to the digitizer. A simple model defined by the output impedance of an amplifier-based calibrator, the characteristic impedance of the measuring cable and the input capacitance of the digital recorder is used to compensate the pulse distortion effects of the measurement setup with a significant influence on the front-time of lightning impulse waveforms. Evaluation of an all-waveform compensation is performed on recorded and simulated data. Investigations to transfer the compensation of the raw data into the curve fitting process resulted in a new no-added noise compensation method and application of the Shannon limit has been introduced as a performance indicator for the dependence of the waveform time parameters on the noise level and bandwidth of the calibration setup. The example presented in this paper, although centered on the topic of the calibrator output impedance, will serve as a pertinent entry point to the calibration of high-voltage dividers and impulse digitizers.

articleTitle: Effect of gas pressure on flashover voltage of cone-type insulating spacer in dry air
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper describes the effects of gas pressure on flashover voltage (FOV) of cone-type insulating spacers in dry air. SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> gas is widely used in Gas Insulated Switchgear (GIS). However, its global warming potential (GWP) is 25,200 times higher than CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Recently, the application of high-pressure dry air has been considered as a candidate for an environmentally friendly insulating gas. In this study, a 1/4 size mini model insulating spacer (designed based on a 245 kV class SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> GIS) were fabricated. Effect of gas pressure from 0.1 MPa-abs to 0.5 MPa-abs on FOV in dry air and flashover traces were investigated. In the experiment, standard lightning impulse voltage (-1.2/50 μs) was used as test voltage and FOVs were measured by the step-by-step voltage raising method. 50% FOV was estimated by Weibull analysis. As a result, the following findings were obtained. (1) The maximum electric field was generated at the shield edge of the central conductor on the concave side of the spacer, (2) we confirmed that the discharge generated from the shield edge of the central conductor to the spacer surface on the concave side by observing flashover trace, and (3) the 50% FOV increased with the addition of nanofiller.

articleTitle: Detection of transformer winding fault using double-end nanosecond pulse method: a simulation study
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The nanosecond pulse method detects various faults in transformer windings with greater sensitivity than the frequency response analysis (FRA) method. The rectangular pulse of the nanosecond range (100–500 ns) is injected from one end of the winding, and the time domain response signal is measured from the other end of the winding in a healthy condition. The mechanical or electrical changes in the winding can be detected by comparing the faulty and healthy responses. However, the healthy response is not always available for comparison for many transformers, particularly older units. Therefore, it becomes difficult to apply the conventional nanosecond pulse method to detect the faults in those transformer windings. Therefore, in this work, a double-end nanosecond pulse method is proposed to detect the faults in the transformer windings without a healthy response. It overcomes the limitation of the conventional nanosecond pulse method. This paper describes the simulation study of the proposed method using a ladder network model of the transformer with continuous disk winding to detect the different types of electrical and mechanical faults in the winding, such as short-circuit faults (inter-turn faults), earth faults (winding to ground faults), and mechanical faults (radial and axial deformations).

articleTitle: The dielectric characteristics of 22 KV XLPE underground cables with degraded artificial joint
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper represents the dielectric characteristics of the 22 kV underground cable test specimen. Two 3 m XLPE underground cables were connected with the heat-shrinkable joint that has been simulated with some artificial defects. The healthy heat-shrinkable terminations are at both ends of the cable test specimen. For this research, the underground cables with the healthy joint, the joint with a copper powder contaminant on the XLPE surface, and the joint with an incision on the XLPE surface were prepared to perform the experiment. To compare the dielectric characteristics of the underground cables with the healthy joint and degraded artificial joints, the polarization and depolarization currents (PDC) measurements and the very low frequency-tangent delta (VLF-TD) testing, according to IEEE standard 400.2-2013, were conducted. From the PDC measurements, the test results are not clearly different for the underground cables with the defective joint when compared to the healthy joint case, except for the electrical conductivity and insulation resistance that show the difference between them. The VLF tangent delta parameters and mean tangent delta comparison curve show differences in each case, which can contribute to assessing the condition of the underground cable systems.

articleTitle: The filtered frequency spectrum method for GPR evaluation due to lightning strikes
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Concerns about the ground potential rise (GPR) developed by lightning strokes, which result in hazardous voltages, have led to models for Lightning Protection Systems (LPS) considering the soil properties. A direct time-domain GPR evaluation may be a realistic estimation using an appropriate model for producing fast and approximate results for different LPS geometries. This is also achieved by considering the aim of creating practical resources for the LPS project, such as its physical installation analysis and risk evaluation of hidden grid ruptures or disconnections. The frequency dependence of the soil parameters (FDSP) cannot be disregarded. otherwise, GPR is not expressed realistically, especially for higher soil resistivity. This article presents an approximate Filtered Frequency Spectrum Method (FFSM) to evaluate the GPR as a fast response assuming FDSP. ATP-EMTP is used for simulation. The frequency spectrum of the lightning current is obtained by Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). The spectrum is split into bands using filters. A circuital model using Transmission Line Modelling is constructed for each band where the final response is obtained by a sum of partial results. The GPR is close to that obtained with Vector Fitting, assuming the reference response. The filter parameters are based on the energy distribution of the input lightning current.

articleTitle: Feasibility study of transfer learning models for across capacity fault diagnosis in induction motors
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: As the global share of renewable energy continues to increase, the operation and maintenance strategy for large wind turbines becomes increasingly important. Therefore, the fault diagnosis of large units has become a focal point in research. In traditional fault diagnosis, a large amount of fault data needs to be collected to train the model. However, historical fault data on large unit are scarce, defective models are difficult to produce, and even if feasible, they are expensive to produce. First, to evaluate the effectiveness of the initial cross-capacity transfer learning, a healthy motor and four artificially defective motor models were selected for the 2-horsepower (source domain) and 5-horsepower (target domain) induction motors so as to measure their vibration signals under different load conditions. Through normalization method, the raw vibration signal is converted into a two-dimensional (2-D) time-domain image and collected into an image set. Secondly, we apply the recent booming transfer learning models, including Deep Domain Confusion (DDC), Deep Adversarial Neural Network (DANN) and Deep Subdomain Adaptation Network (DSAN) for source domain training and cross-capacity target domain testing. Finally, the results were compared and analyzed with an accuracy of up to 80%, which initially confirmed the feasibility of cross-capacity fault diagnosis for future wind turbines.

articleTitle: Statistical pattern recognition of thermal and electrical degradation index of transformer DGA
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In Korea DGA analysis method Health Index uses a weighted summation method, inaccurate lifetime evaluation results can be exemplified. Duval's Triangle, a defect type evaluation method according to IEC 60599 abroad, is designed to suit each country's operating environment, so applying the standard of power transformers with different operating environments has a problem of inconsistent defect types. To resolve this problem, in this paper, the weights were re-selected in terms of thermal and electrical aspects using about 110,000 data acquired in 1983-2016 and the index was presented. In addition, based on the presented index, degradation progress patterns were classified according to the number of operating years.

articleTitle: Effects of electrode configurations on partial discharge characteristics of silicone oil
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In high voltage cable system, joints and terminations are considered to be vulnerable in terms of insulation failure. Although with the fast development of polymer insulation in cable systems, liquid filled cable joints / terminations are still widely used in the industry. One of the insulating liquids used in cable sealing end (CSE) is silicone oil. The common electrode configuration employed for studies related to partial discharge (PD) is the needle-plane (NP) or needle-sphere electrode configuration. Apart from the NP configuration which produces highly divergent electric field, plane-needle-plane (PNP) electrode configuration was used in this research. The PNP configuration has an adjustable needle protrusion that allows quasi-uniform electric field to be generated. This paper aims to study the relationship between the electrode configurations and the PD characteristics of a silicone oil. Partial discharge inception voltages (PDIV) are measured, and partial discharge inception fields (PDIF) are obtained by conducting FEM modelling. For voltage levels above the PDIV, measurements of PD patterns, maximum apparent charge and repetition rates are obtained. Results suggest that the PD characteristics of silicone oil are influenced by the electrode configurations but not the case for PDIF which remains in a narrow range with an average of 667.7 kV/mm.

articleTitle: Voltage endurance testing and lifetime behaviour of high voltage cables with DC vs. AC for electric vehicles
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: With the emerging development of large and powerful electric vehicles, like electric busses or electric trucks, the voltage levels used with electric vehicles is increasing. Systems using 1.2 kV have successfully been developed and the development of 3 kV systems is in progress to increase efficiency and reduce losses. Often the same cables are used in electric vehicles to connect the battery with the inverter using DC voltages and further connect the inverter to the motors where often 3 phase AC voltages are present at the cables. This has brought considerably more attention to the high voltage design and used insulation materials of the cables used in electric vehicles. To test and verify possible designs voltage endurance tests for lifetime estimations have to be performed with AC and DC as electrical ageing will take place in the cable insulation. In this publication we carried out voltage endurance tests at AC and DC at new developed high voltage cables for electric vehicles. The large differences in the results can be explained by accumulated space charges and the different electric field distribution at AC and DC voltages.

articleTitle: A comparative aging study of various commercial biodegradable insulation fluids
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The aging behaviour of three insulation fluids from sustainable sources (natural ester, synthetic ester, and a bio-based hydrocarbon fluid) were compared with that of a conventional mineral oil. All samples contained kraft paper and its degree of polymerisation (DP) confirmed that the aged samples covered most of the transformer lifecycle. The reported mitigating effect of ester oils on paper aging was observed in both ester oils whilst the bio-based hydrocarbon fluid exhibited comparable behaviour to the mineral oil. Natural ester had the highest values of acidity, viscosity and dielectric loss after aging and the bio-based hydrocarbon oil the lowest. The bio-based hydrocarbon fluid would be an excellent replacement for mineral oil in plant, particularly due to its very low viscosity which would aid cooling but with the drawback that paper aging is not mitigated. A synthetic ester is preferable over a natural ester in plant since its chemical, physical and dielectric properties do not deteriorate dramatically after aging.

articleTitle: Linearity extension of UHV class lightning impulse dividers up to 3000 kV
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Recent research has raised questions regarding the validity of the current linearity extension methods for lighting impulse voltages beyond 1500 kV. Factors identified include the unexpectedly large influence of proximity, corona and generator source impedance. The lowest uncertainty claimed by National Metrology Institutes for lightning impulse reference measurement systems up to 1000 kV is 0.5 % for the test voltage value Ut, and 1 % for both the front time T1 and the time to half value T2. Using state-of-the-art methods for a linear extension, earlier research has reported Ut non-linearities of 1 % up to 2700 kV, and more than 3 % above 3000 kV. The non-linearities in front times were significantly larger, and the reasons for that are not understood. A three-week measurement campaign was carried out at the high voltage laboratory at TU Delft in October 2022 to tackle the problem. The campaign started with calibration of nine measuring systems at 400 kV: five based on resistive divider with maximum voltages ranging from 500 kV to 2000 kV, and four based on damped capacitive divider with maximum voltages from 1000 kV to 4000 kV. In the second step these dividers were compared with each other in a step-up procedure while measuring the charging voltage of the generator.

articleTitle: Investigation on dielectric and electrical properties of low concentration graphene oxide filled polyurethane nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Polymers and their composites are predominantly used as the main insulating material in various electrical power and electronic systems. A polyurethane elastomer (PUE) obtained by two-step polymerization of low molecular weight polypropylene alcohol, MDI (diphenylmethane diisocyanate) and BDO (butanediol) has the potential to become the next generation of smart dielectric materials due to its excellent electrical strength, efficient self-healing capability, and good recyclability. Graphene oxide (GO) are an attractive candidate for functional fillers for these polymers to improve their properties. GO not only has a larger specific surface area relative to conventional nanoparticles, low density, and excellent mechanical strength, but also its base and edges have abundant oxygen-containing functional groups, such as epoxy, hydroxyl, carboxyl, and carbonyl groups. These oxygen-containing functional groups make GO have good compatibility with polymer substrates. In this study, PU/GO nanocomposites are obtained by solution blending method. In order not to affect the mechanical properties of polyurethane, the doping concentration is limited to less than 5% volume fraction. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showed that the GO sheets were dispersed uniformly in the polyurethane matrix. The DC conductivity characteristic of the composites was characterized by standard three-electrode testing method. Thermally stimulated depolarization current (TSDC) spectra are used to analyze the relaxation behavior of the composites, and the influence mechanism of doping GO on the conductivity and relaxation behavior of the composites was elucidated.

articleTitle: Evaluation of corona prevention performance of damaged RTV coated insulators to develop on-site repair guidelines
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In order to develop guidelines for the repairing damage to Room Temperature Vulcanizing (RTV) silicone rubber, artificial pollution tests were conducted under different degree of damage to RTV coating. The size of the damage was based on Φ50 mm which was bigger than maximum size expected to be occurred on site. As the results, the influence of coating damage on corona prevention performance was identified and the effectiveness of repairing was confirmed. The guideline was defined that damage sizes of smaller than Φ50 mm were acceptable for repair, while damage bigger than Φ50 mm or damage in all leakage directions were to be replaced. In addition, the discharge position of damaged RTV coated insulator was analysed with equivalent circuit models.

articleTitle: PD measurement above 1 MHz - limitations, challenges, solutions
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Partial discharge measurement has become a well-accepted and widespread diagnosis method. The IEC 60270 international standard defines how partial discharge should be measured, i.e. how to quantify partial discharge and how to perform the measurement in a plausible, repeatable, and comparable manner. However, recently measurements outside the frequency range recommended by IEC 60270 have become popular. The higher bandwidth approach claims to provide a higher signal-to-noise ratio due to lower background noise levels. This paper revises the IEC 60270 frequency range limitations and analyses measurements above those boundaries. The theoretical hypotheses are then verified by practical measurements. Limitations of such measurements are discussed, especially for large test objects or test objects with windings. The usage of the term “measurement” versus the term “indication” as well as the plausibility, repeatability, and comparability of such partial discharge measurements is discussed.

articleTitle: Dielectric properties of biochar polymer composites
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Electrically conductive polymer composites have applications in many areas of high voltage technology as insulators and as field grading elements in cable joints and terminations. Carbon Black is the predominant choice used as a filler material to alter the properties of the polymer composite due to its good conductive properties. Biochar is proposed as an environmentally friendly alternative to carbon black as a filler in conductive polymer composites. Biochar displays good conductive properties with high stability and excellent cation exchange capacity. In this contribution, the dielectric properties of conductive polymer composites incorporating biochar as a filler are examined. Measurements of conductivity, permittivity, and dissipation factor are used to characterise the behaviour of conductive polymer composites. Frequency Domain Spectroscopy in a frequency range of 10 mHz – 1 kHz is used to measure permittivity and dissipation factor. Conductivity measurements are carried out with a petaohmmeter. Measurements revealed an increase in the conductive behaviour of the polymer composite with a rising biochar filler content. The increasing conductive behaviour shows potential for conductive polymer composites in field grading applications. Custom made insulators produced by 3D printing to manifest tailor-made dielectric properties by varying biochar filler content can be investigated for field grading applications.

articleTitle: Evaluation over current protection under parallel arcing short circuit in low voltage distribution network
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Single line short circuit to ground for low voltage network is produce high current with electric arc. Generally, in house or public facility installation, this fault is protected by fuse or miniature circuit breaker (MCB). However, some fault case is not detected by protection device due to very short duration, even though arcing still generated. This case is one of the common root cause fire disasters and defined as Parallel Arc Fault (PAF). PAF is simulated in laboratory by short circuit between stranded cable filaments. The number of filaments that short-circuited varied. During experiments, parameters observed were peak current value, spike duration, and circuit breaker response. Statistical analysis and artificial neural networks (ANN) are used for analysis and evaluate the behaviour of low voltage PAF. The analysis shows that ANN-based detection system is successfully classified into case that protection system fails to work and able to work.

articleTitle: Partial discharge detection in solids at medium frequency voltages by vibration measurement
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Partial Discharge (PD) measurement is a common test method to validate electrical withstand of electric insulation in power electronic topologies with a test voltage similar to the medium frequency operation voltage of power electronic devices. The switched voltage leads to a transient dielectric displacement current. This current is superimposed by a discharge current. Additionally, the spectral contend of both transient currents overlaps. Therefore, PD measurement and filter techniques according to IEC 60270 are affected heavily and become inapplicable. The article focuses on the vibration measurement on solid materials to detect partial discharges inside the insulation. A representative setup was built to investigate in the usability of a vibration sensor to support the standardized PD measurement. First, measurements were performed with a 50 Hz test voltage to verify the sensitivity of a piezoelectric vibration sensor at different cavity volumes. Further, a voltage step simulates a single voltage pulse and produces the corresponding dielectric current. The voltage step was used to investigate in the PD detection performance of the vibration sensor in addition to the standardized PD measurement. The vibration sensor shows a good sensitivity to detect partial discharges. In the case of short voltage steps and high displacement currents the sensor is only applicable using methods of electromagnetic shielding and acoustic decoupling of the test circuit.

articleTitle: Estimation of transient signals for the insulation coordination in a 10 kV battery energy storage system
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In this paper a study for a design of an insulation coordination for a high voltage battery energy storage system (BESS) is presented. The growing power demand for large energy storage systems in the grids for compensation of differences in power generation and consumption, compensation of peak loads or strategic load-balancing motivates research in high voltage BESS with system voltages up to 10 kV. A major challenge in the course of designing of medium voltage BESS is the lack of rules for the insulation coordination. The insulation system in BESS must withstand the DC voltage as well as transient stresses caused by internal (e.g. switching actions, converter ripple) as well as external (e.g. surge voltages caused by lightning strokes) effects. During the design process, the characteristics of the relevant test voltages has to be taken into account, where transient test signals are mandatory for the verification of a high voltage insulation coordination. Inside smaller systems, as the inner “DC-microgrid” of battery storage systems, a large derivation of the transient voltages from the standard test voltages (e.g. “1.2/50” or “250/2500”) is expected. To determine realistic (physical or virtual) test voltages, a transient battery model is designed. In addition to a battery model, outer stray capacitance and inner inductance contribute to the transient system behaviour and are added to a virtual system model. The designed model is excited with expected fault voltages, currents and switching operations. Resulting network node voltages are transferred into electric field strength in the process of the insulation coordination design.

articleTitle: Voltage sharing improvement methods in series-connected MOSFETs for future grid high voltage applications
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In the future, series-connected SiC MOSFETs will become widely used in power-electronic-based medium and high voltage (HV) applications such as modular multilevel converters (MMCs). Balanced voltage sharing among the SiC MOSFET string is hard to be achieved due to possible deviation on MOSFET switching delay. In this paper, two types of gate signal delay adjustment methods (gate balancing core and improved RC snubber method) are presented to solve the unbalanced voltage sharing caused by MOSFET turn-off delay differences. The methods are validated with laboratory experiments performed on low-voltage prototypes and a performance comparison of these two approaches is given. Both methods significantly improve the drain-source voltage sharing, but the gate balancing core method is most suitable for HV and high-frequency applications.

articleTitle: High voltage SiC based calculable impulse voltage calibrator
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The calibration of measuring systems for high voltage lightning impulses and high switching impulse voltages is regulated by the IEC 60060 and IEC 61083 series of standards. In the case of the calibration of transient recorders, so-called impulse calibrators have been available for decades, which are designed as calculable voltage sources for double-exponential voltage waveforms up to an amplitude of several hundreds of volts. The calibrators available on the market have an RLC network and fast relays for generating standardised lightning and switching impulse voltages. However, these calibrators are not well adapted to the transient recorders on the market today, which can measure up to 2000 V. In addition, the used relays contain mercury and therefore are not easily available as well as toxic. This paper describes the design, construction, and feedback of a new impulse voltage calibrator for impulse voltages up to 2000 V. This calculable impulse voltage source has the advantage of being "Silicon Carbide Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors" (SiC MOSFET) based. Furthermore, this calibrator has all common lightning and switching impulse voltage shapes.

articleTitle: Electrical design and testing of additive 3D-printed medium voltage bushings for 24 kV
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Additive 3D printing processes have already been successfully introduced in many sectors. To investigate previously studied materials on a real electric component, the identically designed geometrically controlled electrical bushing was produced using three different 3D printing processes: Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF), Stereolithography (SLA) and Drop-on-Demand (DoD). The manufactured bushings for a maximum voltage of Um = 24 kV were electrically tested according to normative specifications for their partial discharges (PD), their AC breakdown and flashover strength as well as lightning impulse (LI) withstand voltage. In the PD test, the SLA bushing reaches the highest extinction voltage of 28 kV, followed by the DoD bushing with 21 kV. The FFF bushing reaches only 4 kV. During the AC tests, the SLA bushing again reaches the highest voltage of 70 kV, at which flashover occurs. At the DoD bushing, breakdown occurs at 33 kV and at the FFF bushing at 12 kV. Based on the results of the AC tests, only the SLA bushing was subjected to an LI test. Here, flashover under LI stress occurred above 110 kV. To summarise, only the geometrically controlled SLA bushing was able to meet all normative electrical requirements.

articleTitle: Pollution performance of indoor insulators used in HVDC stations
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Insulators for indoor applications may collect contamination due to not perfectly airtight building. Nevertheless, pollution flashover mechanism cannot develop when the humidity is controlled and wetting of the contamination is avoided. Pollution performance of indoor insulators is studied through modelling of humidity uncontrolled environment with ventilation cooling system in a hall of an HVDC converter station located in the vicinity of coast with humid ambient air. Indoor environment is simulated for different power transfer loads of the converter station. Risk of pollution flashover is estimated through analysis of temperature and humidity levels with respect to possible condensation and moisture absorption by pollution deposits. No wetting conditions are revealed due to low humidity levels. Minimum specific creepage distance for HVDC indoor insulators is recommended base d on the best design practice and operational experience.

articleTitle: Backflashover analysis in power transmission lines located on high-resistive porous soil
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This work investigates the influence of the porosity level on grounding modeling proposed by Archie’s formula and the harmonic grounding impedance (HGI) of a cross-foot grounding system buried in this type of soil. Then, the Ground Potential Rise (GPR) generated for the lightning currents representative of the first and subsequent return strokes is calculated. Finally, the overvoltages at the transmission tower struck by two lightning strikes are computed for an overhead transmission line (OHTL) above this soil. Results indicated that harmonic grounding impedance is notably influenced as the porosity level varies. As a consequence, the peak values of GPR waveforms increase with the increase of porosity level as the soil becomes more resistive. Furthermore, the lightning performance concerning the backflashover depends on the soil porosity and injected lightning currents. This work demonstrates the importance of taking into account the porosity level to compute the electromagnetic transient responses adequately.

articleTitle: Technology assessment of DC partial discharge monitoring of thin insulation layers in traction battery systems
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The aim of this paper is (1) to provide a systematic methodological framework to analyse and evaluate high voltage testing innovation processes for sustainable development and (2) to apply the framework for early fault detection of thin insulation layers in traction battery systems. From an engineering perspective, the paper uses a static and dynamic Socio-Technical System Analysis to show the linkage between technological innovations and interactions with the environment and society. The impacts of high voltage testing innovations can be discussed based on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) of the United Nations (UN) using a Sustainability Assessment Methodology for Innovations framed by Prospective Technology Assessment (ProTA). As a result of the Socio-Technical System Analysis, the paper focuses on how the testing innovation contributes to the circular economy of lithium-ion batteries (LIB).

articleTitle: Experimental and numerical study on vacuum arc for designing electrodes of vacuum interrupters
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Vacuum interrupters are expected to be able to apply to DC circuit breakers (DCCBs) for high-voltage DC (HVDC) systems. The objective of this work is to develop a numerical model for improving the design technique of axial magnetic field (AMF) electrodes of the vacuum interrupters suitable for DC interruption. To determine boundary conditions of the numerical model, surface temperature of the AMF electrode was measured by the two-colour pyrometry method. A two-dimensional one-fluid numerical model is also developed. The magnetohydrodynamic approximation and the two-temperature thermal non-equilibrium model is applied. The arc quenching process during free recovery similar to the DC interruption process is analysed using the developed model. It is found that during the steady arc, the smaller the vapor flux from the electrode, the higher the electric conductivity. On the other hand, during the free recovery, the smaller the vapor flux, the higher the decay rate of electric conductivity. It is suggested that the smaller the vapor flux, the more difficult the DC interruption at higher current rate (di/dt).

articleTitle: Investigation of streamer-leader transition during upward lightning
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Upward lightning requires a different approach than downward (cloud-to-ground) lightning. Some of the lightning strikes are triggered by the ground object itself. Whether it happens is dependent on e.g., the geometric dimensions, the structure, and the relative location of the object in its environment, as well as the charge location and distribution in the thundercloud. A computer simulation is featured in this article to investigate the phenomenon. A realistic wind turbine model is selected for the computation along with a thundercloud. Investigation of the thundercloud model is carried out to ensure its applicability to study the streamer-leader transition process. The simulation tracks the amplitude of the electric field between the turbine and the cloud initiated by the charge of the thundercloud with respect to the above-mentioned influencing factors. This electric field leads to a corona discharge and possibly a streamer on the rotor blade tip which might evolve into an upward leader. Calculations are carried out for different cloud heights in the interest of the parameters of the upward leader. The aim of this work is to determine the possible thundercloud heights for the initiation of an upward leader.

articleTitle: Analysis of space charge and current of oil-paper at different aging status by PEA-current measurement
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Oil-impregnated-paper is an essential insulating material which has been widely used in power transformers. As the external current in the circuit under HVDC is correlated with the internal space charge transportation, in this paper, an integrated space charge and external current measuring system is developed to test the time-dependent charge and current simultaneously. A series of oil-paper samples in different aging status are measured. The results indicate that both charge injection and transient current have a close relevance to the aging status of oil-paper. Along with the accelerated aging process, larger injection of homo-charge leads to a faster decrease of current after the voltage application while the external current returns with a faster dissipation of space charge after removal of the voltage. These results help to understand the mechanism of current variation, and may be useful for aging diagnosis on oil-paper insulation.

articleTitle: Prediction of on-load tap-changer switch time from vibroacoustic measurements by machine learnings
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Abstract The on-load tap-changer (OTLC) is the only mechanically moving part of power transformers, responsible for more than one third of the major transformer failures worldwide. Condition monitoring methods are therefore important to identify evolving issues. Failures can be prevented by condition-based maintenance, repair, or replacement of the unit. One popular method for monitoring the performance of an OLTC is vibroacoustic signal analysis. The total switching time of an OLTC is considered as a vital health indicator and thus in this paper we explore the possibility of using machine learning techniques to extract the total switching time. Data from laboratory test were used to train a neural network (NN) which was finally evaluated on different data sets from the test and the results show that the estimation and the true switching time generally agree within ±1 ms.

articleTitle: Simulation of supersonic flow in high-voltage circuit breakers
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: High-voltage circuit breakers (HVCB) are critical protection and control equipment in the electric transmission and distribution system. Analysis of the arc quenching process in the nozzle through modelling and simulation is a key stage in the development process of the HVCB. This paper introduces the first stage of simulation in which the flow is simulated without an arc, which helps to investigate the characteristics of supersonic flow. A model built based on an experimental study was used in the study. Characteristics of the flow including the development of shock and flow separation from the nozzle wall and the electrode surface were observed. Furthermore, the investigation of Mach number and shock strength can help identify flow characteristics. The impact of inlet pressure and the location of the downstream electrode on the Mach number distribution and pressure distribution were analysed. The increase in inlet pressure resulted in an increase in the shock strength. Also, the results show that the position of the downstream electrode has a significant impact on the flow behaviour.

articleTitle: The resonance frequency method for fast approximation of the bandwidth of resistive-capacitive high voltage dividers
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method and calculation formula for fast approximation of the 3 dB bandwidth and frequency analysis of resistive-capacitive (RC) high-voltage (HV) dividers for power-quality measurement. The calculation formula brings stray inductance, resonance frequencies as well as voltage divider ratio and nominal capacitance values of the high-voltage and low-voltage unit into context, which allows the determination of achievable bandwidth of RC dividers. The novel method is potentially helpful when a frequency analysis based on Swept-Sine-Method cannot be conducted due to a large divider ratio in combination with a low input-voltage signal or for designing an RC voltage divider considering the bandwidth-limiting effects. The calculation formula is derived analytically by treating the RC divider as two simplified resonant series circuits. For acquisition of resonance frequencies, two measurement procedures are used and applied to an exemplary 100 kV-RC dividermodule. The formula is verified by comparing the results to a Swept-Sine-Method and AC circuit analysis. Measurement results indicate that the approximation contains low error when the novel method is combined with 2-port-like calibrated measurement of the dividers resonances.

articleTitle: Safe electrical wiring interconnection systems (SEWIS)
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The use of high voltages on aircraft is essential if we are to deliver electrical systems with a high enough power density to enable electrification of propulsion. However, the use of high voltage coupled with the aerospace environment increases the risk of electrical failure and poses a risk to the safety of those on board the aircraft and those involved in its operation and maintenance. The Clean Skies project SEWIS has been focused on the development of methods to ensure the safe operation of the electrical interconnection systems used on board an aircraft (considering issues such as direct contact with a live conductor, exposure to high levels of electric / magnetic fields and the impact that arcs could have on adjacent systems / a composite airframe). This paper will report on the progress that the project has made to understand the failure modes associated with the use of high voltage wiring systems and the opportunities that exist to monitor the electrical system in a manner that gives early indication of such failures taking place. The design of a custom cable and connector system for use in both DC and AC systems will be discussed alongside simulation results derived from finite element analysis and electrical network simulation that highlight the challenges involved in detecting failure.

articleTitle: Design optimization of capacitive bushing using Nelder-Mead method and computer simulations
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This study proposes using the Nelder-Mead method and computational simulations based on the finite element method (FEM) to optimize the capacitive core of an oil-impregnated paper bushing. To this end, a representation of the studied bushing was built using computer-aided design software and simulated in COMSOL Multiphysics<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>. Its core was designed according to a conventional methodology and the proposed optimized methodology. In the proposed optimized methodology, the number of conducting layers was reduced in order to reduce construction materials, and the Nelder-Mead optimization method was used to adjust the position and length of the conductive layers, having as objective to minimize the maximum axial and radial electric fields in the bushing. As result, the bushing designed using the proposed methodology presented a reduction of 24.9% of the maximum electric field intensity. The results suggest that using optimization methods such as the Nelder- Mead method in combination with FEM-based computational simulations can be an effective tool for the optimization of capacitive bushings, reducing manufacture costs and increasing the power system's reliability.

articleTitle: Investigation of the influence of solar radiation on the thermal modeling of power transformers
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The growing number of renewable energy and its expansion in the electrical power grid might require the overloading of power transformers. The operating temperature strongly affects the aging of a transformer by reducing its insulation life especially for high temperatures. Therefore, methods to predict the operating temperatures must provide sufficient accuracy. The operating temperature is affected by the load and environmental factors like the ambient temperature and solar radiation. However, conventional thermal models do not consider additional heating caused by solar radiation which can lead to an underestimation of the operating temperatures. In this contribution, the conventional thermal model of IEC 60076-7 is extended by additional solar heating. Subsequently, the accuracy of the extended model is evaluated and compared to a standard model. Both models are parameterized and validated using data from a wind farm transformer at different seasons. Radiation data for model training and validation is derived from solar sensors installed at the transformer (expensive) and from a clear sky model (cheap). It is shown that the accuracy of standard thermal models can be enhanced by considering the additional heating due to solar radiation. However, the influence of solar radiation in the thermal behaviour of the power transformer decreases for higher load factors.

articleTitle: An FEM simulation model of oil-pressboard insulating systems for HVDC transformers
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In this contribution, a simulation model for the description of the nonlinear dielectric behaviour of an insulation system composed of mineral oil and oil-impregnated pressboard is presented. The model was verified by comparing the simulation results with electric field and current measurements. At the outset, the ideal case, where a homogeneous initial charge carrier distribution according to the definition of ohmic conductivity is present, is analysed to establish the preliminary foundations pertaining to a typical measurement. Following that, the influence of distinct charge carriers on the measured quantities are investigated by altering their parametrisations. In contrast to the ideal case, a real measurement reveals a current trend, that can be explained by an excess amount of initial charge carriers related to the oil-impregnated pressboard layers. Potential possibilities to the origin of the surplus are discussed. Furthermore, it is shown that the dissociable and intrinsic charge carriers alone can reconstruct the measured quantities in terms of the transient behaviour. This points out that, for the field strength studied here (E ≤ 1 kV/mm), the charging of the highly resistive pressboard barriers is dominated by the dissociation of charge carriers in the oil gaps.

articleTitle: Self-healing monitoring method of metallized film capacitor based on time-frequency domain characteristics of UHF signals
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Self-healing (SH) is a unique feature of metallized film capacitors (MFCs), improving the reliability of MFCs by clearing internal defects. On the other hand, SH is also an aging factor of MFC due to the demetallization, leading to the reduction of capacitor plate and resulting in the MFC capacitance loss. The state of MFC should be monitored and efficiently diagnosed when operating in power system. Usually, the MFC monitoring methods base on the calculation of equivalent parameters, especially the MFC capacitance. In this study, a new method for monitoring MFC aging was proposed by directly detecting SH of MFC based on ultra high frequency (UHF) signals. The time-frequency domain characteristics of UHF signals were analysed by using wavelet packet transform (WPT), and then the UHF characteristic frequency was extracted. The UHF characteristic frequency energy has a positive proportional relationship to SH area, enabling this UHF-based monitoring method to detect SH and capacitor loss of MFC visually. Moreover, this method can be conveniently applied to real operating systems by using non-contact UHF sensors without changing the system circuit. This study enriches the SH characteristic information extraction and the MFC state diagnosis in power systems.

articleTitle: Detection of electrical equipment using an artificial neural network with visual spectrum images and thermal images
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Automated monitoring of assets in the energy industry, notably high voltage equipment, can greatly benefit from the detection of these equipment through intelligent algorithms. Currently, several topologies and architectures of artificial neural networks are used in the recognition of objects in images. To train these networks, a very large number of images is required, which is not always available. Computer vision and digital image processing techniques are then applied to expand the existing database. This article explores the combination of images at different wavelengths to improve the performance of the YOLOv5 network in recognizing high voltage electrical equipment in a 500 kV substation. With this objective, two image databases, composed by images in the visible spectrum and infrared images were combined in different proportions and used to train the network. The results showed that expanding the training base with images of different wavelengths can improve the network performance.

articleTitle: Dynamic behaviours of bubbles in transformer oil and their PRPD patterns in oil/pressboard insulation system
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: When partial discharge (PD) is detected in transformers, identification of the source of PD and its risk assessment is necessary to ensure sufficient insulation performance for the safe operation of the apparatus. This study focuses on PD caused within residual bubbles in the oil gap of an oil/pressboard insulation system. In this study, an air bubble is injected into vacuum-degassed oil, and an AC voltage is applied to the oil gap with the procedure according to IEC 60076-3 to investigate the PD characteristics and the bubble behaviours. In the case of a small bubble, the bubble is stretched in the direction of the electric field at first, then it is fragmented by the shock of PD. In the case of a large bubble, the bubble and the insulating oil are agitated by PD with the large PD magnitude and high repetition rate, which we call "the turbulence state". In both cases, the volume of the bubbles gradually decreases with time when we use vacuum-degassed oil. The relationships between the dynamic behaviours of bubbles and phase resolved partial discharge patterns can be used to determine the risk of insulation damage in transformers.

articleTitle: Fault current limiter parameter selection on DC distribution system side in MVDC system
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The MVDC system has many advantages as it can link the renewable distributed power system with the existing AC distribution network, but research on the protection scheme is required because the standard for the DC distribution system has not been established. In general, the energy of a DC power system increases rapidly when a fault occurs. Therefore, it is possible to reduce the stress on the circuit breaker that occurs during interrupting by applying the fault current limiter. However, research on fault current limiter for DC distributed system application have not been conducted, and fault current limiter design considering transient characteristics in MVDC system is required. In this paper, MVDC system was connecting by linking 22.9kV AC power system with ±35kV DC Link. Line-to-line short circuit fault is simulated in ±35kV DC link, fault current is reduced using resistive superconducting fault current limiter(R-SFCL), and fault current is interrupted through Hybrid Circuit Breaker. Accordingly, a short circuit fault was simulated in the ±35kV dc Link, and a protective scheme was proposed that utilizes a fault current limiter to limit the fault current.

articleTitle: New magnetic sensor for partial discharges measurement applied to HVDC constraints inside GIS
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Partial discharges (PD) measurement is the most common way to detect and identify defects for Medium/High Voltage equipment. Inside a Gas Insulated Substation, conventional method and ultra-high frequency (UHF) are usually used to measure PD inside the equipment. Recently, a new PD measurement sensor namely magnetic sensor is proposed, based on current induction. It might be the compromise between conventional and UHF measurement. The aims of this work were to study its behaviour and to compare its performances with other measuring methods. Two different defects (protrusion and floating-moving particle) were placed inside a real size GIS under HVDC constraints. Magnetic sensors were placed successively at several locations. UHF and conventional measurements were used as references. The impact of perturbations, external corona and earthing disturbance currents, on the performance of the different sensors was studied. The sensitivity of the magnetic measurement system is quite high at least 5 pC, with a smaller dependence on location than UHF sensor (distance, angle, presence of spacer …). Magnetic sensor measurement is slightly more sensitive to external corona and earthing current. The patterns given by magnetic sensor are quite similar with the ones given by the other measurements methods.

articleTitle: Thermal-oxidative ageing effect on electrical performance of polypropylene/elastomer blends
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: Polypropylene (PP) is a promising candidate for high voltage direct current (HVDC) cables because of its overall low cost and recyclable nature, but currently limited in real use due to its high stiffness. A propylene-based elastomer (PBE), DOW VERSIFY<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> 2200 was introduced to compensate for this limitation. Meanwhile, the influence of this elastomer component to the lifetime was investigated by thermal-oxidative ageing at a high temperature of 150 °C. The chemical changes were characterised by Fourier-Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy to investigate the extent of ageing. Space charge accumulation behaviour was estimated by the pulsed electro-acoustic (PEA) method and the influence of the elastomer fraction on charge accumulation and decay of PP/elastomer blends was investigated. There is very clear charge injection in PP/elastomer blends, compared to pure PP, which further increases with increased ageing time in the bulk of samples. The DC breakdown strength (BDS) shows an increase with the addition of the elastomer component and keeps increasing for samples at an early stage of the ageing process, before declining as a function of ageing time.

articleTitle: Impact of dry ice and water on safe electrical distances and impulse withstand voltage
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: In order to minimise the time for tower surface preparation, and to improve health and safety conditions for the workers and the environment, National Grid Electricity Transmission have started an innovation project where high pressure water and dry ice jet sprays are being explored as potential alternatives to abrasive or chemical cleaning. The use of such technologies can also reduce the time required to re-paint individual towers. However, it needs to be assessed if the use of water and dry ice sprays could potentially increase the risk of flashovers. The current paper will look to determine the impact of using dry ice and water sprays for tower surface preparation ahead of re-painting activity. The paper will look to determine the safe electrical distances and voltages, based on laboratory tests of a typical rod-plane gap with the introduction of water and dry ice sprays between these gaps.

articleTitle: Partial breakdown detection in vacuum interrupter under lightning impulse voltage
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The transition to climate-friendly and SF6-free switching and insulation media in high and medium voltage is currently an important topic. Vacuum switching technology is one of the possibilities being explored. Due to the degressive characteristic of the insulation capacity of vacuum over the distance, the electrical strength is an important field of research. In this paper, the electrical strength of vacuum switching devices with lightning impulse voltage as transient voltage stress is investigated. Because vacuum interrupters are complex structures with multiple shields, there is a possibility of partial breakdown in the arrangement. A partial breakdown detection system has been set up for the investigation of partial breakdowns. For this purpose, the capacitance of the vacuum interrupter is supplemented with a low-voltage capacitance to form a voltage divider. The appearance of partial breakdowns can thus be detected. The detection method is described in detail and demonstrated by measurements. The device under test used, has a two-stage flashover path including the undefined metal vapor shield. The results show that the breakdown is usually preceded by a partial breakdown. The investigation of partial breakdowns in high-voltage applications e.g. vacuum switches contributes to a better understanding of electrical strength.

articleTitle: Harmonics in MVDC cable systems – study on thermal and electric stress
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: MVDC can assist in resolving issues with the transition to renewable energy by expanding transmission capacity. Due to the use of converters, MVDC systems may be affected by harmonic currents and voltages. However, harmonics are not currently considered harmful in MVDC systems. Nevertheless, harmonics may have an impact on the electric field distribution and temperature in cable systems. Therefore, multiphysics FEM simulations are carried out to examine the general impact of harmonics in MVDC cables. The MVDC cable system experiences an electric field enhancement because of the influence of harmonics. The field enhancement shows the highest impact closest to the conductor. Furthermore, the average relative field enhancement is equal to the relative amplitudes of the harmonics. To investigate the field enhancement for different insulation material properties, different types of XLPE material (AC and DC) are investigated. Findings show that the influence of harmonic voltages rises with the non-linear conductivity of the insulation material. To examine the impact of harmonic currents on the ampacity of MVDC cable systems, FEM simulations are presented. The dielectric losses of MVDC cables compared to conductor losses are smaller than 0.01% and therefore negligible. Harmonic currents cause a very slight reduction in ampacity.

articleTitle: Surface insulation performance of atmospheric and fluorinated insulating gases at highly divergent electric field conditions
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper examines the surface insulation performance of atmospheric gases, namely, technical air (21/79% O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>), nitrogen (N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>), carbon dioxide (CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) and the gas mixture of 4% fluoronitrile (C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N) balanced with CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. The test configuration replicates the contact region between charged metal conductor and solid dielectric both surrounded by the gaseous insulation medium. Three polymers, namely, polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), polyether-ether-ketone (PEEK) and polyvinylidene-fluoride (PVDF), of different relative permittivities are tested. The test object is subjected to alternating (AC) voltage waveform at power frequency (50Hz) and the partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) and flashover voltage (FOV) levels are identified. The obtained results showed that both PDIV and FOV decrease with the increase of the relative permittivity of the solid dielectric with slight variation in the sequence of the atmospheric gases with regards to their performance. The binary mixture of 4/96% C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>N/CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> was found to be better than technical air and N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. However, it was found to be comparable to that of CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, in some cases as discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Implementation of RTV coating on 500KV transmission line insulator S2P-Adipala to prevent pollution-related disturbance
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: To maintain the performance of the insulation components on the 500 kV transmission line against significant exposure to pollutants, PT PLN (Persero) UIT JBT has conducted a pilot project to implement RTV-Coating on the 500 kV S2P-ADPLA. The purpose of implementing RTV-coating is to provide an alternative to polymer insulators so that the risk of mechanical failure in polymer insulators can be mitigated and, at the same time, good pollutant resistance performance is obtained. The performance of the insulator coated with RTV is assessed based on routine visual inspections, thermal testing, and corona intensity testing under operating conditions. Then, to support the condition assessment, a comparison analysis was also carried out with glass and ceramic insulators that were not coated with an RTV coating, and comparisons were made with polymer insulators installed on the same conductor.

articleTitle: Evaluating OLTC condition based on feature extraction from vibro-acoustic signals
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: The On Load Tap Changer (OLTC) faults account for about 30% of the power transformer failures. Transformers are one of the most critical assets in the electric power network. Therefore, monitoring this component continuously and detecting any incipient faults is essential to prevent power transformer outages. In this paper, vibro-acoustic signal analysis has been adopted to evaluate the OLTC condition. Vibration signals obtained from the in-service on OLTCs are analysed using statistical parameters in two steps. The first step evaluates the signal envelope to identify changes over the operating period. In this regard, each vibration signal envelope is compared with a reference envelope, and the degree of similarity is estimated by Pearson’s correlation coefficient, mean similarity, and peak similarity. The similarity values are later used to identify changes over the time elapsed to derive general information about the envelopes. In the second step, vibration signal envelopes are subdivided into six parts based on the peak positions. Subsequently, the statistical parameters are computed for each part, and the best fit ones are identified based on regression coefficients. The proposed approach can be seen as a useful tool allowing extracting features with potential to detect OLTC faults.

articleTitle: A study of the effect of temperature on cavity partial discharges in polyethylene insulation
publicationTitle: 23rd International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH 2023)
abstract: This paper examines cavity partial discharge (PD) mechanisms in polyethylene insulation material as a function of temperature. Experimental PD measurements were carried out in accordance with the IEC 60270 standard. A test voltage of 11 kV ac and frequency of 50 Hz was used. The test temperatures studied were 15°C, 40°C, 50°C, 60°C, 70°C, 80°C and 90°C. Test specimens with a cavity diameter of 2.5 mm were assembled using three 1.5 mm thick polyethylene sheets sandwiched between two flat brass electrodes. Partial discharge parameters such as the charge magnitude, inception voltage and PD phase resolved pattern (PDPRP) were measured and analysed at varying temperatures. Results showed that Partial Discharge Inception Voltage (PDIV) increased linearly with temperature for the entire test range. PD charge magnitude initially decreased with temperature from 15°C to 60°C and then increased from 60°C to 90°C. The evolution of PDPRP with temperature was characterised by a turtle-like pattern at ambient temperature, which transitioned into a rabbit ear PDPRP as the temperature increased to 90°C. The findings are interpreted using the mean free path effect on ionisation probability as well as the residual charge dynamics in the cavity as a function of temperature.

articleTitle: Pultrusion made materials for outdoor insulation and their HV tests
